{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Time: ordered timer inputs / 2

Status: integration preview. This publication defines data and the required runtime
behavior. A package import does not install a scheduler or authorize an executable
binding. Native support is an explicit host selection. The MyOS Java adapter implements
this publication; other runtimes must qualify their own integration.

## 1. Layering and inputs

Language stores and validates Blue values. Contracts runs lifecycle handlers,
operations and workflows. BEX computes effects. This Time protocol introduces a
channel for processor-derived inputs and steps for emitting requests. Coordination
must integrate pending timers into its existing input selection, complete-prefix
publication, durable progress and account-scoped execution. No separate graph
scheduler, global ancestor barrier, per-timer Timeline, or external business entry
is introduced.

Starting management runs Contracts initialization without an incoming Timeline
entry and without an initialization timestamp. A lifecycle workflow may emit a
complete Timer Request already stored in the document. BEX does not read a clock.
An operation may also emit a request; its arrival timestamp is not used to derive
the requested deadline. A Timer Request merely stored somewhere in document data
is not active until emitted by a successful managed-document invocation.

## 2. Timestamp

The field is `timestamp`: a nonnegative Integer Unix timestamp in microseconds
since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, using the same unit as the selected Coordination
Timeline timestamps. For example, `1790931600000000` is a requested deadline, not
a measured execution time. Text dates, seconds, floating point values and booleans
are not interchangeable with this field. There is no `at`, `atUs`, `afterUs`,
implicit `now`, relative-delay base, or worker-clock field in this protocol.

The selected Contracts edition accepts external processing timestamps from 0 to
2^53 - 1 inclusive. This preview uses that existing numeric representation bound;
it does not introduce a structural, cardinality or depth limit. A different
numeric domain requires a compatible Contracts/Coordination edition and a new
Time publication, rather than silently truncating an Integer.

The processor may wake late. Once eligible, a Timer Fired input occupies the
requested deadline's logical position. Its Contracts eventTimestamp is the
request's timestamp, NOT a wall-clock observation and NOT an originating
initialization/operation timestamp. This supplies the existing three-input
Contracts interface only when the future firing is processed. Initialization
still supplies no external event or timestamp.

## 3. Messages

A Timer Request has exactly type, channel, timestamp and optionally key and
context. channel is the local Time channel key, not a Timeline ID. A supplied key
is nonempty Text. context is arbitrary valid captured Blue data, not code to
reevaluate later. Reserved metadata is interpreted under Language rules; unknown
ordinary top-level request fields are rejected by the Time runtime.

A Timer Fired has exactly type, registrationId and request. Its request is the
original committed Timer Request, preserved as an exact Blue value. An inline
presentation and a verified exact reference may differ physically without
changing that identity. No callback/workflow name is stored, and no execution
clock or inferred relative deadline is added.

A Cancel Timer Request has exactly type, channel and key. This version cancels
by key only. Cancellation by registration ID, recurrence, cron and relative
delays are outside this version. Applications may emit subsequent explicit
requests to implement their own bounded repetition.

## 4. Event effects and custom steps

Contracts/Trigger Event and BEX $appendEvent can emit a fully constructed Timer
Request. Both use normal Contracts commit/rollback behavior. A native Time/Schedule
Timer step accepts a single `request` body field, interpreted as a read-only BEX
expression. The expression returns an untyped object containing channel,
timestamp, optional key and context. The step attaches the exact Timer Request
type, validates the completed message, and returns one staged emitted event.
A result with its own type or unsupported fields is rejected, not overwritten.

Time/Cancel Timer follows the same procedure, with channel and key. Evaluating
arguments may read the current event, call, document and earlier step results
using the current Contracts expression frame. It may not read a wall clock,
perform host I/O, register a timer immediately, or reinterpret its context as
future executable code. Standard BEX gas must be charged before work, against
the same invocation budget; the step does not receive a second 10,000,000 budget.
Any effects in an expression-root evaluation are rejected.

A helper emitting the same completed request through ordinary Compute must have
the same registration meaning. Emitting a request is NOT a firing. A Triggered
Event Channel observing that request does not constitute a Time channel firing.
A conditional BEX program can choose whether to append a request. A preceding
step returning false is not implicitly a workflow branch.

## 5. Registration, scope and identities

Only effects surviving the originating document's commit create or cancel
registrations. The Time runtime must validate the entire staged effect batch
before making it eligible to commit. Malformed requests or an invalid local
channel reject the originating attempt atomically; earlier changes and requests
from that attempt do not become effective. The emitter is the managed document
that actually produced the effect, not each ancestor that later observes it.
Use Contracts provenance/effect occurrences, not a scan of public payloads.

A registration belongs to an engine/account context, managed-document identity,
Time channel key, and that channel's generation. It is not keyed by the changing
current document BlueId alone. An unrelated business update does not rearm or
invalidate it. Replacing/removing the channel or ending the managed lifetime
invalidates that generation's pending registrations. Ordinary embedding attach
or detach is not by itself removal of the separately managed child.

The canonical identity descriptor is the Blue value:

    { domain: "Time/registration/1", contextId: <stable context identity>,
      documentId: <stable managed identity>, channel: <key>,
      channelGeneration: <generation>, occurrenceId: <committed effect identity> }

registrationId is its Language BlueId. occurrenceId identifies the source commit
and local effect position using existing committed-effect provenance. It is not
just the emitted payload's content BlueId. Two identical emitted requests at
different occurrences create different unnamed timers; replaying the same
occurrence yields the same registration. Independent contexts need not share a
registration ID. They reproduce it when replaying the same identified context.

A key selects at most one pending registration within this scope. Reusing the key
replaces that pending registration with a new identity. Without a key each
occurrence is independent. Cancellation of a missing key is an idempotent no-op.
Replacement and cancellation only affect a registration they precede in logical
input order; they cannot undo an already prior firing. One source commit's
requests and cancellations apply in their emitted order. Thus schedule-then-
cancel leaves no pending timer; cancel-then-schedule leaves the new one pending.

## 6. Eligibility, completeness and deterministic order

A host alarm is only a wake-up hint. Firing requires evidence that authoritative
time has reached the requested timestamp, relevant histories are closed through
the required boundary, all predecessors/prerequisites have been processed, and
the registration is still pending. A fetched latest head or silence on an idle
Timeline is insufficient. Strictly increasing append timestamps alone do not
prove that an earlier unobserved entry cannot arrive. A completeness promise
must establish both availability of the required prefix and that future accepted
entries cannot be inserted into that closed prefix.

The required source set is the document's current dependency/history selection,
not a list frozen when the timer was first emitted and not every Timeline on the
platform. Missing authorized history means WAITING, not permission to ignore a
possible earlier cancellation. Reevaluate dependencies after earlier inputs or
topology changes. Preserve exact historical child outcomes and the existing
cyclic dependency/group rules; a new Time feature must not reintroduce a global
parent-completion barrier or deadlock a cycle by demanding impossible mutually
final completeness.

Pending timers occupy candidate positions as soon as their source commit is
visible. Every input uses Coordination's lexicographic order
(timestamp, sourceBlueId, entryBlueId). An ordinary entry uses its Timeline ID;
a timer uses its Timer Source ID and Timer Entry ID. There is no input-class
priority. At equal timestamps a cancellation wins only when its entry precedes
the timer. Dependency prerequisites still take precedence; this is not a new
global order across unrelated documents.

Each managed document has one immutable Timer Source with exactly type,
contextId and documentId (the stable managed identity, not its current state ID).
A Timer Entry has exactly type, source (an exact Timer Source reference),
timestamp (the requested deadline), and message (an exact Timer Fired reference).
Its message contains the registration identity and original request. Neither
object contains arrival time, worker identity, mutable status or a predecessor.
Multiple timers may have the same source and timestamp. Pending entries are
candidates, not append operations on a strictly increasing Signed Timeline.

The Time adapter admits this exact Timer Entry type wherever the selected
Coordination receipt/history/attachment format records the effective input.
It preserves the existing order tuple and receipt construction. This extension
is enabled only for the exact approved Time publication; arbitrary entry types
remain invalid. The outer Timer Entry is the durable input identity, whereas
Contracts receives its Timer Fired message and deadline. Retained completion
records preserve both identities so receivers verify the original invocation.
Ordinary Signed Timeline validation and its strict timestamp rule are unchanged.

A newly emitted request must have a timestamp strictly greater than the
invocation's logical timestamp, regardless of whether its cause is an operation,
a timer or a received child outcome. New child initialization inherits the
causal floor of the attaching invocation. Requests at or before that floor are
rejected as TIME_DEADLINE_BEFORE_POSITION before publication. No fixed minimum
interval is imposed beyond strict increase. Hosts may fairly throttle processing
without changing logical timestamps or skipping backlog positions. Pending
registration quotas are host resource limits, not automatic recurrence rules.

A genuinely new standalone document with no committed external position may
initialize with an already elapsed absolute deadline. Process it as due once
time and input completeness are established. A previously committed overdue
registration after downtime also retains its original candidate position; it
is not a new backdated registration.

## 7. Admission and authority

Time/Timer Channel derives from Contracts/Channel, NOT from a generic accepting
External Channel. Bind its exact type and rules identity to a trusted
external-channel implementation. This is an external input to the Contracts
machine, but it is generated by the document processor, not appended by a user
to a Timeline. Unsupported Time channels and steps must fail explicitly.
Loading the package data must never enable them automatically.

Before preparation, the runtime binds admission evidence to the exact receiver
snapshot, managed identity, channel and generation, event identity, registration,
requested timestamp, prerequisite coverage, and engine context. Recheck it on
replay. A Timer Fired-shaped payload on a Timeline, a forged client evidence
object, wrong generation, replaced key, duplicate completed registration, or
mismatched request cannot create a timer firing. Ordinary Timeline inputs can
still be observed by ordinary Timeline workflows, but never impersonate Time
channel admission. Timer firing conveys only the agreed document transition;
it cannot impersonate a party or bypass another document's operation authority.

## 8. Durable progress, parents and failure

The authoritative state is committed effects plus durable per-registration
progress. Pending wake-up indexes are reconstructible projections. Persist the
source cursor, registration identity, generation, key replacement/cancellation,
selected input and terminal disposition with idempotent writes and the engine's
existing publication/receipt protocol. Do not require cross-table PostgreSQL
transactions or treat multiple uncoordinated writes as atomic.

A crash before the source commit exposes no timer. A crash after commit but before
index update must rediscover it. Commit results and firing disposition through
the existing durable publication protocol so a crash cannot create a second
committed firing or lose the first. An old alarm after cancel/replace is harmless.
Do not mark a timer done before its outcome is durable. This publication does
not prescribe a new journal implementation in the data package.

An unresolved timer at T holds the receiver's complete-prefix publication before
its position. A parent must not be told its child is complete through T while the
child still owes a timer-driven transition there. This is a per-dependency
completeness requirement, not a rule that the child waits for all parents before
continuing. Shared parents consume the retained completed child history without
rerunning that child once per embedding.

One-shot timers become terminal after their committed processing disposition.
A successful firing with no matching workflow is terminal NO_MATCH. A deterministic
Contracts failure or gas exhaustion follows the selected Coordination terminal
input policy, with rollback and recorded disposition; it must not permanently
block later input or retry forever as though it were a missing wake-up. Host
crash, resource shortage, unavailable proofs or unfunded account are not such
terminal semantic results. Preserve account-scoped authority/access and budgets.

## 9. Metering and qualification

The Contracts 10,000,000 shared gas ceiling is unchanged. BEX evaluation, message
construction, validation and accepted effect processing must be charged through
the chosen runtime before proportional work. Candidate discovery/proof retrieval
is host work subject to host and account budgets, not an invented unbounded
free background workload. No new universal timer-count, graph-depth or collection
cardinality ceiling is introduced. Exact native tariffs, metering of admission
validation, cyclic progress, durable storage and cross-language parity must be
qualified before native support is advertised. The conformance harness's fixture
counters are not a calibrated production gas policy.

This edition selects the exact 10M gas prerequisites. Previously published content retains its original semantics.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts

Blue Contracts processes an event against exact managed Blue documents and returns
the resulting state, ordered emitted occurrences, deterministic gas and replay
evidence. It uses Language for content semantics and BEX for evaluation.

## Final gas edition

`1.0.0-final-gas.1` retains the existing tariffs and the 10,000,000-gas shared
maximum. Each charge is checked before work happens. Canonical outcomes contain
the final admitted gas total and, on exhaustion, one rejected-charge diagnostic.
They do not contain per-charge histories. Turn and unit proofs carry scalar gas
contributions, and continuation commitments carry totals and configured local
counters. Removing the history does not remove budget enforcement or replay
verification.

`SPECIFICATION.md` and `spec/contracts-final-gas.md` are the same normative text,
including eighteen executable Python modules. Source overrides and their hashes
are listed in `docs/sources.json`; the earlier reference remains frozen.
The 32 native type definitions are generated by the specification's catalogue
recipe. `types/` contains authoring inputs and `docs/types/` their exact views.

The specification, types, packages and receipts have new exact identities. A host
must explicitly install this edition. Keep the original runtime when replaying
old snapshots or histories; see [migration](MIGRATION.md).

## Local verification

With Python 3.13+, pytest, PyYAML, Java 21 and `BLUE_JAVA_CLASSPATH` pointing to
the qualified Java Language runtime and its dependencies:

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package demo
./blue-package test
python ../tools/build_final_gas.py blue-contracts --check
```

The rebuild check compares the full archive, unpacked distribution and dependency
lock without modifying the selected publication. Package verification alone does
not certify a host implementation. [Qualification](QUALIFICATION.md) distinguishes
the new edition from earlier reference reports.
"}

7m8k8P8b8Kn2jHF96EQogWTpsouytXmDFQ3qdmWd.text: {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue BEX 1.0 **Edition:** `blue-bex/2026-10-07-gas-10m-1` **Normative form:** one complete specification with executable algorithm appendices ## Abstract BEX is a deterministic expression and statement language encoded as Blue-compatible data. It evaluates against explicit inputs and produces a value, an ordered changeset, ordered events and a logical work ledger. BEX does not perform document mutation or select externally ordered inputs. ## Contents - [1. Scope and conformance](#scope) - [2. Exact dependencies and interpretation](#dependencies) - [3. Purpose and imported language](#section-3) - [4. Machine and invocation](#section-4) - [5. Value domains and absence](#section-5) - [6. Numeric and Text rules](#section-6) - [7. Source classification and static positions](#section-7) - [8. Evaluation order and laziness](#section-8) - [9. Reads and observations](#section-9) - [10. Pointers and ordered changesets](#section-10) - [11. Collections](#section-11) - [12. Variables, functions, and return](#section-12) - [13. Effects and host intrinsics](#section-13) - [14. Gas](#section-14) - [15. Blue output boundary](#section-15) - [16. Errors and determinism](#section-16) - [17. Executable inventory and conformance](#section-17) - [18. External capability boundary](#section-18) - [19. Composition with Language and Contracts](#section-19) - [20. Release and identity](#section-20) - [21. Immutable host values](#section-21) - [22. Shared host metering](#section-22) - [23. Resource-proportional work accounting](#section-23) - [24. Equality and conversion ordering](#section-24) - [25. Occurrence and effect traversal](#section-25) - [Appendix A. Complete operator reference](#operators) - [Appendix B. Complete executable algorithms](#algorithms) ## 1. Scope and conformance This specification defines the protocol identified by this edition. Its prose, tables and algorithm appendices form one normative contract. It is independent of source-repository branches, release tags, installation paths and prior discussions. Named external semantics are selected exactly in §2. Where an implementation uses another programming language, it MUST preserve the same specified observations; matching internal classes or diagnostic wording is not required unless explicitly identified as an observation. **MUST** and **REQUIRED** express requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** express prohibitions. **SHOULD** and **SHOULD NOT** express recommendations whose departures require understood consequences. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** express permissions. Examples marked informative do not add requirements. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a defect, not permission to choose an outcome. A finite conformance corpus is evidence, not a proof for every possible input. A package distributes this specification; it does not install a processor. The package's BlueId, this specification Text's BlueId and the OCI/archive digests identify different content. This document does not contain its own calculated identity or the generated identities of types that refer to it. ## 2. Exact dependencies and interpretation This edition selects Blue Language package `8XGYNufx24r7Dc5bGoeobcGNCn9roLzSfZCQyHBTaTx4`, whose complete specification Text is `H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQmWnc`. Node construction, exact references, specialization, output admission and BlueIds have the meaning defined by that Language release. BEX is independent of Contracts. A host may supply Language-backed matching, node identity, finite reads and explicit intrinsics. Contracts is one such host and binds the supplied BEX context and ledger according to its own specification. BEX MUST NOT substitute ambient state or an unversioned implementation for these declared interfaces. Package imports supply exact content. Authoring prefixes are local bindings and do not leak through transitive imports. An imported definition retains its exact references. Mounting another package cannot change the selected interpreter or replace an existing type reference. Within this edition's interpreted package graph, the selected Language release MUST agree throughout; cross-Language conversion and mixed-rule cyclic sets are not defined. One selected Language governs a complete cyclic identity set and its owning proof. ## 3. Purpose and imported language BEX evaluates data-encoded programs against explicit, read-only inputs and produces values, ordered changesets, and ordered events. It neither fetches arbitrary resources nor publishes a document. A Contracts processor decides whether proposed effects can be applied; Coordination determines which authenticated external input is eligible. The reader is assumed to know Blue Language 1.0. Node admission, effective types, specialization, exact versus Source representations, references, set finalization, and BlueId are imported, not redefined. A BEX value is not a Blue node. In particular, Python object identity, dictionary iteration order, and native truth testing do not define BEX semantics. The executable algorithm appendix contains the complete evaluator and host-value algorithms. Readable rules and executable algorithms together define this edition; disagreement is a defect, not permission to choose either result. ## 4. Machine and invocation An invocation has a compiled program; an explicit context; a gas ledger; lexical function frames; an ordered changeset; and an ordered event list. Context supplies the selected document snapshot, event, current contract, previous step results, named bindings, and executing scope. Optional adapters provide finite document reads, Blue specialization checks, and exact-type intrinsics. No process-global variable is a program binding. No Python expression is evaluated from program text. The interpreter recognizes data forms, not Python, JavaScript, or embedded shell commands. An installed intrinsic is trusted host code and is outside that sandbox boundary. A successful invocation returns `Result(value, changeset, events, gas_used, gas_trace)`. It does not apply its changes. Returned effects remain ordinary BEX values until the Contracts output boundary has validated and converted them. ## 5. Value domains and absence The domains are undefined, null, Text, Integer, Double, Boolean, Object, and List. `UNDEFINED` is a singleton distinct from Python `None`, which represents internal BEX null. Boolean is not Integer. Objects have Text keys. Integers use exact integer arithmetic; Doubles use finite decimal observations and cross the Blue Double boundary as finite binary64 values. Missing member lookup yields undefined. Undefined object members are omitted by Blue conversion. Undefined list elements, including sparse overlay holes, cannot cross that boundary. Null is not an empty object and is rejected at the Blue output boundary. An actual empty object remains an actual empty object. `$emptyObject` is the explicit empty-object constructor. `$exists` is false only for undefined. Null therefore exists. Truth is false for undefined, null, false, empty Text, empty Object, and empty List; other values are true, **including numeric zero**. `$empty` and `$isEmpty` test the inverse of this truth rule, not Python's truthiness. ## 6. Numeric and Text rules Integer conversion accepts integers, integral finite numbers, and canonical decimal integer text. Fractional values and noncanonical integer spellings fail. Numeric conversion rejects Boolean, collections, nonfinite numbers, and malformed numeric text. Arithmetic operators in this edition produce exact Integer results, and division requires an exact Integer quotient. Division by zero or a fractional quotient fails. Numeric equality compares numeric value across Integer and Double. Other equality is domain-sensitive and recursive. It must not be substituted for BlueId equality or Language specialization. Collections do not stringify implicitly. Null and undefined stringify to empty Text where coercion is allowed; names, paths, keys, and operation names require presence and cannot use that absence coercion. Text-key ordering is Unicode code-point ordering. Gas size estimation counts UTF-16 code units, not Python string length or UTF-8 bytes. These are different operations and must remain separate. Nonfinite Doubles and lone Unicode surrogates are invalid runtime values at the relevant boundary. There is no universal source-depth, call-frame, numeric-text, Integer-result-size or Blue-output Integer-length ceiling. Integer arithmetic, finite binary64 values, canonical text, static recursion rejection and output validity remain mandatory. A host that cannot compile or evaluate otherwise valid finite work reports operational incompleteness, not invalid syntax, a false arithmetic error or gas exhaustion. Gas is a logical work rule, not an operating-system resource sandbox. Large operand/allocation paths require correctly placed deterministic work charges and safe host isolation; a local machine failure cannot create a different semantic history. ## 7. Source classification and static positions A single-key object whose key starts with `$` is an executable form when encountered in expression or statement position. It must name an installed operator valid for that position. Other objects are recursively evaluated data constructors. `$literal` prevents evaluation of its payload as program data, but does not authorize executable material in static Blue definition positions. Type-related and schema positions are static. Constants and function-argument patterns are static. Compilation rejects unknown operators, invalid operand shapes, unknown variables/constants/functions, malformed static names, reserved user-container names, invalid call argument sets, and recursive function-call graphs. Both sides of a lazy runtime construct still undergo static validation. A function body selects `expr` ahead of `do`. An explicit named entry must exist and take no arguments. The implementation also validates the root body even when a named entry is selected. Definition constants/functions can be supplied as an already available object to the compiler; loading a referenced program definition is a host integration obligation. ## 8. Evaluation order and laziness Object constructors evaluate keys in deterministic order; lists evaluate left to right. Function arguments evaluate in key order. Lazy operators evaluate only the branch or subsequent operand needed to establish the result. This applies to Boolean connectives, coalescing/default selection, conditionals, and lookup defaults. A static error in an unused branch is still an error. A runtime error or gas charge in an unselected branch does not occur. Empty or missing values cannot be replaced by Python idioms such as `value or fallback` unless they implement the particular BEX operator's rule. ## 9. Reads and observations `$document`, `$event`, `$currentContract`, `$binding`, `$steps`, `$var`, and `$const` read only their designated source. A variable or constant name containing `/` remains a name; its optional pointer is a separate operand. A named step is addressed by the step's actual Language `name` label, not its list position when a name was supplied. A Compute invocation sees a stable selected-document snapshot. A later Compute step sees effects successfully applied by earlier steps. `$resultValue` overlays this invocation's accumulated changes on its snapshot; it does not publish them. Finite managed-document reads use the closure's selected dependency projection, never an independently advancing source's latest public head. The context's matcher implements `$is` using Blue semantic admission and specialization. The interpreter does not guess that a JSON shape is a valid Blue type. Missing patterns, unknown required definitions, and uninstalled matcher capabilities are not accepted as successful matches. ### Exact node identity `$nodeBlueId: EXPR` evaluates EXPR once and returns a Text containing the ordinary Language BlueId. Charge `nodeIdentityRequested = 5` after evaluating the operand and before calling the host's Language identity boundary. The boundary shares the invocation ledger and cannot use a separate unmetered hash implementation. An admitted exact host collection retains its selected exact identity, including owning-set member identity, without expanding its descendants. A newly computed value passes the existing strict Blue-output validation and Language Exact admission/identity construction. Newly built containers preserve exact nested operands and their identity evidence; storage presentation cannot change charges. Null or undefined roots, malformed references, invalid type slots and incomplete owning-set evidence fail; missing required content is not replaced by an invented identity. Scalars are ordinary BEX scalar values and receive their corresponding Language scalar identity; metadata erased by scalar observation is not reconstructed. Equality and type specialization remain different operations from exact identity comparison. The standard Contracts context installs this boundary. Standalone BEX hosts supply `Context.node_blue_id(value, gas)` backed by the same Language operations; without it the operator fails with a boundary error. It does not perform network lookup or register user code. `processingEvent` remains a Contracts binding read through `$binding`; no `$processingEvent` operator is introduced. ## 10. Pointers and ordered changesets BEX value pointers use JSON-pointer escaping. Both empty Text and `/` designate the value root in this profile. This differs from the Language query API's empty-key behavior; adapters must not delegate blindly. Relative document paths resolve against the executing scope; already absolute document paths remain absolute. A Contracts processor separately checks whether a proposed absolute path is writable by that scope. A changeset is an ordered list of add, replace, or remove proposals. Non-remove proposals require a value. Remove ignores no hidden expression: its value operand is not evaluated by the append operation. Appending preserves duplicate operations and their order. BEX's observation overlay is **not** Contracts mutation. Overlay removal from a List creates a sparse undefined position and does not shift later elements. Actual Contracts array removal does shift later elements. Intermediate overlay objects are constructed deterministically. A sparse result may be observed internally but cannot be serialized as a Blue List containing undefined. ## 11. Collections Collection operations support Lists in index order and Objects in sorted key order. Query bindings are lexical for that query and are restored afterward. Statement `forEach` uses its declared iteration slots and executes its body for each selected item. An empty collection executes no iteration body. Map and flat-map produce Lists; flat-map requires a List result per item. Filter preserves the input's collection category. Reduce threads its accumulator. Some, find, and find-entry stop after the first decisive match. Find-entry preserves the selected value and occurrence information rather than replacing occurrence identity with value identity. Iteration gas is charged for each admitted visited item. Short-circuiting stops both later evaluation and later iteration charges. Collection construction retains its specified logical charges. Host memory/cancellation controls are operational and may interrupt without establishing a semantic rejection; they are not universal collection-size restrictions. ## 12. Variables, functions, and return `let` declares function-frame slots. Parallel declarations evaluate their initializers against the old frame; an explicit declaration order enables ordered dependency between initializers. `set` updates an existing declared slot. Conditional declaration visibility is checked statically. Function calls use isolated frames, exact declared argument-name sets, and supplied Blue argument-pattern checks. Functions share the invocation's effect accumulators and gas ledger but do not implicitly capture another function's locals. Recursion is rejected during compilation. Business-process cycles therefore arise from Contracts event work, not recursive BEX function calls. Explicit return exits the current function/body. Without an explicit result, the interpreter returns the accumulated changeset and events. A called function's return does not terminate its caller. Failure exits the invocation and does not authorize partial publication. ## 13. Effects and host intrinsics Event append preserves multiplicity. Two equal event values are two emission occurrences; their BlueIds may be equal. Occurrence identity belongs to the hosting Contracts closure. The BEX interpreter does not deduplicate by content identity. An intrinsic must have an exact static type ID present in the invocation's installed capability registry. Unknown IDs fail compilation. Runtime removal of a capability fails execution. Intrinsics receive copied explicit operands and the same gas meter; they must return explicit BEX values and account for bounded work. Files, network, clock, and randomness are not implicit capabilities. ## 14. Gas Compilation consumes no semantic gas. Each admitted expression, statement, read, call, pointer operation, collection item, append, and size-dependent operation is charged by the algorithm at its specified point. A failed charge is recorded as rejected work and does not increment admitted `used` gas. The default scalar tariffs are: expression 1; statement 1; document read 2; event/current-contract/steps/variable read 1; result-value read 2; pointer get base 1; pointer set base 3; object set base 2; append-change/event base 5; iteration item 1; function call 2. Size/path contributions are defined by the algorithms, not by wall-clock time. A Compute step can impose a positive local cap while charging each admitted operation to a shared Contracts closure meter. A local-cap rejection is distinguished from shared-cap rejection in the trace. A cap is checked before work is admitted. Gas allowance, used gas, attempted rejected charge, and operational cancellation are different values. The trace and tariff in the executable annex define this edition. A conforming implementation preserves the admitted charges and first rejected charge for identical inputs. Equivalence to a different BEX release or another tariff is a separate interoperability claim, not an additional unstated rule. ## 15. Blue output boundary `blue_value` converts runtime values into a JSON-compatible, null-free proposal. It is not semantic admission and does not return a BlueId. Authoring aliases are resolved in an explicit authoring/preparation stage before this proposal enters the runtime output boundary. Runtime type slots MUST contain exact Blue references. The host admits the proposal through Language Exact admission and uses the resulting validated exact value; it MUST NOT resolve aliases, replay Source list construction, or reinterpret a generated string as an installed type at this stage. A BEX program may compute arbitrary Text, but a Text in a runtime type slot is not thereby a type reference. A host accepting raw data-encoded programs with unresolved literal type aliases must reject the resulting effect, not silently reinterpret it. The corrected boundary does not collapse null to `{}`. A whole null event or null patch value fails. Undefined object members may disappear, but required fields must still satisfy the host effect schema. Effect structural validation precedes mutation, so a later malformed effect cannot cause an earlier effect to be published. ## 16. Errors and determinism Compilation error, runtime error, invalid Blue output, actual gas exhaustion and host/incomplete execution are distinct failure families. The former portable resource caps are removed. Resource exceptions must propagate as incomplete host work, not be wrapped into ordinary BEX runtime failure and terminally rejected by a feeder. A caller may not turn an unavailable required Language definition or provider proof into a successful computation. A runtime exception never means "no changes" success. Determinism requires identical admitted inputs, program and definitions, installed capabilities, matcher behavior, selected document projection, and gas schedule. Python hash seed, input-map insertion order, cached parsing, and unrelated documents must not affect the semantic result. Stateful or nondeterministic intrinsics violate this requirement unless their observations are explicit frozen inputs. ## 17. Executable inventory and conformance the operator appendix lists every installed expression and statement operator. The complete annex supplies their compilation, evaluation, value and gas definitions. Each marked module is extracted without modification. The source table in this specification identifies the exact modules and their dependencies. Conformance preserves successful results, ordered proposals, short-circuit behavior, static errors, runtime errors, output-boundary errors and gas observations. Required cases include Boolean/Integer distinction; undefined/null/empty-object distinctions; exact arithmetic; type-pattern matching; every operator family; function scope; side-effect order; Unicode ordering and size; output rejection; and local/shared gas limits. Passing a finite corpus is evidence, not a proof for all programs or capabilities. ## 18. External capability boundary The standard algorithms require no arbitrary external I/O. A host supplies explicit document projections, a Language-backed matcher, and any selected intrinsic registry. A missing required capability or exact definition cannot be converted to successful evaluation. Intrinsics are trusted, explicitly installed code with their own semantics and bounded work; an unknown intrinsic ID is rejected. This edition defines no production network acquisition service, operating-system sandbox, universal intrinsic package or Java diagnostic mapping. An independent implementation conforms to this edition by preserving its specified results, not by reproducing an undocumented behavior of another runtime. Host memory protection and process isolation remain operational obligations; they cannot change the semantic outcome of an admitted computation. ## 19. Composition with Language and Contracts User-binding declarations are constants, functions, function arguments, local `$let` slots (both forms), and collection/loop item, key, index and accumulator slots. All reject the reserved names listed by `compiler.RESERVED`, including `$previousItems`. Ordinary literal object keys and host-provided read bindings are not user-binding declarations. `$previousItems` is a reserved Language name in BEX user-binding containers. It is not a BEX instruction and cannot manufacture Language list inheritance at runtime. `$previous` and other Source-only controls likewise do not replace Exact admission of effects. An unevaluated object containing dynamic expression fields is not an instance of its eventual result type. A repository can author that value through ordinary BEX `$objectFromEntries` construction with exact type references. Resulting events and patch values are admitted only after evaluation. Rewriting a program changes its identity and may change its gas; this does not weaken Language validation. The Contracts invocation supplies the selected executing document as the BEX document. BEX receives no ambient enclosing process or independently advancing public head. Contracts owns mutation boundaries, internal event occurrence identities, initialization, termination, checkpoint settlement, graph finalization and publication. BEX returns proposed effects and never advances those states itself. The standard Contracts binding uses its contextual business-value document projection for both `canonical` and `resolved` BEX read modes. This is an explicit Contracts binding, not a redefinition of the Language serialization APIs. Configured program data is distinct from effective business values: inherited specification prose must not be inserted into a literal program or effect. ## 20. Release and identity The complete specification comprises its readable rules, operator reference, executable algorithms and explicit dependency selection. Its BlueId names that exact Text. The publication manifest records its identity outside the Text, avoiding a self-reference. A normative change creates a new exact specification identity. Test reports, implementation-only packaging, tutorials and provenance notes do not silently amend this edition. ## 21. Immutable host values The numeric, equality, binding and control semantics are those defined in this specification. A trusted host may supply immutable collections implementing the host-value interface in values.py. Collection kind, keys, reads, variables, function arguments and persistent overlays operate on these values without eager recursive cloning. Output conversion uses the host's finite exact representation. 8ncKHLULWkzyNKEHfzpswF6iKZfc3H1DzDpgH8UC.text: {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue BEX 1.0 **Edition:** `blue-bex/2026-10-12-final-gas-1` **Normative form:** one complete specification with executable algorithm appendices ## Abstract BEX is a deterministic expression and statement language encoded as Blue-compatible data. It evaluates against explicit inputs and produces a value, an ordered changeset, ordered events and a deterministic admitted gas total. BEX does not perform document mutation or select externally ordered inputs. ## Contents - [1. Scope and conformance](#scope) - [2. Exact dependencies and interpretation](#dependencies) - [3. Purpose and imported language](#section-3) - [4. Machine and invocation](#section-4) - [5. Value domains and absence](#section-5) - [6. Numeric and Text rules](#section-6) - [7. Source classification and static positions](#section-7) - [8. Evaluation order and laziness](#section-8) - [9. Reads and observations](#section-9) - [10. Occurrence and effect traversal](#section-25) - [Appendix A. Complete operator reference](#operators) - [Appendix B. Complete executable algorithms](#algorithms) ## 1. Scope and conformance This specification defines the protocol identified by this edition. Its prose, tables and algorithm appendices form one normative contract. It is independent of source-repository branches, release tags, installation paths and prior discussions. Named external semantics are selected exactly in §2. Where an implementation uses another programming language, it MUST preserve the same specified observations; matching internal classes or diagnostic wording is not required unless explicitly identified as an observation. **MUST** and **REQUIRED** express requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** express prohibitions. **SHOULD** and **SHOULD NOT** express recommendations whose departures require understood consequences. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** express permissions. Examples marked informative do not add requirements. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a defect, not permission to choose an outcome. A finite conformance corpus is evidence, not a proof for every possible input. A package distributes this specification; it does not install a processor. The package's BlueId, this specification Text's BlueId and the OCI/archive digests identify different content. This document does not contain its own calculated identity or the generated identities of types that refer to it. ## 2. Exact dependencies and interpretation This edition selects Blue Language package `8XGYNufx24r7Dc5bGoeobcGNCn9roLzSfZCQyHBTaTx4`, whose complete specification Text is `H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQmWnc`. Node construction, exact references, specialization, output admission and BlueIds have the meaning defined by that Language release. BEX is independent of Contracts. A host may supply Language-backed matching, node identity, finite reads and explicit intrinsics. Contracts is one such host and binds the supplied BEX context and meter according to its own specification. BEX MUST NOT substitute ambient state or an unversioned implementation for these declared interfaces. Package imports supply exact content. Authoring prefixes are local bindings and do not leak through transitive imports. An imported definition retains its exact references. Mounting another package cannot change the selected interpreter or replace an existing type reference. Within this edition's interpreted package graph, the selected Language release MUST agree throughout; cross-Language conversion and mixed-rule cyclic sets are not defined. One selected Language governs a complete cyclic identity set and its owning proof. ## 3. Purpose and imported language BEX evaluates data-encoded programs against explicit, read-only inputs and produces values, ordered changesets, and ordered events. It neither fetches arbitrary resources nor publishes a document. A Contracts processor decides whether proposed effects can be applied; Coordination determines which authenticated external input is eligible. The reader is assumed to know Blue Language 1.0. Node admission, effective types, specialization, exact versus Source representations, references, set finalization, and BlueId are imported, not redefined. A BEX value is not a Blue node. In particular, Python object identity, dictionary iteration order, and native truth testing do not define BEX semantics. The executable algorithm appendix contains the complete evaluator and host-value algorithms. Readable rules and executable algorithms together define this edition; disagreement is a defect, not permission to choose either result. ## 4. Machine and invocation An invocation has a compiled program; an explicit context; a gas meter; lexical function frames; an ordered changeset; and an ordered event list. Context supplies the selected document snapshot, event, current contract, previous step results, named bindings, and executing scope. Optional adapters provide finite document reads, Blue specialization checks, and exact-type intrinsics. No process-global variable is a program binding. No Python expression is evaluated from program text. The interpreter recognizes data forms, not Python, JavaScript, or embedded shell commands. An installed intrinsic is trusted host code and is outside that sandbox boundary. A successful invocation returns `Result(value, changeset, events, gas_used)`. It does not apply its changes. Returned effects remain ordinary BEX values until the Contracts output boundary has validated and converted them. ## 5. Value domains and absence The domains are undefined, null, Text, Integer, Double, Boolean, Object, and List. `UNDEFINED` is a singleton distinct from Python `None`, which represents internal BEX null. Boolean is not Integer. Objects have Text keys. Integers use exact integer arithmetic; Doubles use finite decimal observations and cross the Blue Double boundary as finite binary64 values. Missing member lookup yields undefined. Undefined object members are omitted by Blue conversion. Undefined list elements, including sparse overlay holes, cannot cross that boundary. Null is not an empty object and is rejected at the Blue output boundary. An actual empty object remains an actual empty object. `$emptyObject` is the explicit empty-object constructor. `$exists` is false only for undefined. Null therefore exists. Truth is false for undefined, null, false, empty Text, empty Object, and empty List; other values are true, **including numeric zero**. `$empty` and `$isEmpty` test the inverse of this truth rule, not Python's truthiness. ## 6. Numeric and Text rules Integer conversion accepts integers, integral finite numbers, and canonical decimal integer text. Fractional values and noncanonical integer spellings fail. Numeric conversion rejects Boolean, collections, nonfinite numbers, and malformed numeric text. Arithmetic operators in this edition produce exact Integer results, and division requires an exact Integer quotient. Division by zero or a fractional quotient fails. Numeric equality compares numeric value across Integer and Double. Other equality is domain-sensitive and recursive. It must not be substituted for BlueId equality or Language specialization. Collections do not stringify implicitly. Null and undefined stringify to empty Text where coercion is allowed; names, paths, keys, and operation names require presence and cannot use that absence coercion. Text-key ordering is Unicode code-point ordering. Gas size estimation counts UTF-16 code units, not Python string length or UTF-8 bytes. These are different operations and must remain separate. Nonfinite Doubles and lone Unicode surrogates are invalid runtime values at the relevant boundary. There is no universal source-depth, call-frame, numeric-text, Integer-result-size or Blue-output Integer-length ceiling. Integer arithmetic, finite binary64 values, canonical text, static recursion rejection and output validity remain mandatory. A host that cannot compile or evaluate otherwise valid finite work reports operational incompleteness, not invalid syntax, a false arithmetic error or gas exhaustion. Gas is a logical work rule, not an operating-system resource sandbox. Large operand/allocation paths require correctly placed deterministic work charges and safe host isolation; a local machine failure cannot create a different semantic history. ## 7. Source classification and static positions A single-key object whose key starts with `$` is an executable form when encountered in expression or statement position. It must name an installed operator valid for that position. Other objects are recursively evaluated data constructors. `$literal` prevents evaluation of its payload as program data, but does not authorize executable material in static Blue definition positions. Type-related and schema positions are static. Constants and function-argument patterns are static. Compilation rejects unknown operators, invalid operand shapes, unknown variables/constants/functions, malformed static names, reserved user-container names, invalid call argument sets, and recursive function-call graphs. Both sides of a lazy runtime construct still undergo static validation. A function body selects `expr` ahead of `do`. An explicit named entry must exist and take no arguments. The implementation also validates the root body even when a named entry is selected. Definition constants/functions can be supplied as an already available object to the compiler; loading a referenced program definition is a host integration obligation. ## 8. Evaluation order and laziness Object constructors evaluate keys in deterministic order; lists evaluate left to right. Function arguments evaluate in key order. Lazy operators evaluate only the branch or subsequent operand needed to establish the result. This applies to Boolean connectives, coalescing/default selection, conditionals, and lookup defaults. A static error in an unused branch is still an error. A runtime error or gas charge in an unselected branch does not occur. Empty or missing values cannot be replaced by Python idioms such as `value or fallback` unless they implement the particular BEX operator's rule. ## 9. Reads and observations `$document`, `$event`, `$currentContract`, `$binding`, `$steps`, `$var`, and `$const` read only their designated source. A variable or constant name containing `/` remains a name; its optional pointer is a separate operand. A named step is addressed by the step's actual Language `name` label, not its list position when a name was supplied. A Compute invocation sees a stable selected-document snapshot. A later Compute step sees effects successfully applied by earlier steps. `$resultValue` overlays this invocation's accumulated changes on its snapshot; it does not publish them. Finite managed-document reads use the closure's selected dependency projection, never an independently advancing source's latest public head. The context's matcher implements `$is` using Blue semantic admission and specialization. The interpreter does not guess that a JSON shape is a valid Blue type. Missing patterns, unknown required definitions, and uninstalled matcher capabilities are not accepted as successful matches. ### Exact node identity `$nodeBlueId: EXPR` evaluates EXPR once and returns a Text containing the ordinary Language BlueId. Charge `nodeIdentityRequested = 5` after evaluating the operand and before calling the host's Language identity boundary. The boundary shares the invocation meter and cannot use a separate unmetered hash implementation. An admitted exact host collection retains its selected exact identity, including owning-set member identity, without expanding its descendants. A newly computed value passes the existing strict Blue-output validation and Language Exact admission/identity construction. Newly built containers preserve exact nested operands and their identity evidence; storage presentation cannot change charges. Null or undefined roots, malformed references, invalid type slots and incomplete owning-set evidence fail; missing required content is not replaced by an invented identity. Scalars are ordinary BEX scalar values and receive their corresponding Language scalar identity; metadata erased by scalar observation is not reconstructed. Equality and type specialization remain different operations from exact identity comparison. The standard Contracts context installs this boundary. Standalone BEX hosts supply `Context.node_blue_id(value, gas)` backed by the same Language operations; without it the operator fails with a boundary error. It does not perform network lookup or register user code. `processingEvent` remains a Contracts binding read through `$binding`; no `$processingEvent` operator is introduced. ## 10. Pointers and ordered changesets BEX value pointers use JSON-pointer escaping. Both empty Text and `/` designate the value root in this profile. This differs from the Language query API's empty-key behavior; adapters must not delegate blindly. Relative document paths resolve against the executing scope; already absolute document paths remain absolute. A Contracts processor separately checks whether a proposed absolute path is writable by that scope. A changeset is an ordered list of add, replace, or remove proposals. Non-remove proposals require a value. Remove ignores no hidden expression: its value operand is not evaluated by the append operation. Appending preserves duplicate operations and their order. BEX's observation overlay is **not** Contracts mutation. Overlay removal from a List creates a sparse undefined position and does not shift later elements. Actual Contracts array removal does shift later elements. Intermediate overlay objects are constructed deterministically. A sparse result may be observed internally but cannot be serialized as a Blue List containing undefined. ## 11. Collections Collection operations support Lists in index order and Objects in sorted key order. Query bindings are lexical for that query and are restored afterward. Statement `forEach` uses its declared iteration slots and executes its body for each selected item. An empty collection executes no iteration body. Map and flat-map produce Lists; flat-map requires a List result per item. Filter preserves the input's collection category. Reduce threads its accumulator. Some, find, and find-entry stop after the first decisive match. Find-entry preserves the selected value and occurrence information rather than replacing occurrence identity with value identity. Iteration gas is charged for each admitted visited item. Short-circuiting stops both later evaluation and later iteration charges. Collection construction retains its specified logical charges. Host memory/cancellation controls are operational and may interrupt without establishing a semantic rejection; they are not universal collection-size restrictions. ## 12. Variables, functions, and return `let` declares function-frame slots. Parallel declarations evaluate their initializers against the old frame; an explicit declaration order enables ordered dependency between initializers. `set` updates an existing declared slot. Conditional declaration visibility is checked statically. Function calls use isolated frames, exact declared argument-name sets, and supplied Blue argument-pattern checks. Functions share the invocation's effect accumulators and gas meter but do not implicitly capture another function's locals. Recursion is rejected during compilation. Business-process cycles therefore arise from Contracts event work, not recursive BEX function calls. Explicit return exits the current function/body. Without an explicit result, the interpreter returns the accumulated changeset and events. A called function's return does not terminate its caller. Failure exits the invocation and does not authorize partial publication. ## 13. Effects and host intrinsics Event append preserves multiplicity. Two equal event values are two emission occurrences; their BlueIds may be equal. Occurrence identity belongs to the hosting Contracts closure. The BEX interpreter does not deduplicate by content identity. An intrinsic must have an exact static type ID present in the invocation's installed capability registry. Unknown IDs fail compilation. Runtime removal of a capability fails execution. Intrinsics receive copied explicit operands and the same gas meter; they must return explicit BEX values and account for bounded work. Files, network, clock, and randomness are not implicit capabilities. ## 14. Gas Compilation consumes no semantic gas. Each admitted expression, statement, read, call, pointer operation, collection item, append, and size-dependent operation is charged by the algorithm at its specified point. A failed charge is recorded as rejected work and does not increment admitted `used` gas. Accepted charges update the running scalar only. They have no canonical rows, ordinals or transcript. Results contain `gas_used`, not `gas_trace`. The default standalone allowance remains 10,000,000. A caller-supplied shared meter is never reset; each invocation reports its own admitted contribution. Local counters and the shared total still enforce each charge before work. Retain only the first rejected charge, without a charge ordinal; a failed meter cannot resume accepting work. Optional debug traces are noncanonical, off by default, and never required for conformance, replay or durable publication. A compatibility API may expose an empty trace accessor, but this is not a result field in the new protocol. This is a new exact BEX edition. Earlier publications retain their original trace-bearing result and conformance rules; hosts must select those rules explicitly when replaying earlier histories. The default scalar tariffs are: expression 1; statement 1; document read 2; event/current-contract/steps/variable read 1; result-value read 2; pointer get base 1; pointer set base 3; object set base 2; append-change/event base 5; iteration item 1; function call 2. Size/path contributions are defined by the algorithms, not by wall-clock time. A Compute step can impose a positive local cap while charging each admitted operation to a shared Contracts closure meter. A local-cap rejection is distinguished from shared-cap rejection in the first-rejected-charge diagnostic. A cap is checked before work is admitted. Gas allowance, used gas, attempted rejected charge, and operational cancellation are different values. The charge positions and tariffs in the executable annex define this edition. A conforming implementation preserves the deterministic admitted gas total and first rejected charge for identical inputs. Equivalence to a different BEX release or another tariff is a separate interoperability claim, not an additional unstated rule. ## 15. Blue output boundary `blue_value` converts runtime values into a JSON-compatible, null-free proposal. It is not semantic admission and does not return a BlueId. Authoring aliases are resolved in an explicit authoring/preparation stage before this proposal enters the runtime output boundary. Runtime type slots MUST contain exact Blue references. The host admits the proposal through Language Exact admission and uses the resulting validated exact value; it MUST NOT resolve aliases, replay Source list construction, or reinterpret a generated string as an installed type at this stage. A BEX program may compute arbitrary Text, but a Text in a runtime type slot is not thereby a type reference. A host accepting raw data-encoded programs with unresolved literal type aliases must reject the resulting effect, not silently reinterpret it. The corrected boundary does not collapse null to `{}`. A whole null event or null patch value fails. Undefined object members may disappear, but required fields must still satisfy the host effect schema. Effect structural validation precedes mutation, so a later malformed effect cannot cause an earlier effect to be published. ## 16. Errors and determinism Compilation error, runtime error, invalid Blue output, actual gas exhaustion and host/incomplete execution are distinct failure families. The former portable resource caps are removed. Resource exceptions must propagate as incomplete host work, not be wrapped into ordinary BEX runtime failure and terminally rejected by a feeder. A caller may not turn an unavailable required Language definition or provider proof into a successful computation. A runtime exception never means "no changes" success. Determinism requires identical admitted inputs, program and definitions, installed capabilities, matcher behavior, selected document projection, and gas schedule. Python hash seed, input-map insertion order, cached parsing, and unrelated documents must not affect the semantic result. Stateful or nondeterministic intrinsics violate this requirement unless their observations are explicit frozen inputs. ## 17. Executable inventory and conformance the operator appendix lists every installed expression and statement operator. The complete annex supplies their compilation, evaluation, value and gas definitions. Each marked module is extracted without modification. The source table in this specification identifies the exact modules and their dependencies. Conformance preserves successful results, ordered proposals, short-circuit behavior, static errors, runtime errors, output-boundary errors and gas observations. Required cases include Boolean/Integer distinction; undefined/null/empty-object distinctions; exact arithmetic; type-pattern matching; every operator family; function scope; side-effect order; Unicode ordering and size; output rejection; and local/shared gas limits. Passing a finite corpus is evidence, not a proof for all programs or capabilities. ## 18. External capability boundary The standard algorithms require no arbitrary external I/O. A host supplies explicit document projections, a Language-backed matcher, and any selected intrinsic registry. A missing required capability or exact definition cannot be converted to successful evaluation. Intrinsics are trusted, explicitly installed code with their own semantics and bounded work; an unknown intrinsic ID is rejected. This edition defines no production network acquisition service, operating-system sandbox, universal intrinsic package or Java diagnostic mapping. An independent implementation conforms to this edition by preserving its specified results, not by reproducing an undocumented behavior of another runtime. Host memory protection and process isolation remain operational obligations; they cannot change the semantic outcome of an admitted computation. ## 19. Composition with Language and Contracts User-binding declarations are constants, functions, function arguments, local `$let` slots (both forms), and collection/loop item, key, index and accumulator slots. All reject the reserved names listed by `compiler.RESERVED`, including `$previousItems`. Ordinary literal object keys and host-provided read bindings are not user-binding declarations. `$previousItems` is a reserved Language name in BEX user-binding containers. It is not a BEX instruction and cannot manufacture Language list inheritance at runtime. `$previous` and other Source-only controls likewise do not replace Exact admission of effects. An unevaluated object containing dynamic expression fields is not an instance of its eventual result type. A repository can author that value through ordinary BEX `$objectFromEntries` construction with exact type references. Resulting events and patch values are admitted only after evaluation. Rewriting a program changes its identity and may change its gas; this does not weaken Language validation. The Contracts invocation supplies the selected executing document as the BEX document. BEX receives no ambient enclosing process or independently advancing public head. Contracts owns mutation boundaries, internal event occurrence identities, initialization, termination, checkpoint settlement, graph finalization and publication. BEX returns proposed effects and never advances those states itself. The standard Contracts binding uses its contextual business-value document projection for both `canonical` and `resolved` BEX read modes. This is an explicit Contracts binding, not a redefinition of the Language serialization APIs. Configured program data is distinct from effective business values: inherited specification prose must not be inserted into a literal program or effect. ## 20. Release and identity The complete specification comprises its readable rules, operator reference, executable algorithms and explicit dependency selection. Its BlueId names that exact Text. The publication manifest records its identity outside the Text, avoiding a self-reference. A normative change creates a new exact specification identity. Test reports, implementation-only packaging, tutorials and provenance notes do not silently amend this edition. ## 21. Immutable host values The numeric, equality, binding and control semantics are those defined in this specification. A trusted host may supply immutable collections implementing the host-value interface in values.py. Collection kind, keys, reads, variables, function arguments and persistent overlays operate on these values without eager recursive cloning. Output conversion uses the host's finite exact representation. The host must bind coherent resolution and meter demanded work. `$fail` and `$failIf` expose the distinct EXECUTION_REJECTED diagnostic so a host can classify explicit business rejection without treating every BEX error as a user refusal. Arithmetic and control tariffs are defined by the executable gas module. Collection equality keeps its ordered short-circuit comparisons. A host can provide a stable comparison key for an exact effective recipe in its captured context. Repeated pairs in a cyclic comparison need not be unfolded again; unrelated fields and unequal pairs remain observable. Equality must not eagerly read the remaining values after a decisive mismatch. ## 22. Shared host metering When invoked by Contracts, BEX uses the same bounded meter: **10,000,000 maximum/default** for the complete Contracts attempt, with supported stricter local limits. No BEX frame, intrinsic, compiled-program cache or lower standalone-Gas setting can detach from or reset the parent meter. Standalone BEX API budget configuration remains a separate API contract; it cannot enlarge the standard Contracts allowance. Work charges apply independently of physical resource controls. Conversion, Integer arithmetic, collections, strings and output sizing use the exact counters, quantities and charge positions defined here. Implementations MUST NOT substitute after-the-fact bit-length caps or wall-clock timeouts for the specified meter. Any changed tariff requires a separately identified specification and conformance vectors. Preserve ordinary validation failure order and short-circuit behavior; no charges execute in an unselected branch. Compiler structure checks remain semantically complete, including unused branches and forbidden recursive functions. Compilation still consumes no BEX semantic gas under this schedule; any inability to finish compilation is a prerequisite/host failure, not a fabricated failed debit. This rule neither exempts the containing Contracts work from its existing charges nor makes first-time authoring free in physical resources. ## 23. Resource-proportional work accounting Contracts continues to supply one shared meter with a maximum of 10000000. BEX compilation and host prerequisite acquisition are outside that invocation meter. A host interruption is incomplete execution, never a BEX semantic rejection. Three additional BEX counters have unit weight 1: `integerWork`, `textWork`, and `valueMember`. They are charged to the current invoking member before their corresponding work. Let L(n) = max(1, ceil(bit_length(abs(n))/32)). Addition and subtraction debit max(L(a),L(b)); multiplication debits L(a)*L(b); division debits 2*L(a)*L(b), before the zero/exact-division check and arithmetic. A conversion from Integer to decimal Text/Double debits L(n)^2 before conversion. Conversion from decimal Text to Integer uses max(1,ceil(4*digitCount/32))^2; decimal numeric values use their coefficient digits plus positive decimal exponent. Text syntax inspection also debits ceil(codePointCount/64) `textWork` before scanning. An Integer already represented as Integer needs no conversion debit. Runtime values are immutable during evaluation: literal reads, variable reads, function arguments and results share values; operators never mutate them. Program input and public Result defensive copies are physical boundary work. Explicit collection construction and snapshots of the accumulating `$changeset`/`$events` debit one `valueMember` per member before allocation. Comparison debits one `valueMember` per visited pair before inspecting it. Immutable host views are retained without traversing their descendants; their actual reads remain charged by the owning host. Text traversal/construction debits `textWork` per at-most-64-code-point block; Integer comparison debits the sum of operand limbs. Equality visits pairs in order and stops on the first mismatch. Concatenation and split debit their known input/output-bound text blocks before allocation; collection concatenation/merge debit each copied member before insertion. Specified size-dependent effect/overlay charges retain their base and size formula, but debit the base first and then each visited size contribution before traversing that contribution. Scalars use the existing UTF-16 size definition; Integer decimal conversion is precharged as above. No whole recursive output walk precedes a single future debit. Exact host transfer uses its canonical accounting form defined below, independent of inline/reference materialization; it does not expand untouched bodies. A rejected debit is never admitted; the first failed debit and its complete arbitrary-precision quantity are retained. Diagnostic size is not saturated. The admitted gas total and first rejected charge are observable results of this schedule; accepted-charge history is not retained. ## 24. Equality and conversion ordering All equality callers, including `$eq`, `$ne` and `$includes`, use the same numeric-coercing comparator. Visit object members in Unicode code-point key order, independently of native insertion order, host enumeration order or Python hash seed. List order is unchanged. {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Clause connections preview

Directly authored BEX, lowered by `Connected Clause` into existing Contracts and
Time definitions during the ordinary clause planning hook. There is no JavaScript
or Python business-code generator. `Hello Clause` is a tiny reusable action.

Exports: Connected Clause, Hello Clause, Hello Said, Greeting Request, Ping, and
Other Ping. The last two provide distinct nominal event types for the examples.

The Java `ClauseConnectionsTest` builds and mounts an exact preview package from
these files against this repository's pinned dependencies. It does not add the
package to the application's default catalog. Run from the repository root:

```bash
runtime/gradlew -p runtime :blue-core-service:test --tests blue.core.ClauseConnectionsTest --no-daemon
```

Use JDK 21. The archive and observations are written under ignored
`reports/clause-connections/`. See `docs/guides/CLAUSE-CONNECTIONS.md` for the
source matrix, execution rules, complete examples, testing boundaries, and
preview restrictions. Python runtime qualification is deferred.

The `blue-package.yaml` manifest selects version 0.2.0-preview.1 for the
composition kit. This version adds explicit library-owned automatic actions,
managed embedding bindings, shared Compute Definitions, `actionResult`, and
`embed: false` for observers of already managed documents. See the companion
`docs/guides/COMPOSITION-TUTORIAL.md` for Payment and business examples.


Unpublished candidate. Authored Blue/BEX definitions are authoritative. See ../docs/payment-family.md for the tested package selection and integration boundaries.

## Conditions on a named action

`parameters.conditions.<actionName>` adds a BEX predicate to every connection of
that action. It is evaluated after the action's original requirement and typed
arguments, before preflight or any `before`, action or `after` effects. It can only
add a restriction. A false result fails with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`; an unknown
action name is rejected during planning. Omitting a condition adds no restriction.
Conditions use the action's own document and selected named sources, not an
incoming observer's state. Cross-document changes require explicit application
events when they are intended to trigger an action automatically.

## Structural state

A clause type can declare `initialState`, keyed by a pointer binding name, with an
object initial value. Connection planning contributes that state through the
ordinary Clauses state-ownership checks. This installs data without dispatching
a business action and does not grant an exception to Activation. Ledger and
Amendments use it for their empty initial state. A state-only clause may omit
`actions`; a supplied action declaration must still be an object. Only the admitted clause type
supplies this declaration; runtime requests cannot inject a state initializer.
"}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Document Dispatch

Document Dispatch Policy evaluates a read-only BEX program once before each native channel delivery, using the current local document view and a runtime-owned dispatch binding containing kind, channel and operation. All installed policies must return an object with allowed Boolean and optional reason Text; policies run in canonical contract order without short-circuiting. A false decision skips every handler on that delivery. External inputs are still consumed and checkpointed, never deferred or replayed after policy changes. Embedded documents process independently; their installed updates precede the parent delivery under the existing native schedule. Only runtime-generated delivery kinds distinguish embedded and internal work from external messages. Decisions are committed in local completion evidence. Programs cannot emit events, change state or terminate processing. Ordinary BEX metering applies plus one dispatchPolicyCheck unit per policy. The binding is additive and opt-in by an exact declaration; documents without this declaration retain their dispatch semantics.

This candidate is an explicit native extension. Importing it alone does not grant authority or install code. Hosts must support the exact type and rules binding. The BEX decision belongs to the declaring document.

A denied request may publish native progress and independently processed child updates, but executes no handlers for that request. Its completion records `allowed: false`; Coordination records `DISPATCH_REJECTED` with the policy reason. Caller retries must be new requests. Canonical input ordering, authenticated provider history and dependency receiving remain unchanged.
"}
