{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts — demand-scoped execution edition

**Status:** normative candidate rules for a local experimental publication; not a qualified release or an implemented conformance claim.
**Proposed edition:** `blue-contracts/2026-10-22-demand-scoped-1`.
**Proposed package version:** `1.0.0-demand-scoped.1`; final release metadata is assigned by the canonical build owner.
**Baseline:** [final-gas specification](contracts-final-gas.md).
**Conformance and implementation gates:** [demand-scoped cases](contracts-demand-scoped-conformance.md).

The canonical build assigns the candidate BlueIds from these exact rules and their pinned imports. Prior archived publications and existing specifications remain unchanged. This candidate may be built locally to bind and test the new implementation; it MUST NOT become a production default or a qualified release until the linked conformance gates and normal lifecycle tests pass. Sections 12.1–12.5 define the replacement algorithms and take precedence over the baseline's conflicting whole-certification and whole-closure calls; baseline scheduling and unrelated semantics remain unchanged. The candidate label is not evidence that D1–D5 have passed.

## 1. Contract and compatibility

The new edition defines successful execution as completion of every obligation required by the requested Contracts transition, including its required evidence retention. It does not certify every value transitively reachable from its input, event or result. Blue Language remains the authority for exact identity, effective types, constraints, exact evidence and cyclic proof validation. `strict_certify`/`NativeRuntime.strict` retain their full meaning.

The public cause remains the original exact event and supplied timestamp. Channel Event Checkpoint retains `event: {blueId: ORIGINAL_EVENT_ID}`. Event bytes, signatures and predecessor links MUST NOT be rewritten. This edition introduces neither `entryId` nor `eventProofs`, serialized coverage certificates, external completion tokens or new trusted claims in document content.

All prior editions retain their original processing, certification, gas and storage rules. An exact installed edition binding selects this policy before a request executes; availability, account age, author-supplied labels and cache state cannot select it. New and old account runtimes may coexist in one process without sharing edition-dependent conclusions. Cross-edition processing of one managed document is outside this release.

Unless explicitly revised here, retain the final-gas edition's operation selection, deterministic scheduling, protected markers, occurrence identities, lifecycle, generalization, failure observations and public API. Coordination determines signed source validity, authority, history and admission under its separately selected edition; Contracts does not infer these from an event-shaped value.

## 2. One obligation policy

An invocation has a private working context and an obligation set. An obligation identifies:

```
(edition, input snapshot, original cause, current exact member/view,
 contextual Recipe, processor role, operation/purpose, required coverage)
```

The tuple is a semantic identity, not a required new serialized format. Coverage denotes what was established: exact identity/evidence, effective header, contextual predicate, selected value/subtree, managed occurrence, or complete Language value/definition. These categories MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable trust levels. A contextual predicate fact is not a whole-value certificate, even when its exact BlueId equals a completely certified value in another role.

The native processor and the actual operation determine obligations. Source availability MUST NOT change their meaning. A successful full-content execution and a successful missing-unused-content execution on the same source MUST have identical observations and logical gas. A required missing record produces `NEEDS_RESOURCES`; invalid evidence produces the native validation error; unsupported semantics produces an explicit failure, never a successful filter mismatch or a false absence.

Obligations are extended by actual observations and writes. Conditional BEX evaluation adds obligations for its discriminant and selected branch under normal BEX semantics. An unselected branch does not acquire an execution obligation merely because it is reachable. Metadata and constraints may nevertheless require inspecting it. This rule does not allow the processor to ignore an already established obligation when a resource is unavailable.

There is no exemption set keyed only by BlueId. The same exact body may be opaque predecessor data and a required current operand. The latter role MUST perform its own contextual validation and demand missing content. Repeated obligations may reuse verified facts only when their complete context and coverage agree; metering follows the logical work rule, not physical reuse.

## 3. Native observations and contextual validity

The current Java interfaces provide building blocks, not a ready-made general scoped certificate:

| Operation | Actual interface | Meaning and restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact root/evidence | `NativeRuntime.identity`, `NativeRuntime.open`; `RuntimeBridge.open` | Exact record and owning proof are verified when opened. A hash/reference alone does not establish type validity. |
| Effective contextual header | `NativeRuntime.head/readHead(Recipe, runtime)` | Preserve effective type, inherited contributions, requirements and metadata. A header is not a full certificate. |
| Descendant selection | `NativeRuntime.child(Head, key)`; `RuntimeBridge.child/select` | Derive the child from the effective parent Recipe; do not replace it with a standalone reference that loses `valueType`, `itemType` or inherited requirements. |
| Contextual whole subtree | `NativeRuntime.validate(Recipe, runtime, goal)` | Validates that selected subtree using Language semantics. It may demand descendants; it is not a partial-validation flag. |
| Containing constraints | `runtime.validateConstraints(Head, root)` | Run native constraints against the actual effective head. Constraint evaluation may demand more content. This call alone does not check every metadata, type or structural obligation. |
| Native type/definition | `NativeRuntime.ancestry/subtype`, `NativeRuntime.strict(...,"definition")` where whole definition is required | Do not replace native subtype, fixed-value, specification or schema logic with string/type-name checks. |
| Scalar observation | `RuntimeBridge.project` on the selected Recipe | Projection consumes a value; its result must not be hashed as the original exact identity. |
| Full certificate | `NativeRuntime.strict` / `RuntimeBridge.certify` | Unchanged complete Language check; only actual successful full checks may populate its cache. |

Every operation that observes a node MUST establish the validity of the information it uses, including the containing constraints that govern that observation. Own and inherited type/schema, `specification`, fixed values, labels, merge policy and container metadata are not optional simply because the selected descendant is otherwise well typed. Requiredness, presence and absence are resolved through the effective parent; unavailable evidence is not absence.

A processor MAY defer a child's value validation only if neither its action nor a governing predicate requires that value. It MUST still check governing predicates that apply at its selected container boundary. For example, an invalid `maxFields` on `contracts` cannot be bypassed by validating each contract separately. A `valueType` constraint on `count` cannot be discharged by certifying the number outside its parent. A specification reference required for the selected node must resolve and validate with Language's definition semantics.

The lowering of each native handler into these obligations MUST be listed and tested. If a Language predicate requires the entire subtree, invoke that native predicate with the required evidence; do not substitute a structural guess. If the existing interfaces cannot express a necessary selected predicate without imposing unrelated full validation, record an executable reproducer and an explicit API/design decision before publication. This draft does not authorize altering Language or BEX semantics or introducing a global skip-validation switch.

### 3.1 First bounded lowering: required containers

The initial additive Java primitive observes an already-required object or list container. It does not decide optional-child presence and is not a replacement for complete snapshot validation. It verifies authored and effective type/specification/item/key/value metadata through native definition checks. For an empty effective constraint description, there is no constraint predicate to evaluate: after explicit required-container shape checks, this lowering does not call the native constraint routine's incidental concrete-child counting. A nonempty effective constraint continues through native evaluation and may widen the demand, except for the required-object presence lowering below. This is a Contracts obligation/gas-plan decision, not a change to Language strict validation.

A container/header obligation MUST retain its original contextual Recipe and discharge its governing definitions. After constructing the native effective Head and establishing presence using the existing native occurrence/root rules, it MAY discharge the effective constraint without native object-field counting if and only if the Head kind is `object`, the checked occurrence is present, and the effective constraints description contains exactly `required` with a Boolean value. The required-presence predicate is then satisfied; no field-count predicate exists. This MUST still charge the existing `schemaPredicateEvaluated` obligation for `required` and MUST NOT establish a whole-value certificate or reusable value obligation.

Absent occurrences, scalar/list/none kinds, and every other effective constraint combination MUST continue through native validation. Inherited constraints are part of the effective description. In particular, `minFields`, `maxFields`, key/value/item rules and required scalar/list payload checks MUST NOT be bypassed. Governing metadata and observed ordinary records retain their existing obligations. Native presence remains authoritative: an object-shaped definition alone is not a present value. Legacy validation and tariffs are unchanged.

Canonical key validation is currently exposed only through whole native subtree validation. The first primitive therefore widens a container with explicit `keyType` to complete selected validation; it does not claim lazy `keyType` support or duplicate Language's key parser. Actual selected-value use performs full selected exact certification plus the contextual Recipe validation, preserving parent `itemType`/`valueType` requirements. Neither the container observation nor its return value is stored as a full certificate. These restrictions remain explicit until tested lowering is expanded.

### 3.2 Handler requirements

Discovery reads the effective contract map, keys, runtime type ancestry, ordering and fields used to classify/route a declaration. It MUST NOT project or certify an entire workflow merely to identify its handler. The exact installed runtime catalogue supplies the handler policy; business document IDs and workflow IDs do not.

Before an eligible handler executes, validate its consumed declaration fields, filter and selected step under their contextual Recipes. Filters preserve native presence, refinement and constraint semantics; only proven mismatch returns false. A request schema or authorization predicate that requires a payload makes that payload required. The same applies to ordinary observers: operation routing is not an exemption from an observer's actual reads.

Initial supported handler policies MUST be derived from the actual Order, Activation and mandate primitive inventory. Adding a recognized custom runtime without a defined obligation policy MUST fail explicitly, not inherit a permissive policy. This is a runtime capability rule, not a business whitelist.

## 5. Invocation and publication algorithm

The following pseudocode specifies ordering and invariants. `require_for` is a proposed internal obligation operation, not an existing Language API. Its handler-specific lowering and the complete executable reference implementation are release gates.

```
execute(edition, input, originalEvent, time):
    assert installed exact edition/bindings
    tx := fork input state, Language evidence context, obligation facts,
               archive updates, completion registrations and retained output
    require_for(tx, RESTORE_OR_INPUT, input)
    require_for(tx, EVENT_DISPATCH, originalEvent, time)
    run existing deterministic Contracts scheduling in tx
        before each observation: require_for(tx, selected contextual role)
        before installing each patch: native construct/generalize and
            require_for(tx, affected contextual write obligations)
        after patch: reconcile and finalize required local/graph obligations
    require_for(tx, FINALIZE, resulting managed graph)
    retained := prepare_required_records(tx, input, result, originalEvent)
    verify retained records can satisfy cold restore and local receive obligations
    seal outcome and its cause/edition/member bindings
    atomically install tx context, stable state, retained output, archive and
        process-local completion establishment
    return APPLIED
on missing, invalid, exhausted or incomplete execution/required retention:
    discard tx effects, evidence additions, selected facts and registrations
    return the edition's failure/incomplete result against original input
```

Preparing retention is part of success, not an optional operation after completion establishment. A late export failure cannot leave a newly capturable result, advanced checkpoint, archive entry or reusable selected fact behind. Preserve previous prepared/committed output. Repeating the exact input/event/time after obtaining the required evidence runs against the original stable input and does not duplicate a previously partial mutation.

This local atomic boundary is distinct from durable host publication. The host's existing journal transaction MUST atomically publish the completed state/evidence, original cause, progress, emitted effects and retry obligations. A transient local result is not evidence of durable commit. Host failure cannot publish a receipt/progress record without its required content. This draft does not require a new journal or service.

## 6. Completion guarantee and normal receiving

A new-edition completion establishes: this installed edition executed the identified input and original cause through all required obligations, obtained the exact resulting managed state and ordered output, and prepared all evidence required by this completion's storage/receive contract. It does NOT assert complete Language validity of every transitively reachable value.

Preserve the existing local capability boundary:

1. Only the actual successful local attempt may establish an outcome; bind input snapshot identity, event BlueId/timestamp, release, exact runtime bindings, before/after member views, receipt, units and ordered effects.
2. `capture` requires that established local outcome and matching process-local provenance. Validate selected members, owner birth rules and complete unit inclusion. A user-provided receipt, after-body or matching hash is insufficient.
3. `receive`/live receive verifies issuer, capability lifetime, cause, compatible exact edition/bindings, owned members, captured occurrence tickets and predecessor views. It validates its own contextual obligations. Incorporation is not full certification of the source's opaque closure.
4. Process restart does not deserialize a trusted capability from input bytes. The installed privileged local `CompletionReader` may recover an atomically committed local completion, verify descriptor/receipt and bindings, restore required before/after evidence under this edition, and re-establish local provenance. Arbitrary imported snapshots cannot invoke this path.
5. Modified, foreign, expired, overlapping or incompatible completion records remain rejected. This edition does not define public third-party execution proofs.

The existing descriptor's `release`, `runtimes`, before/after vectors, event, timestamp and receipt carry these bindings; there is no new user-authored coverage flag. Changing an edition changes its immutable specification identity and therefore its interpretation. The reference implementation MUST explicitly apply the new guarantee at establishment and rehydration; deleting `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION` is not an implementation.

## 7. Retention, privacy and cyclic exact content

Compute required records from the obligation roles and replay/restore requirements, not from whatever extra content happens to be cached. A record may be required in one role even if another role defers the same BlueId. Retaining unused private bodies because they were available in the full-control runtime violates deterministic scoped export/privacy.

For acyclic exact records, preserve exact identity while emitting finite child references; verify identity after serialization. Traversal follows the required roles. Do not serialize an inline ancestor wholesale when it contains an excluded descendant. A missing excluded descendant is not replaced by null, empty content or a fabricated value.

For a cyclic member, retain and verify the Language owning-set proof and required member body using the existing canonical proof/body mechanism. Do not emit an ordinary acyclic `mode: exact` record under `master#i`. Deduplicate with a finite identity/context/role work set, not by dropping owning proofs or globally whitelisting an identity. Historical graph edges such as A(T) → B(T) → A(T−1) remain exact historical edges, not latest-state aliases.

Cold restore opens and verifies actual supplied exact records and owning proofs, then derives the required obligations anew under the selected edition. Serialized statements of prior validation are not trusted. Missing content needed for these obligations must still wait/fail. Record presence or prior selective success cannot seed complete closure caches, `RuntimeBridge.certified`, or full Language validation caches.

The primitive inventory must identify actual cycles used by Order/Activation. There is no global cycle prohibition. If a required cycle cannot be retained privately with valid owning evidence, report that concrete case and resolve its contract before claiming qualification.


### 12.3 Required records and genuine cyclic proof/body

The required-record worklist contains `(exact node, contextual Recipe and ancestor obligations, role, retention purpose)` derived from structural restore/receive requirements and actual invocation obligations.

Transport preparation also retains ordinary records for local-free exact Values actually constructed during this invocation and the required evidence of its actual emitted outputs. Construction capture is scoped to newly constructed Values and their established exact identities; it MUST NOT enumerate provider inventory, traverse explicit Refs or certify future referenced payloads. These records use the same native shallow-record/owning-proof preparation as other required transport. Invocation forks copy this pending retention state; successful finish merges it into prepared content before sealing and publication, while failed or abandoned work drops it. Preparing exact evidence for actual emitted outputs does not add a second logical tariff or a new completion authority. This is produced-content retention, not a demand for every possible future handler body.

The required-record worklist is not a snapshot of all available resolver evidence and not a full Language closure walk. Each role defines which child edges are required; actual consumed values and governing definitions include their required validation dependencies. A bare original event reference remains present without forcing unused payload edges.

```
prepare_records(roots, obligation roles):
    todo := deterministic required roots/roles
    seen := empty set of (identity, role, purpose)

    check := fresh NativeRuntime with ONLY records plus explicitly declared public package records
    verify/open all prospective records in check using native evidence verification

    return records
```

Do not access private Language caches reflectively or construct a replacement proof algorithm. `NativeRuntime.records`/`retain` are intentionally complete closure operations and cannot substitute for this worklist.

Verification in the producer context is insufficient: `verifyEvidence` inherits its provider and can conceal omitted auxiliaries. The fresh checker MUST NOT inherit producer state, validation facts or nonpublic evidence.

If a retained canonical owning proof itself contains private data that cannot be removed without changing the proof, this is a concrete representational conflict to report, not permission to redact a proof or omit it. ### 12.5 Logical obligation traversal and reuse

This edition introduces a separate obligation ledger; it does not change the old edition's `LogicalWork.validate/visit` algorithm or select behavior by broadening `finalGas()`. One attempt owns the ledger and meter. A chunk continuation copies both; an independent attempt or cold processor starts a new ledger. Failed fork work cannot publish facts or completion, even when its returned diagnostic reports gas already consumed.

The ledger key is `(contextual Recipe.key, obligation kind, coverage)`. Kinds are `container`, `definition`, and `value`; coverage identifies the complete selected contextual subtree for `value`, and the observed container/predicate/header set for `container`. Ancestor observations have their own keys. An unchanged BlueId under a different Recipe or coverage is a distinct obligation. Container/definition success never establishes a value key. Global Language/bridge caches do not affect this logical ledger.

The reference algorithm is:

```text
require(obligation):
    first require each enclosing container in outermost-to-innermost order
    if this exact obligation key succeeded in this invocation:
        charge validationProofReused once
        return its previously established obligation result
    dispatch by kind using the algorithms below
    record success only after the native check succeeds
```

For `container`, open each authored Recipe part through `LogicalWork.open` (which charges `nodeManifestOpened` once per exact ID per invocation), construct the unchanged native effective Head, and follow its applicable governing definitions with `definition` obligations. Each type edge followed charges `typeEdgeFollowed`; each explicitly selected ordinary child edge charges `objectMemberRead`, or `listItemRead` for an index. Charge `schemaPredicateEvaluated` once for each key of the effective constraints' `describe()` map, in sorted-key order. Perform the native required-container check and native effective predicate evaluation, subject only to the required-object presence lowering in §3.1: an effective object occurrence established present by native rules, with exactly the Boolean `required` constraint, discharges that predicate without incidental field counting while retaining its predicate charge. Empty effective constraints have zero predicate charges and no concrete-count walk. Incidental resolver/cache work inside the native predicate implementation is physical work, not a second logical traversal or a whole-subtree value charge. Predicate-driven widening invokes an explicit `value` obligation, whose own charges are separate; it cannot silently establish a value certificate from the container result.

For `definition`, traverse the exact definition evidence needed by native definition certification in deterministic native field/list order. Each distinct exact manifest opened is charged through the same invocation `LogicalWork.open`. Traversed ordinary fields charge `objectMemberRead`; items charge `listItemRead`; type edges charge `typeEdgeFollowed`. Deduplicate exact cycles within this definition traversal; do not regard a cycle visit as successful native certification. Then certify with goal `definition`. Do not evaluate a definition's declared minimum, maximum, enumeration or required-value constraints against the definition as if it were a value. Owning proofs use the native evidence verifier. Only successful native definition certification establishes this definition obligation.

For `value`, use an edition-specific traversal retaining the existing `LogicalWork.visit` scalar/list/object predicate accounting on the selected contextual Recipe, including its comparisons, text blocks, integer limbs, member examinations and pending value-proof keys. The old `carriedRoots` early return is disabled: a captured/portable source identity alone is not successful contextual value coverage. The old `previous` equality shortcut is likewise disabled unless the corresponding same-invocation contextual value obligation already succeeded. Do not call the old unmodified `visit` as the new reference algorithm. Its traversal is rooted at the selected Recipe, not the surrounding document. Then require both native strict selected evidence and `NativeRuntime.validate(selectedRecipe, context, "value")`. Publish the logical pending proof keys only after both checks succeed. A prior container or definition obligation does not enter that value-proof set. Do not pass an enclosing whole-root `previous` value to skip a changed contextual requirement; unchanged-subtree reuse requires the same contextual Recipe key and previously successful value coverage in this invocation.

In the new edition, establishing the identity of an explicit `Exact.Ref` reuses that reference's exact identifier. This identity-only case returns `local=false` and MUST NOT open the referenced body, rebuild it or charge identity hashing for that body, including when the reference appears as a part of local identity construction. It MUST NOT establish an `established` fact, a value certificate or successful contextual value coverage. Constructed local values retain their existing native identity construction and hash charges. A later required value read or owning-proof verification still establishes its own native obligations; an explicit reference is not evidence of its target's validity. This clarification does not alter legacy edition tariffs.

Handler ordering, BEX execution, patch construction/generalization, graph construction, emitted-event accounting and semantic exact identity construction retain their existing tariff operations. Replace only calls whose old purpose was whole-root validation with the declared obligation algorithm. Record preparation/serialization and fresh transport verification do not add independent semantic gas; exact identity construction already charged by the semantic operation is not charged again because an exporter chooses a different equivalent record encoding. No charge depends on whether a deferred child happens to be locally available.

Post-mutation checks observe enclosing containers afresh if their contextual Recipe changed, validate the changed value in its resulting context, and recheck native structural/lifetime invariants before finalization. {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Demand-scoped Contracts — conformance proposal and release gates

Companion to [normative design draft](contracts-demand-scoped-draft.md). Status: required cases proposed for a new immutable edition; no claim that current Java/reference algorithms pass. Old final-gas cases remain unchanged. These cases must be represented in the canonical executable reference and Java tests before publication is qualified.

## Comparison rules

A is the preserved old build/edition/packages/journal. B is the candidate build with exactly those old inputs. Compare complete observations, BlueIds, snapshots, receipts, scalar gas, checkpoints, terminal decisions and subsequent cold operations exactly.

C uses the candidate build and the same new exact input sources/publications across variants. Compare full/missing-unused content, inline/reference, warm/cold, embedded/standalone and same-edition participants exactly. Do not compare differing publication IDs between A and C as though they were the same document. Do not normalize gas, checkpoints or internal observation fields to obtain equality.

Each failure test must distinguish missing resources from invalid content and unsupported semantics. Fixture/setup failures are not evidence for the intended assertion. Keep the original signed bytes, target flags and source order.

## Native obligations and evidence

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS01 | Plain counter with original event Ref and unavailable unused historical operand | Normal new-edition process and export succeed; full/missing results and gas agree; ordinary full Language strict still requires that operand |
| DS02 | Exact native type discovery on an unused workflow whose step body is unavailable | Discover handler role/order without opening step body; selecting that handler later produces exact resource demand |
| DS03 | Conditional expression selects x; y body unavailable | x branch executes without fetching y; condition or contextual schema that actually requires y instead waits; no missing-to-false coercion |
| DS04 | Count constrained by parent `valueType`, typed field, inherited constraint and own schema | Standalone scalar certificate is insufficient; contextual valid value succeeds, invalid mutation fails, missing applicable definition waits |
| DS05 | `contracts` map schema `maxFields:0`; analogous list `itemType` and governing required fields | Invalid container rejected although every child would pass independently; constraints survive inline/reference representations |
| DS06 | Missing/invalid selected-node `specification`, type ancestry, labels, fixed values or merge metadata | Same native outcomes as complete contextual Language checks; no hand-written approximation or broad metadata omission |
| DS07 | Patch changes enclosing schema/type/valueType while child exact ID remains unchanged | Prior contextual success cannot be reused; new obligations fail/wait before exposing candidate to next step |
| DS08 | Same missing BlueId appears as unused historical target and current required operand | Historical identity observation succeeds; required role demands exact content; caches and delivery order do not alter result |
| DS09 | Ordinary event observer with selected metadata filter, nested filter and explicit private operand read | Native match/mismatch semantics preserved; required reads wait; ordinary observer not suppressed merely because operation routing skips |
| DS10 | Partial restore then full strict, warm repeated failure, cold restore, cache-pressure/reuse control | No partial fact is a full certificate; same logical decisions/gas and exact required IDs under all variants |

## Restore, atomicity and retention

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS11 | Tampered envelope/commitment/release/runtime/member key/edge/lifetime/protected marker | Restore rejects for the actual corruption, with state/evidence/cache rollback |
| DS12 | Checkpoint subtype adds constraints; timestamp is an exact scalar reference | Apply actual contextual constraints; selected scalar projection validates integer; no identity or persisted-byte rewrite |
| DS13 | Excluded private operand inline inside a retained ancestor vs ordinary reference | Same exact IDs and results; exported records contain no excluded private body; shallow serialization does not drop required evidence |
| DS14 | Genuine cyclic member and owning-set proof; altered proof/body; historical A(T)→B(T)→A(T−1) | Correct proof/body survives cold restore; invalid proof fails; no acyclic exact record emitted for a cyclic identity; history remains historical |
| DS15 | First patch installed/finalized, then BEX read needs unavailable exact resource | NEEDS returns original state/checkpoint, previous context/evidence/prepared output/archive/provenance; first mutation demonstrably occurred, not only a failed candidate |
| DS16 | Same process receives only required record and retries exact input/event/time | One successful effect, complete strict/full reference equality within new edition; repeat committed event follows actual reference idempotency behavior |
| DS17 | Real required-retention failure, plus explicit fault injection after APPLIED calculation | No capturable completion, archive/progress/effects or evidence from failed attempt; distinguish natural missing-resource repro from injected transaction test |
| DS18 | Scoped export alone into empty process, then real next operation | No parent test runtime/evidence leaks; required content demand and constraints reconstructed from exact records; original event Ref retained |

## Completion and integration

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS19 | Successful local new-edition outcome, capture complete owned unit, normal receive and dependent reaction | Actual provenance established after required retention; received state/effects correct without pretending source closure is fully certified |
| DS20 | Foreign issuer, copied descriptor, modified receipt/event/time/release/runtime, expired capability, partial unit or wrong predecessor | Existing integrity checks reject; an exact after-body alone does not establish execution |
| DS21 | Atomically committed local record, fresh worker CompletionReader, receive then next operation | Trusted local origin plus descriptor/commitment checks re-established; arbitrary imported snapshot cannot manufacture provenance |
| DS22 | Crash before/after content fetch and before/after durable publication | One journal transaction owns completed state/evidence/progress/effects; pending demand survives; no lost wake or duplicate effect |
| DS23 | Actual authorized provider supplies required content after wait | Native continuation succeeds; unauthorized/missing provider response remains waiting or denied under existing host rules; manual addEvidence alone is not acceptance evidence |
| DS24 | Same process alternates old/new accounts with shared package caches | A/B old results remain exact; new policy never contaminates old bindings/certificates; incompatible cross-edition document processing is not silently enabled |
| DS25 | New-edition actual typed Order with Activation, existing timelines, exact Order mandate | Seller/Partner embedded and Customer standalone equal at all stable prefixes, both operations and restart; no unnecessary Agreement-version fetch; normal completion/journal, not overlay |

DS25 additionally requires Coordination's separately specified Q06/Q13 cases: exact/nonexact/no target, stale/future/foreign, incomplete own history, ordinary observer, child birth/prebirth/ties, initialized attach/rebase and historical cycles. Contracts-only PASS does not discharge those cases. Agent absent, Agreement-only, revoked and temporarily missing required proof are distinct cases; admission is not business execution.

## Experimental evidence and migration of assertions

The preserved run97407 demonstrates DS15/DS16 only for an isolated fixed two-step counter. It records assigned/finalized count2, NEEDS for the actual private record, rollback to count1, one-record retry and exact strict observations/gas708; repeat committed event gas160 matches strict reference. Run85630 adds repeated overflow/replay/capture refusal within that restricted overlay. Run51631 validates the plain profile after the shared compiler change. None establishes new-edition completion or signed Order integration.

Keep these artifacts and old tests unchanged as historical evidence. Port their assertions into normal edition-selected Java tests. The new normal completion tests expect established capture; historical overlay tests continue to expect `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION`. Do not reinterpret them as the same API guarantee.

## Publication gate

Before changing canonical package selection or generating a candidate publication:

1. Resolve D1–D5 in the design draft and inventory the actual native handler primitives.
2. Integrate the prose and obligation algorithms into a complete new specification with executable reference routines; reconcile every inherited full-certification/closure call explicitly.
3. Give restore/event/patch/finish/retain/export/cold/receive equivalent implementations and meaningful negative cases, not only YAML changes.
4. Build exact IDs using repository tooling, preserve old archives, then bind the candidate runtime to those generated identities.
5. Record which cases are PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or BLOCKED with exact source/publication IDs. Missing tests are not implicit passes.
6. Qualify A/B and C separately, including actual network/provider and journal restart; then enable the qualified new binding only for new registrations.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Native runtime contract

The exact package, protocol, rules and exports are pinned in
`integration-selection.json`. Native MyOS enables this publication in its
agreements and mandates profiles; the standard profile remains unsupported.

| Export | Contracts role | Body fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timer Channel | external-channel | none |
| Schedule Timer | step | request |
| Cancel Timer | step | request |

Steps evaluate `request` once with the ordinary BEX call/event/document/steps frame
and the same invocation meter. Effectful expressions, explicit types, missing
fields and unknown fields fail. The resulting typed request is an ordinary staged
event. Direct Trigger Event and Compute emissions follow the same commit path.

The committed event occurrence identifies a registration. Registration, keyed
replacement/cancellation, source state and wake-up index commit in one conditional
journal publication. A firing's resulting document, receipt and terminal timer
status also commit together. Worker leases recover abandoned attempts; replays
cannot create an extra committed firing.

The virtual Timer Source is scoped by engine context and stable initial document
identity. Its immutable Timer Entry stores source, deadline and exact Timer Fired
message. Receipts retain the entry; Contracts processes the message at the deadline.
The native Time adapter extends receipt/history input validation only for this
approved exact type. Signed Timeline rules are unchanged.

Every pending entry participates in ordinary input selection immediately. A clock
alarm only wakes the owner. Selection uses the common three-part order, current
sources, existing dependency readiness and SCC ownership. Pending child timers
prevent parents from advancing through their position. Receiving a child's
completion does not register its emitted requests again in the parent.

MyOS advances only its own timeline providers' signed closed prefixes. It serializes
that advance with admission and caps it before any prepared, unpublished entry.
External sources must provide their own proof. `completeBefore > deadline` is
required, including all ties. Host time is used for eligibility, never as a
replacement for logical event time. There is no independent EventBridge schedule
per timer and no AWS resource created per timer.

The host wakes due timers on a 100 ms scan; unavailable prerequisites retry with a
250 ms minimum alarm delay. Per-document and per-account token buckets prevent
one self-rescheduling document monopolizing workers (10 and 100 firings/second,
with bursts of 16 and 100). Pending defaults are 1,024 per document and 16,384 per
account/profile, configurable with `blue.time.maxPendingPerDocument` and
`blue.time.maxPendingPerAccount`. These are host admission/resource policies,
not a minimum logical timer interval. Over-limit attempts roll back atomically.
Restarting a process resets rate-limit bursts but not durable timer state.

`GET /documents/{sessionId}/timers` returns pending registrations, requested
microsecond timestamps, immutable entry/message/source IDs and channel generation.
Cancellation is a document operation, not an administrative timer-delete API.
Paused documents retain their timers and resume in logical order. Removed channel
generations invalidate timers. Detaching an independently managed document does not.

Adding these exact runtime bindings does not reinterpret old binding semantics.
Existing saved snapshots remain readable; introducing Time attaches the new
bindings. The engine release marker is advanced so old binaries reject a journal
containing this new input format instead of silently ignoring it.
"}

ESDxi9qNrWrZXChcdcenhHmPY5UPCJXtwihEvTBC.text: {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts 1.0 **Edition:** `blue-contracts/2026-10-07-gas-10m-1` **Normative form:** one complete specification with executable algorithm appendices ## Abstract Blue Contracts defines deterministic, gas-bounded transitions over exact Blue documents. It specifies channels, operation selection, sequential workflows, local updates, child-first managed composition, cyclic component rounds, initialization, atomic failure, replay and completion reuse. Effects are published only after a complete successful transition. ## Contents - [1. Scope and conformance](#scope) - [2. Exact dependencies and interpretation](#dependencies) - [3. Scope and central rule](#section-3) - [4. Public API, outcomes and document representation](#section-4) - [5. Exact graph and occurrence records](#section-5) - [6. Standard categories and complete type catalogue](#section-6) - [7. Actual-value filtering](#section-7) - [8. One selected operation call](#section-8) - [9. External channel acceptance, lifetimes and checkpoints](#section-9) - [10. Deterministic completion machine](#section-10) - [11. Nested steps and BEX effects](#section-11) - [12. Patches, validation and local Document Updates](#section-12) - [13. Local FIFO, output batches and lifecycle](#section-13) - [14. Dynamic graphs, collections, shared members and cycles](#section-14) - [15. Generalization and explicit valid retyping](#section-15) - [16. Lazy content and installed runtime extensions](#section-16) - [17. Logical gas and host-independent resource semantics](#section-17) - [18. Atomicity, replay and chunking equivalence](#section-18) - [19. Conformance and integration](#section-19) - [20. Normative algorithms and provenance](#section-20) - [21. Generic Coordination integration boundary](#section-21) - [22. Lazy immutable host values](#section-22) - [23. Exact-value transfer accounting](#section-23) - [24. Selected descendant evidence](#section-24) - [Appendix A. Complete transition model](#transitions) - [Appendix B. Logical metering and schedule](#metering) - [Appendix C. Complete executable algorithms](#algorithms) ## 1. Scope and conformance This specification defines the protocol identified by this edition. Its prose, tables and algorithm appendices form one normative contract. It is independent of source-repository branches, release tags, installation paths and prior discussions. Named external semantics are selected exactly in §2. Where an implementation uses another programming language, it MUST preserve the same specified observations; matching internal classes or diagnostic wording is not required unless explicitly identified as an observation. **MUST** and **REQUIRED** express requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** express prohibitions. **SHOULD** and **SHOULD NOT** express recommendations whose departures require understood consequences. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** express permissions. Examples marked informative do not add requirements. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a defect, not permission to choose an outcome. A finite conformance corpus is evidence, not a proof for every possible input. A package distributes this specification; it does not install a processor. The package's BlueId, this specification Text's BlueId and the OCI/archive digests identify different content. This document does not contain its own calculated identity or the generated identities of types that refer to it. ## 2. Exact dependencies and interpretation This edition selects Blue Language package `8XGYNufx24r7Dc5bGoeobcGNCn9roLzSfZCQyHBTaTx4` and its complete specification Text `H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQmWnc`. Language is a direct prerequisite: document admission, effective types, specialization, exact references, specification metadata, cyclic identities and BlueIds use its defined operations. This edition requires Blue BEX package `6m7CxeDA9F74LyfU1H5zYGmo6ozXr4zJFbh7j6F6QJ7a`, protocol specification `H4bhWaD45C4MbrWYgj3Z6kXY9NoBa6gYms9mnbRMyta7`, and normative rules Text `7m8k8P8b8Kn2jHF96EQogWTpsouytXmDFQ3qdmWdY5A3`. Every BEX-bearing position in an invocation uses that evaluator contract and the host interfaces defined here. Selecting another package or operator table MUST NOT substitute another BEX mode. BEX values and proposed effects are not automatically admitted Blue values; the output boundaries below are mandatory. Coordination is not a prerequisite of Contracts. A higher-level host may establish external ordering, authority and durable histories; it supplies the original accepted event and timestamp through the public transition defined here. Contracts does not query a timeline provider or assign actor authority on its own. Package imports supply exact content. Authoring prefixes are local bindings and do not leak through transitive imports. An imported definition retains its exact references. Mounting another package cannot change the selected interpreter or replace an existing type reference. Within this edition's interpreted package graph, the selected Language release MUST agree throughout; cross-Language conversion and mixed-rule cyclic sets are not defined. One selected Language governs a complete cyclic identity set and its owning proof. ## 3. Scope and central rule **C01.** The public transition remains: ```text process(document, event, eventTimestamp) -> resulting document, emitted events, gas ``` `document` is the selected exact root and its required managed graph. The event is one complete original external Blue value. Time is supplied as integer microseconds. A successful attempt finishes required initialization, local turns, child-batch applications, cyclic feedback and exact finalization. All returned changes remain one atomic result. **Completion boundary.** Within a document, updates are immediate and application events are queued. Across a managed boundary, only a **sealed completion** is observable. A sealed completion contains the source's completed document/view and its ordered output occurrences. It is not necessarily durably committed. A child producing no events still supplies its resulting state. No standalone channel parameter, delivery-list ingress, payload selector or alternate request selector is introduced. The chunk protocol in the annex is a processor-internal decomposition of this same transition; a completion is not an external event and cannot invoke an operation by masquerading as one. **C02.** Contracts defines all processing described here, including child incorporation and cycle turns. Obtaining, ordering and authorizing external inputs, worker ownership, persistent-history scheduling, billing and external delivery are outside this specification. **C03.** Language retains sole authority for Source, exact content, identities, resolution, cyclic sets and type validity. BEX retains its evaluation, numbers, functions, bindings and effect accumulation. Contracts chooses views and applies effects. Missing exact evidence is not an empty object or an ordinary filter mismatch. ## 4. Public API, outcomes and document representation ### 2.1 Three inputs The Python-compatible public API remains `Processor.process(document, event, eventTimestamp)`. Its bound method has exactly these three parameters. Processor construction configures the exact runtime registry, resolver, gas ceiling and optional member-local ceilings; those are fixed execution configuration rather than extra per-event routing arguments. `document` can be a verified `Snapshot`, the SDK representation of the selected exact rooted document, or a fresh Source object. The latter is admitted and initialized within the attempt. It is not permissible to author protected processor markers in a fresh Source object. Use verified snapshot restoration for an already managed document. The required SDK-compatible returned `Outcome.document` is the resulting `Snapshot`. Its selected root BlueId is `result.document.documents[result.document.root].blue_id`. `processor.read(result.document, path)` reads business content. `Outcome.emitted_events` contains exact references to the selected root's publicly emitted values. `processor.emitted(result)` opens those values for display. Tuple unpacking yields `(document, emitted_events, gas)` in the order in C01; the `Outcome` additionally carries diagnostics and replay evidence. These SDK records do not add inputs to the Contracts transition. Optional `begin / next_chunk / execute_chunk / accept_chunk / finish` methods implement the internal protocol in the executable appendix; they do not publish partial state or add another external ingress. A storage host may use a different representation if it preserves the same exact content, managed-occurrence evidence and semantics. ### 2.2 Time and identities **C04.** `eventTimestamp` MUST be an integer from 0 through 2^53−1, in microseconds. Booleans, floating-point values, strings, negative numbers and out-of-range integers are rejected. Contracts never substitutes a wall clock or an event field for this argument. This range preserves the defined's portable timestamp representation; BEX Integer arithmetic is not narrowed by it. The original event's identity is established with the unchanged validated Language operations. Selection of an inner call does not alter this identity. Equal timestamps do not imply equal events. No timestamp-only external ordering relation is inferred. ### 2.3 Result states | Status | Document and public events | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `APPLIED` | Complete resulting state and selected-root emissions | The attempt can commit, including graceful termination. | | `FAILED` | Original input snapshot; no public events | Invalid call, invalid effect, validation failure, explicit BEX failure, unsupported demanded executable or another defined Contracts error. | | `GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Original input snapshot; no public events | The next logical charge exceeds the shared or owner-local remaining allowance. The admitted prefix and rejected charge are reported. | | `NEEDS_RESOURCES` | Original input snapshot; no public events | Required exact content or managed-view evidence is unavailable. This suspended attempt reports no completed semantic gas ledger; rerun from the original inputs after evidence is supplied. | | `TERMINATED` | Original input snapshot; no public events | The selected root was already legitimately terminated. | Invalid SDK arguments, invalid fresh Source admission and invalid configuration may raise `ContractError` before a runnable attempt exists. Cyclic units A unit has a pending inbox per member, a consumed seed/init set, a turn serial per member, a coherent last sealed component view, and buffered external output. ```text RUN_CYCLIC_UNIT(U): repeat: charge componentRoundOpened before the round; no independent round-count ceiling V := immutable coherent view of U's last completed round inputs := snapshot pending per-member batches and remaining seed/init work clear only those pending items included in inputs results := [] for member in U.members in key order: if member has eligible inputs: results += RUN_LOCAL(input using V for all peer reads) merge each result's OWNED member changes into V reconcile member edge declarations and retire invalid generations use Language to finalize ACTUAL resulting cyclic components validate the resulting coherent component; create immutable RoundSeal # RoundSeal maps local after-views to the exact finalized member vector retain output per source in round/member/turn/local-ordinal order route each new output batch to surviving captured intra-unit tickets place those batches, each bound to RoundSeal, in NEXT-round inboxes # never invoke this round's peer callbacks absorb topology joins and pending initialization via A08/A09 until no pending batch, initialization or external seed remains expose one UnitCompletion to outside containers ``` A member without work does not rerun its external operation merely because a peer changed state. At the next round, peers see the just sealed V'. This is deterministic even if turn calculations are physically parallel; logical acceptance/metering remains member-key ordered. A split keeps U's execution group until quiescence, but finalizes identities under the actual split graph. New joins are handled below. No special wave, epoch or host scheduling concept is part of this algorithm. ### A08. Initialization and dynamic creation barrier For initial initialization, build dependency units and capture all discovered uninitialized member references before any initialization writes or descendant refreshes. Initialized members are carried, not reinitialized. A03 lifecycle dispatch happens once per new activation. Cyclic initialization uses A07's round-0 lifecycle work and subsequent local-event feedback. For a child created by an in-progress parent patch: 1. Record its exact creation body, new occurrence generation and creation cause. Do not invent an external input or checkpoint. `created during this attempt` alone does not change Language admission rules. 2. Discover its uninitialized dependency closure. Distinguish new members from existing initialized members and ancestors already initializing. The latter are **read-only pins to their last sealed/pre-initialization exact views**, not recursive initialization requests. 3. Initialize the new-only closure dependency-first; use rounds for SCCs among the new members. Capture all such members' pre-initialization IDs once. A back-reference to the suspended creator reads its sealed pre-turn view, never its private patched body. Mark any resulting live join for A09 rather than recursively entering the creator. 4. Seal the newly initialized members and supply their completed states to the suspended creator. Queue all eligible direct-child initialization outputs as complete batches behind existing queue items. Do not drain the creator's queue inside its current handler; local Document Update continuations still run at A06's boundary. 5. Resume the creator's patch/handler. Its next normal step sees the child initialized. It cannot seal upward until this barrier and its own work are complete. 6. When the creator seals, activate the pending live bindings coherently and recompute units. A cyclic join uses the completed creator view and retained child result; internal messages already delivered during the barrier are not redelivered. Remaining feedback becomes subsequent group-round work. If evidence is missing, fail/suspend the whole attempt under A10 rather than expose an incomplete child. The same deterministic gas ledger applies to this process. Any physical allocation/work interruption remains an incomplete attempt, not a child-initialization rejection. A child later removed by its creator can have consumed calculation gas without surviving in the resulting active graph. ### A09. Topology changes, unit promotion and route capture Maintain monotonically increasing member-activation and edge-generation counters as in the defined. Whenever a declared edge changes, retire the previous occurrence and allocate the next generation in deterministic source/path order. Keep retired records for evidence without treating their inventory as active processing work. There is no universal active-graph capacity ceiling. **Route capture:** for original phase work, capture the source's incoming edge tickets from the coherent phase-start graph. For newly initialized children, capture the newly active direct tickets at the creation barrier. A later edge never acquires source events already emitted/sealed before it existed. A continuing source's subsequent turn captures then-current tickets. Source output values themselves contain no route paths. A split changes actual edges/identities but not the current execution-unit union. At the next input start there is no sticky grouping from the previous attempt. Previously sealed source turns remain valid completed turns. A merge does not replay their operation or undo past local observation. It changes which further work is internal before the unit may expose its **final** result outside. If a receiving member already ran in this attempt, new eligible incoming work creates a new reaction turn with no repeated external seed; its accumulated output retains the prior turn order. A unit may not seal outward while it has a pending dependency that can still supply required work. A whole-root result waits for all required units even if a chunk finished earlier. This is why arbitrary database task completion is not the chunk-ready predicate. ### A10. Atomic failure and finalization Keep the original input snapshot immutable. APPLIED alone authorizes publication of the full attempt result. Any invalid request, patch, received completion, identity, protected state, callback or final containing constraint rolls back every tentative frame/completion/marker/output in the attempt. Deterministic gas exhaustion has its existing exact rollback and rejected-charge behavior. A physical resource/cancellation exception abandons the tentative attempt without constructing a canonical semantic failure. For GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED preserve admitted rows and the first rejected charge, not speculative suffix work. For NEEDS_RESOURCES preserve the original state and the defined missing-resource disposition; do not invent a completed gas receipt or a successful prefix. A physical cancellation is not a fabricated protocol gas error. Propagate a typed incomplete/host condition through every callback, Language bridge, BEX boundary, chunk driver and receiving adapter; do not let a broad exception wrapper turn it into invalid evidence or invalid input. No terminal result, input-disposition or checkpoint is issued from the unfinished attempt. Finalization uses only sealed owned states. Substitute current verified member-local edges, run the real Language cyclic-set finalizer, retain owning-set proofs, rebuild outside references dependency-first, validate every affected context, and write invocation revision/topology generation once. No finalizer invokes business update/event handlers. Root projection records only root-origin occurrences; other completions remain internal result evidence. A source turn calculated earlier can remain retained as non-authoritative immutable evidence after a larger attempt fails; its mere existence does not change the returned original state or commit any effect. A separate earlier successful standalone call has its own atomic boundary and is not rolled back by an unrelated later call. ### A11. Chunked execution and the equivalence argument The optional chunk driver is: ```text begin(document, event, time) -> opaque Attempt next_chunk(Attempt) -> verified ChunkToken | no-more-work execute_chunk(ChunkToken) -> sealed candidate completion accept_chunk(Attempt, ChunkToken, completion) -> updated private Attempt finish(Attempt) -> the same public Outcome as PROCESS ``` This is not a second public event format. `next_chunk` chooses exactly the ready unit/turn/round prescribed above; it supplies frozen local seeds and dependency views, not a caller-selected external delivery list. `accept_chunk` checks the one-use token, exact inputs, profile, result capability, occurrence lifetimes and logical work prefix. Duplicate acceptance cannot duplicate effects or charges. `finish` rejects unfinished attempts. An acyclic subgraph may be calculated in a separate process and transported as exact completed data when all token bindings remain the same. Parent-independent semantic payloads are final state and own output. Binding metadata, initial exact view and metering evidence prevent stale/forged substitution. A root-level standalone Outcome is not accepted blindly as a local completion: its setup/root projection and snapshot-root commitments differ and must be normalized through the supported extraction/verification path. **Induction for a static DAG:** leaves execute identical local turns; therefore their state/output pairs agree. Given identical completed dependencies, their container installs the same states, prequeues the same occurrences, executes the same BEX and handlers against the same views, and seals the same result. Induct to the root. Every logical charge is accepted in the same normal-form sequence, yielding identical successful and failing prefixes. There is no parent callback into an unfinished source frame, so an interleaving cannot invalidate the substitution. **Cycles:** induct over A07 rounds instead of graph depth. Each round begins with the same component vector and inboxes, runs identical local turns and finalizes the same exact component. Stop or fail on the same boundary. The component, not an individual cyclic member, is the independently completed external chunk. **Dynamic graphs:** chunk acceptance follows A08/A09. A join can invalidate a formerly independent cut. Preserve completed turns and promote the remaining work; never force a precomputed stale partition to finish as if topology had not changed. Equivalence covers identical execution of this state machine, not arbitrary regrouping that changes its semantic turns. A native implementation can use a single heap, an explicit continuation object, serialization between chunks, or verified computation reuse. It must have no visibility into another member's unsealed frame and must preserve the logical trace. Parallel wall-clock completion order is ignored. ### A12. Every local work segment has relative ordinals, stable owner keys and an input logical-proof prefix. On chunk acceptance, validate and append that same segment in the canonical order; physical completion order is irrelevant. A cached segment with a different logical proof inventory, dependency context, profile, seed selection or budget-prefix semantics cannot be copied unchanged. Re-execute the local kernel or derive/verify its exact normal-form work through the implementation's supported equivalent path. It is never sufficient to set gas to the cache lookup cost. A previously admitted segment cannot merge twice for the same logical chunk; distinct receiving occurrences still have their own application costs. Retain the defined rejected-charge behavior: stop before the first work item that exceeds shared or owner-local remaining gas, return its exact rejected charge, and expose no state/output. Speculative work beyond that point is physical diagnostic work only. Do not execute an unbounded speculative callback merely to discover a ledger. It must follow the declared live or verifiable work-ledger contract; the 10,000,000 shared ceiling is not reset for it. Physical interruption abandons speculation and is not a semantic rejection. Consequently: ```text gas(rooted attempt) = gas(chunked execution of that attempt) ``` but not necessarily: ```text gas(standalone B call) + gas(standalone A call) ``` The latter contains repeated top-level setup/root projection and can be a different declared atomic context. Use the shared attempt driver for exact total/rejected-prefix comparisons. ### Required gas qualification Run direct/chunk differential cases at ample gas, exact-success allowance, one unit below it, and restrictive member-local ceilings. Compare ordered rows, admitted total, first rejection, owner attribution, state and public output. Include zero-event state propagation, duplicate paths, cold storage, callbacks, cyclic rounds, initialization, late failure and a retired receipt. {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Qualification

The executable tests are in the MyOS checkout. `./blue-package test` runs them.
The package's preserved 0.1 Python fixture is historical evidence only. No current
Python-native implementation or cross-language parity is claimed.

`CoordinationTimeTest` exercises strict deadlines, exact logical timestamps,
keyed replacement/cancellation, equal-time common ordering, trusted inclusive
completeness, late earlier cancellation, rollback, pause/resume, removed channel
generations, multiple simultaneous timers, forged Timeline payloads, failed and
unmatched terminal inputs, child propagation, dependent operations, and cycles
that later split.

`TimeIntegrationTest` exercises real-clock idle timelines and SQLite process death
before/after registration and before/after firing commits. The subprocess is halted,
not cleanly shut down. On reopening, both transitions must occur exactly once and
retain their original requested timestamp differences.

MyOS uses the same conditional publication interface for SQLite and DynamoDB.
Live AWS verification exercises its DynamoDB journal. Local kill-window testing
is SQLite-specific; it is not proof of every possible infrastructure outage.
Host overload can delay observation. Safety requires trustworthy clock and source
completeness, as it does for the selected Coordination profile. Arbitrary dynamic
topologies and cross-language parity are not exhaustively proven by this suite.
"}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Language

Blue Language defines immutable typed content graphs, exact BlueIds, specialization, schemas, reusable packages, and references to additional protocol semantics.

## Read the specification

`SPECIFICATION.md` is the complete normative document for Blue Language 1.0, edition `blue-language/2026-09-26-specification-metadata-1`. It includes the core registry, ordinary Package and Protocol Specification definitions, and complete executable algorithms. No separate Blue specification is needed to determine this edition's Language rules.

`SPECIFICATION.html` in the source workspace is a generated reading view of the same Markdown. The Markdown is the identified normative Text. In the data-only `.bluepkg` artifact, read `spec/language.md`; it contains exactly the same document.

## Contents

- `types/` contains the six core registry bodies and the two ordinary standard definitions. Package and Protocol Specification are the package's two named exports; core names are established by the Language registry itself.
- `conformance/` contains unchanged portable Language cases and additional release checks.
- `dist/` contains the built package archive, exact package root, records, and manifest. Its `spec/language.md` is byte-identical to the source `SPECIFICATION.md`; `docs/types/` contains the same type sources. Archive conformance JSON arrays preserve the original case objects from the source JSONL files.
- `reference/python/` preserves the selected Python implementation and the support resources it imports. Those source copies are implementation evidence; older prose files retained inside that snapshot are not additional normative documents for this publication.
- `tools/` contains a local publisher and verifier. It performs no remote publication.
- `verification/` records the scope and results of the actual checks for this delivery.

## Local use

The commands below run from this source workspace, not from the unpacked data-only artifact. Python 3.13 or newer is required. The reference includes its YAML reader. Running the metadata regression tests also requires pytest.

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package inspect
./blue-package test
python3.13 examples/use_package.py
```

A deliberate package build is:

```sh
./blue-package build
```

Normal verification and testing do not update pins, regenerate expected results, or change any referenced implementation source. Package acquisition is independent of Language interpretation; this project does not contact a registry.

## Identity and versioning

The package has a BlueId calculated under the selected Language. Archive and file checksums are separate integrity identifiers. This complete publication has a new package identity; it does not automatically replace the Language package referenced by existing BEX, Contracts, Coordination, or application packages.

Published definitions retain their exact IDs. The eight supplied registry/standard definitions and the executable Language algorithms are unchanged from the selected reference. Adoption by a dependent package is an explicit new dependency selection, not an identity rewrite.

This edition defines no automatic cross-Language import or cycle conversion. One selected interpretation governs an entire cyclic identity set and its proof. Compatible behavior, if introduced by a later Language edition, must be specified by that edition; no compatibility registry or version-range resolver is required here.

## Publication

The package can be retained locally or distributed through any file or artifact service. `dist/package.bluepkg` is the data artifact. GitHub and OCI are optional distribution infrastructure, not authorities that assign its BlueId. Nothing in this delivery has been published to an external registry.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue BEX

BEX evaluates explicit inputs into a value, ordered proposed changes and events,
and a deterministic admitted gas total. It does not apply document changes.

## Final gas edition

`1.0.0-final-gas.1` checks each charge before work and accumulates scalar gas.
Results have `value`, `changeset`, `events` and `gas_used`; accepted-charge rows
and `gas_trace` are not part of this edition. The default standalone allowance
remains 10,000,000. A supplied shared meter is never reset. Local and shared caps
retain their rejection order and one compact first-rejected-charge diagnostic.
A meter that has rejected work cannot resume accepting charges.

`SPECIFICATION.md` and `spec/bex-final-gas.md` contain the identical complete
normative text and six executable modules. The exact overrides and hashes are
listed in `docs/sources.json`. The earlier specification remains in `spec/bex.md`
and the frozen references remain unchanged for historical qualification.

This is a new exact protocol identity. Hosts must retain the old edition when
replaying old histories. Loading package data does not install an evaluator or
authorize an intrinsic. Optional debug traces are noncanonical and off by default.

## Local verification

With Python 3.13+, pytest, PyYAML, Java 21 and `BLUE_JAVA_CLASSPATH` pointing to
the qualified native Language runtime:

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package test
python ../tools/build_final_gas.py blue-bex --check
```

The new-edition tests execute the finite conformance vectors and cover shared
meters, exact budgets, rejection and the absence of charge history. Historical
reference tests must run against their original frozen edition. Passing a finite
corpus does not establish universal conformance; see `QUALIFICATION.md`.
"}

H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQ.text: {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Language 1.0 ## Specification — 26 September 2026 **Edition:** `blue-language/2026-09-26-specification-metadata-1` **Publication:** complete specification, including standard definitions and normative algorithms ### Abstract Blue is a language for immutable, content-addressed graphs. Its nodes describe values, reusable definitions, constraints, and references to other nodes. A node may be used as a type: it contributes compatible structure and requirements without losing the identity of either the type or its instance. A BlueId identifies exact content, not a mutable name, a location, or a resolved interpretation. This specification defines the node model, portable input representations, exact identity, specialization, schemas, list construction, graph access, validation, specification metadata, and the standard package model. It also defines how a processor associates additional meaning with identified specifications. Particular workflow, coordination, rendering, query, and other application protocols define their own behavior; installing their content does not install an implementation. ### Status and authority This document is the complete normative definition of this edition. Its prose, tables, standard definitions, and normative algorithm annex form one contract. No separate Blue document, source-repository branch, release tag, implementation guide, or project discussion supplies an unstated rule. Examples marked informative illustrate the rules and do not extend them. A conformance claim identifies this edition and the implemented role. Publishing this document or a package containing it does not certify an implementation. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a specification defect; it is not permission to choose a convenient interpretation or regenerate expected results. ### Requirement terms **MUST** and **REQUIRED** state absolute requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** state absolute prohibitions. **SHOULD** states a recommendation that may be departed from only after understanding and documenting the consequences. **SHOULD NOT** recommends against a practice under the same condition. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** indicate permitted alternatives. Requirements expressed with these terms apply only to the role and operation being specified. ### Contents - [1. Scope, conformance roles, and interpretation](#scope) - [2. Nodes, graphs and operation roles](#model) - [3. Serialization, scalar codecs and empty content](#parsing) - [4. Exact normalization and BlueId](#identity) - [5. References, verified graph access and materialization](#graph) - [6. Types, specialization and validation goals](#types) - [7. Schemas: predicates, narrowing and conjunction](#schemas) - [8. Lists and specialization](#lists) - [9. Preprocessing and Source preparation](#preprocessing) - [10. Complete and selected resolution](#resolution) - [11. Validated creation, canonical authoring, minimization and export](#admission) - [12. Cyclic identities and owning-set proofs](#cycles) - [13. Diagnostics and safe operation boundaries](#diagnostics) - [14. Conformance and operation equivalence](#conformance) - [15. Worked examples — informative](#worked-examples) - [16. Authoring bindings and exact content availability](#authoring-bindings) - [17. Specification metadata](#specification-metadata) - [18. Standard packages and protocol descriptors](#packages) - [19. Edition selection and cyclic identity boundaries](#edition-boundaries) - [20. Protocol interpretation and document processors](#processors) - [Appendix A. Algorithm notation and primitive operations](#notation) - [Appendix B. Exact registry and preprocessing selectors](#registry) - [Appendix C. Ordinary standard definitions](#standard-definitions) - [Appendix D. Complete normative algorithms](#algorithms) - [Appendix E. Portable conformance-request protocol](#fixture-protocol) - [Appendix F. Exact repository carrier](#repository-carrier) ## 1. Scope, conformance roles, and interpretation ### 1.1 Content model Blue represents information as a graph of immutable typed nodes. A document is one root together with the portion of the graph presently materialized. Types are themselves nodes. Using a node as a type contributes requirements, fixed content, and compatible structure to the instance. Language operations establish exact content, its identity, or specific conclusions about its meaning. They do not grant authority or perform external business actions. This edition defines no workflow scheduler, transaction coordinator, network service, database layout, or portable execution gas tariff. **LANG-SCOPE.** An implementation MUST apply the structural Language rules to all reserved fields, including `contracts`, without inferring execution behavior from the field name. Application protocols MUST NOT change the Language rules used to parse, identify, or resolve content in an established interpretation context. ### 1.2 Conformance roles A **Language implementation** provides the content and operation semantics defined in this document. A **package processor** additionally constructs, verifies, or mounts packages according to §18. A **protocol processor** performs a stated task under additional identified protocol rules, according to §20. A single program may perform several roles; a reader may perform only the Language role. **LANG-AUTHORITY.** Full Language conformance requires the operation contracts in this document, not only structural hashing. An implementation MAY organize its APIs, records, storage, caches, and algorithms differently, provided that it preserves the required observations, identities, proof obligations, and failure distinctions. A subset implementation MUST identify its supported subset and MUST NOT advertise omitted behavior as supported. The executable notation in Appendix D specifies complete Blue-specific procedures. Python allocation, private attributes, diagnostic English, and reference cache layout are not required interfaces. The selected mathematical and serialization behavior is required. The six core registry bodies in Appendix B are exact content; they are not illustrative substitutes. ### 1.3 Selecting Language An **interpretation context** fixes the Language edition, core registry, input role, explicitly selected authoring bindings, and the evidence and resource controls available to an operation. The Language selection is established before processing identity-bearing content. An ordinary `type` reference or a document's `specification` metadata does not retroactively choose a different parser, identity algorithm, or registry. **LANG-VERSION.** All steps of one identity, resolution, or admission calculation MUST use one coherent selection of Language rules. A content address MUST NOT be reassigned to different exact content. Retained content and validation evidence MUST NOT be silently reinterpreted under a different edition. Compatibility and cyclic identity boundaries are specified in §19. A bootstrap Language package identifies its selected rules and standard definitions; it is verified by an implementation already able to interpret those rules. It does not install or derive that implementation. Its own identifier is not embedded into the content from which that same identifier is calculated. ### 1.4 Exact identity, availability, and trust An identifier and a body are different kinds of evidence. A correct identifier identifies content. It neither makes the content available nor establishes its author's authority. A correctly identified body is not necessarily a valid completed value or a supported protocol. Admission and support assertions MUST distinguish these claims.
