Registry addresses, source paths, release labels, timestamps, and display aliases are not alternative BlueIds. An established provider result is interpreted only in the role and context under which its content can be verified. --- ## 2. Nodes, graphs and operation roles ### Purpose Separate **what a node contains**, **how it is represented**, and **what an operation proves**. These distinctions determine whether two inputs should have the same identity and whether successful hashing is enough to admit a document. ### 2.1 Exact content and an effective view An exact node has its own fields, literal metadata, scalar payload or list elements. Its effective view additionally applies the inherited declarations and compatible constraints relevant to that node. Resolution retains the exact origin; it does not overwrite that origin with its view. **LANG-EXACT-VIEW.** Two distinct exact nodes MAY resolve to identical effective views. An implementation MUST NOT infer identity equality from that observation alone, or recover a lost exact origin by guessing from a bare resolved view. The ordinary hasher identifies exact content, not a resolver object. For example, Text PLN and Currency PLN retain different own type edges. An enclosing Holder declaration may interpret either as Currency PLN. Their exact child identities remain different. All five complete instance inputs appear in §15. ### 2.2 A reference is not an overlay A pure reference has exactly one member: ```yaml blueId: GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC ``` The same object with a sibling, even a null sibling, is invalid. To specialize a referenced node, place the reference under `type` and supply instance fields outside it. Expansion reveals an existing node; specialization creates a new, more constrained node. **LANG-REFERENCE.** A reference and its verified exact materialization denote the same node. At a complete node-valued position, replacing one with the other MUST preserve exact identity. A semantic operation MUST NOT expose the reference wrapper as an ordinary `blueId` field. Its conclusions depend on the selected operation and verified content, not expansion state. A reference to a compiled list result is exact content. It is not a reusable Source instruction that should be executed at its new location. Representation equivalence applies to a node and its exact representation, not to an unevaluated constructor expression and an unrelated exact operand. ### 2.3 The node model A materialized node contains reserved metadata and at most one primary payload. Scalars use `value`; lists use `items`; objects use direct ordinary child fields. A metadata-only node may have no payload. The empty map `{}` is a present empty object, not a missing declaration. Bare objects do not acquire a Dictionary type, and bare lists do not acquire a List type, merely through normalization. **LANG-NODE-SHAPE.** A node MUST NOT combine scalar, list and ordinary-object payloads. The reserved-invalid fields `properties` and `constraints` MUST be rejected. Ordinary keys colliding with reserved fields cannot be represented directly as application map keys; an application-defined escaped structure is required. | Field | Role and permitted shape | Identity contribution | |---|---|---| | `name`, `description` | Literal Unicode string | Literal string | | `specification` | Complete reference-valued metadata; explicit node in Source, exact reference after preparation; see §17 | Exact target identity | | `type`, `itemType`, `keyType`, `valueType` | Complete node; Source alias before preprocessing; exact reference afterward | Exact defining-node identity | | `value` | Scalar literal, never an object or sequence | Own-type encoded literal | | `items` | Sequence slot, not a separately replaceable node slot | Ordered payload-list identity | | `blueId` | Final identifier, exclusively in a pure reference | The identifier itself | | `blue` | Source-root preprocessing configuration only | Absent from the resulting content | | `schema` | Exact node interpreted using §7 | Exact child identity | | `mergePolicy` | Literal `positional` or `append-only` | Identity of the corresponding core Text scalar | | `contracts` | Exact node interpreted as a content map when needed | Exact child identity | | Any ordinary field | One complete child node | Exact child identity | For example, `name: {blueId: ...}` is invalid: a label is literal metadata, not a node slot. To reference a list, replace the whole list node, not the `items` sequence slot. ### 2.4 Input roles | Role | Meaning | May execute Source construction? | |---|---|---| | **Source** | Authored document with optional directive, aliases and construction expressions | Yes, once | | **Preprocessed Source** | Baseline-normalized Source; controls can remain | Yes, at compilation | | **Exact** | Already-established complete content, possibly partially materialized | No | | **Direct** | Exact input with every type and specification position already a pure reference | No | | **Compact canonical wire** | Explicit codec using verified list-prefix records | Decode, never replay Source | | **Effective result** | Interpretation bound to exact origins and coverage | Not an exact-input replacement | **LANG-INPUT-ROLE.** Every operation MUST establish the role of its input before interpreting it. JSON versus YAML does not select the role. Loading a published exact body MUST NOT execute its contents as new Source. A failed verification MUST NOT be retried under other modes until an identity happens to match. ### 2.5 Abstract operations The names below identify contracts, not mandatory SDK method names. `Context` means the fixed Language/registry/bindings, any explicitly selected out-of-band resource controls and available verified or verifiable evidence. Returning an identity alone never establishes semantic validity. | Operation | Input role | Output | Evidence | Guarantee | |---|---|---|---|---| | EXACT_ID | prepared exact Node/Ref | exact identity | identities of complete child contributions; bodies only for preparation that requires them | none | | PREPARE_SOURCE | Source and fixed environment | constructed exact node + new dependencies | preprocessing and actual construction dependencies | structural preparation; not whole admission | | ADMIT_SOURCE | Source + explicit definition/value goal | validated canonical exact result + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | whole-graph admission; root duplicate normalization | | ADMIT_EXACT | existing exact input + goal | validated same exact node + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | whole-graph admission; no migration | | ADMIT_DIRECT | strict Direct input + goal | validated same exact node + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | Direct type-slot grammar plus admission | | ADMIT_CANONICAL | compact wire + goal | decoded validated exact node + artifacts | prefix, type and required graph evidence | admission after the declared codec | | RESOLVE_COMPLETE / CERTIFY | prepared exact input/recipe + goal | effective head and certified obligations | requested definition/active value closure | specified semantic closure | | OBSERVE | exact input, path and question | established / absent / incomplete / invalid | dependency closure of this question | only declared coverage | | LOOKUP_EXACT | exact graph and pointer | exact child, literal, sequence or absence | required direct navigation evidence | no contextual Source reconstruction | | SPLIT_FRAGMENTS | exact graph and complete-node cuts | same root plus exact fragment map | selected nodes and structural ancestors | identity-preserving materialization | | REFINE_EXACT | ordered exact base and overlay | complete exact compatible result | required exact operands and declarations | preserves inherited guarantees; not arbitrary edit | | CHECK_SUBTYPE | candidate and parent definitions | Boolean or invalid/incomplete result | needed type and preservation evidence | specified subtype relation | | REFINE_SCHEMA | ordered inherited/authored schemas | constraints or refined exact schema | schema operands and required domains | no explicit weakening | | CONJOIN_SCHEMA | independent constraint descriptors | combined internal constraints | previously established predicates | conjunction, not override admission | | EXPAND / COLLAPSE | exact graph + complete-node paths | another materialization | navigation and selected exact nodes | same exact identities | | MINIMIZE | certified exact origin + goal | valid Source and available dependencies | enough evidence for the round trip | same required effective view; ID may change | | ENCODE_EXACT / DECODE_EXACT | exact content / exact wire | identity-preserving exact representation | declared dependencies | codec, not Source compilation | | ENCODE_COMPACT / DECODE_COMPACT | exact content / compact wire | identity-preserving compact representation | selected prefix evidence | codec, not Source replay | | FINALIZE_SET / VERIFY_MEMBER | symbolic set / owning-set proof | master/mapping or verified member | complete set boundary and proof | exact set addressing; admission separate | **LANG-ADMISSION-CLAIM.** Structural naming MUST NOT be presented as semantic admission. An operation claiming whole-document admission MUST establish the required exact graph and type definitions, then certify its explicit goal. A selected observation MUST NOT be used as whole-document certification. Definition and completed-value goals are distinct proof obligations, not different Blue node kinds. ### 2.6 Fundamental relationships | Relationship | Required distinction | |---|---| | Exact equality | Includes own labels, type and all identity-bearing content | | Scalar predicate comparison | Uses effective domain and the specified payload rules | | Preservation | May permit additional object fields while retaining inherited guarantees | | Subtype | Uses the specified structural/nominal relation, not a matching name | | Semantic round trip | Preserves the observations defined by `same_view`; need not preserve Source ID | | Availability | Missing evidence is neither an absent field nor a valid target | **Algorithm:** A01 defines records and invariants; A03 defines exact identity; A06 defines effective recipes. `OPERATIONS` in the annex composes existing algorithms into the abstract operation contracts without a storage or receipt dependency. --- ## 3. Serialization, scalar codecs and empty content ### Purpose and input Parse one JSON or portable YAML document into the shared node model without losing distinctions that determine identity. Formatting outside strings is not content. Parsed strings and number categories are content-bearing inputs to the subsequent codec. ### 3.1 Text parsing **LANG-PARSE.** Read exactly one document. Reject duplicate decoded keys, non-string map keys, malformed Unicode and invalid syntax. A document root MUST NOT be null. JSON `\u` escapes use ASCII hexadecimal digits; valid surrogate pairs decode to one Unicode scalar, and unpaired surrogates fail. A parser MUST NOT replace malformed input with replacement characters. Numeric tokens retain this complete ASCII grammar until scalar encoding: ```text -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)? ``` A token with neither point nor exponent is integer-spelled. A token with either is decimal/exponent-spelled. Thus bare `1` and `1.0` are not interchangeable inference inputs. **LANG-YAML.** YAML supplies presentation syntax only. Quoted and block scalars are strings. An empty plain scalar or exactly `null` is null; exactly `true` and `false` are Boolean; a full JSON-number match is a retained number token; other permitted plain text is a string. Reject anchors, aliases, explicit tags, directives, merge-key syntax, multiple documents and non-JSON data types. Quoted `"<<"` is an ordinary string key. Plain `True`, `~`, `01`, `.inf` and date-looking text are not implicit Boolean, null, numeric or timestamp values. **LANG-TEXT.** Preserve parsed strings exactly. Do not trim, case-fold, normalize Unicode, normalize line endings inside parsed strings, or remove block-scalar trailing newlines. YAML folding and chomping determine the parsed string. Different resulting strings may identify different nodes even when they look similar. ### 3.2 Wrappers and nulls A bare scalar and a `value`-only wrapper normalize alike. A bare list and an `items`-only wrapper normalize alike. Explicit additional metadata remains content. **LANG-EMPTY.** In ordinary objects, remove null-valued members but preserve an object left empty. Never remove a list position. Source list null becomes the designated hole. Exact and Direct list null is invalid. `{}`, `[]`, absence, empty Text and the hole are distinct. | Input | Exact-normalization consequence | |---|---| | `{x: null}` | `{}` | | `{x: {y: null}}` | `{x: {}}`; the `x` edge remains | | `{value: null}` | `{}` | | `{blueId: X, extra: null}` | Invalid mixed reference, before null removal | | Source `[null, {}, []]` | `[HOLE, {}, []]`, three positions | | `[1,2]` and `{items:[1,2]}` | Same payload-only list | | `{type: List, items:[1,2]}` | Different exact node with an explicit type edge | The hole is the ordinary exact object `{$empty:true}`. Its exact identity is `6V647wzsPU3zXvrc5AwKsqbFmkgHWV8WAeyBfNG1T8Rx`. A reference to that node has the same hole behavior. `{$empty:false}` or the same object with additional metadata is ordinary different content. Hole-filling permission applies only at the list-specialization positions specified in §8. ### 3.3 Own-type scalar encoding **LANG-SCALAR-INFERENCE.** Without an own type, strings infer Text, Booleans infer Boolean, safe integer-spelled numbers infer Integer, and decimal/exponent numbers infer Double. No automatic container type is inferred. Converting an untyped decimal token to an integer because its current value is integral is not permitted. The safe unquoted Integer interval is `[-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]`, inclusive. | Exact own type | Admitted input and exact output | |---|---| | **Integer** | Decode an integral numeric token exactly, or a canonical decimal Integer string. Store safe results as numbers and larger results as quoted canonical decimal strings. | | **Double** | Decode an admitted decimal token/string to the nearest finite binary64 value, ties to even. Both zero signs have one commitment. | | **Text** | Require a string. No automatic stringification. | | **Boolean** | Require a Boolean. No truthiness or string-to-Boolean conversion. | | **Custom type** | Retain the exact own type ID. Strings and Booleans stay their literal category; safe integral numeric spellings share the canonical numeric payload; other finite numeric values use binary64. Do not fetch ancestry merely to choose an intrinsic identity codec. | **LANG-INTEGER-CODEC.** An unsafe integer-spelled token fails; quoted canonical decimal with explicit Integer is the portable representation. An explicit-Integer decimal/exponent token is evaluated as an exact decimal rational and must be integral. Canonical Integer strings forbid `+`, whitespace, leading zeros, `-0`, fractions and exponents. Numeric zero spellings normalize to zero. A natively tagged mathematical Integer is not a parsed unsafe number token. **LANG-DOUBLE-CODEC.** Binary64 parsing uses round-to-nearest, ties-to-even. Nonfinite results fail; finite underflow to zero is permitted. Do not use an implementation-specific epsilon or decimal rounding during later comparisons. Integer-looking helper output does not change a Double node's type. Formatting follows the exact algorithm in A03, not a host's default floating-point display. **LANG-CUSTOM-CODEC.** Intrinsic own-type encoding and contextual interpretation are separate. Resolution may interpret canonical Text under an inherited Integer requirement without rewriting that exact Text node. Core Integer and core Double remain nominally distinct, even when their payloads compare numerically equal. ### Outcomes and algorithm Successful parsing returns values preserving these categories. Normalization returns `Node`/`Ref` values and newly established dependencies. Syntax, Unicode, grammar and codec errors are invalid input; reaching a declared resource bound is incomplete, not permission to truncate. Complete procedures: A02 and A03; contextual scalar decoding: A06. --- ## 4. Exact normalization and BlueId ### Purpose Calculate a content address from an established exact node. This operation neither proves type validity nor replaces content with the effective view. Source creation, strict admission and codecs are separate compositions over this same identity function. ### 4.1 Exact input preparation **LANG-NORMALIZE.** Normalize permitted wrappers, own scalar encodings, null omission and type slots. In Exact mode, identify an inline type from its own exact content, retain its body as a dependency and place its reference in the parent. Direct mode requires all four type slots and the `specification` metadata slot already to contain pure references. Unresolved Source aliases are not Exact or Direct input. Preserve complete explicit child nodes. Do not insert inherited fields, subtract a child's inherited fields, apply contextual type narrowing, or silently remove an explicit field during exact hashing. The separately named canonical authoring operation in §11 permits only its specific root-duplicate transformation. **LANG-SCHEMA-IDENTITY.** `schema` and `contracts` use ordinary exact child identities. Predicate evaluation does not change their exact content. Exact enum order and duplicates remain identity-bearing; effective enum interpretation is a separate operation. Explicit false keyword values are not removed merely because a predicate appears neutral. ### 4.2 Hash helper Let `I(n)` identify a prepared node. Let `H(m)` hash raw canonical JSON helper `m`. A helper is not Blue content and is never passed through primitive inference again. **LANG-HASH.** A reference contributes its target identity directly. For a materialized node, retain `name`, `description` and `value` as literals. `items` contributes its payload-list identity; `mergePolicy` contributes the exact core Text identity of its literal; every other retained field contributes its child identity. Hash the resulting helper once. ```python def helper(n,token=None): m={} for k,v in n.fields: if k in LITERALS: m[k]=v elif k=='items': m[k]={'blueId':list_id(v,token)} elif k=='mergePolicy': m[k]={'blueId':identity(scalar('Text',v),token)} else: m[k]={'blueId':identity(v,token)} return m ``` For an `items`-only node the result is the payload-list identity itself. A metadata-bearing list additionally hashes the outer object helper. The root's identity is the document identity; there is no filename or document-envelope hash. ### 4.3 List fold **LANG-LIST-HASH.** Preserve order, multiplicity, nesting and all exact elements. Start with `H({"$list":"empty"})`. For each element, update the accumulator with the domain-separated pair of the previous payload identity and the element identity. Do not hash an array of elements or an array of IDs instead. ```python def append_id(p,e): return H({'$listCons':{'prev':{'blueId':p},'elem':{'blueId':e}}}) ``` ```python def list_id(xs,token=None): p=H({'$list':'empty'}) for x in xs: p=append_id(p,identity(x,token)) return p ``` A known exact payload-prefix ID can seed further fold steps. It does not by itself establish the prefix's length, element contents or type validity. A prefix reference used as an ordinary element denotes a nested list, not concatenation. ### 4.4 Canonical helper bytes **LANG-CANONICAL-BYTES.** Apply the canonical helper encoding defined here and in Appendix D to each helper. Order decoded object names by unsigned UTF-16 code units; preserve array order. Use required JSON escapes, exact Unicode content and the specified shortest binary64 rendering. Encode as UTF-8 without BOM, optional whitespace or trailing newline. Hash those bytes with SHA-256 once. The binary64 formatter searches exact rational candidates. Fixed notation applies from decimal exponent −6 through 20; otherwise use lowercase `e`, a `+` for a nonnegative exponent and no redundant leading zeros. The full candidate-selection and tie rules are executable in `number_text`. Neither a locale formatter nor default whole-object serialization supplies the required behavior automatically. **LANG-ID-ENCODING.** Base58-encode the 32 digest bytes using `123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz`. Leading zero bytes become leading `1` characters. Do not add a checksum, multibase prefix, byte reversal or hexadecimal intermediate. Incoming plain IDs must canonically decode to exactly 32 bytes. A cyclic-member ID is a plain master followed by `#` and a canonical nonnegative decimal index. ### 4.5 Why representation substitution works — informative A complete child and its reference supply the same child ID to the same helper position. Consequently the parent helper bytes are unchanged. Repeating the argument upward proves substitution for finite acyclic structure; repeating the fold proves it for lists. This is an identical-preimage argument, not a claim that finite digests are injective. Cyclic finalization has the separate ordering and proof rules in §12. The premise matters: replacing content with an inherited delta or replaying a Source constructor does not preserve the exact child. The hash rule cannot make those transformations correct. **Outputs:** exact ID; helper traces may be exposed separately. **Evidence:** the reference identity itself suffices for structural naming; requested interpretation or admission can require bodies. **Full algorithm:** A03. Worked bytes appear in §15. --- ## 5. References, verified graph access and materialization ### Purpose Obtain the exact content needed for an operation without making its meaning depend on whether that content was inline, cached or fetched. Address verification establishes that a body belongs to an ID. Semantic certification establishes different facts and follows §§6–10. ### 5.1 Evidence required to open a node **LANG-VERIFY.** Before using a fetched plain body, normalize it in the explicitly selected role and recompute its exact ID. Require equality with the requested ID. A body consisting only of a reference repeating the requested ID is not materialization evidence. A fetched child may remain referenced; authenticating its parent's direct commitment does not require recursively fetching it. An ordinary exact provider supplies already-established content. A separately selected Source provider must bind the interpretation environment and establish the requested exact result through that declared preparation path. Neither interface may retry under alternate modes or substitute a different registry after a mismatch. The provider-record procedures in Appendix D define the required interpretation and evidence checks. An adapter may use another carrier while preserving those checks. **LANG-EVIDENCE-OUTCOME.** Required unavailable or incomplete content yields an incomplete operation. Wrong or malformed content yields invalid evidence. Neither is semantic absence. A complete direct manifest must authenticate every direct contribution needed to establish its identity; a partial map cannot establish a missing key by omission. No body is trusted merely because it came from a cache or a configured database. A finalized cyclic member requires an owning-set proof. Hashing its detached materialized body as an ordinary node does not authenticate its `MASTER#index` identity. ### 5.2 Logical paths **LANG-PATH.** Paths use slash-separated components and tilde escaping over the abstract node as follows. `""` denotes the root; `/` denotes an empty-named child; `/items/0` denotes a list element. Only `~0` and `~1` are valid escapes. Traversal must open a referenced container when its structure is required. The syntax wrapper's `blueId` is not a semantic child. Literal slots can be inspected where the operation permits them. They cannot be collapsed into child references. The `items` sequence is not an independently addressable node slot; its complete enclosing list is. ### 5.3 Expansion, collapse and fragments **LANG-MATERIALIZATION.** Expansion reveals selected verified nodes; collapse replaces selected complete nodes by their exact references. Both preserve root identity and the identities of retained exact children. Navigational ancestors may be opened; unrelated child payloads need not be opened solely to carry their references. A cyclic handle preserves its member identity and owning proof during these operations. The fragment operation cuts a declared set of complete-node positions. Its structural ancestors are materialized as needed, selected non-root nodes are collapsed and the returned fragment map supplies their bodies under their own IDs. A cut is a request to export the selected complete node, including when that node is already a reference. Verify and include its body under the requested exact ID; do not silently omit an available referenced cut. Required missing evidence makes the split incomplete and wrong evidence invalid. Unselected referenced children remain opaque unless another required navigation opens them. For cyclic members, retain the member address and supply the owning-set proof with the exported body, rather than hashing the detached body into a new address. The order of the requested cuts does not select different fragment content. Literal slots and the `items` sequence slot are not valid cuts. ### 5.4 Immutable evidence and caches **LANG-CACHE.** Reusing immutable verified content may eliminate physical retrieval. It MUST NOT change successful semantic results, erase a validation obligation or turn incomplete evidence into established absence. Interpreted results are bound to the exact input, requirements, goal and selected rules, not solely to a display body. A changed exact node requires a new identity and any newly necessary checks. Whole-graph admission can require substantially more evidence than a selected read. This does not make selected reads invalid: their result must state the scope of what was established. No selected result becomes a whole-document certificate by being stored in a cache. **Inputs:** an exact node/reference, selected paths or a requested body, and the fixed evidence context. **Outputs:** the verified node, changed materialization or declared observation. **Failures:** invalid paths/content/evidence; incomplete evidence or limits. **Algorithms:** A04, A06 and A12. --- ## 6. Types, specialization and validation goals ### Purpose A type contributes guarantees. A descendant may add compatible information, fill permitted declarations and narrow constraints, but cannot contradict those guarantees. Whether a node is used as a definition or a completed value is a property of the operation, not an extra serialized node category. ### 6.1 Any admitted node may be used as a type **LANG-TYPE-CONTRIBUTION.** Using node T as a type contributes its declared structure, fixed values, nested requirements, collection metadata and schemas. Retain T's exact identity separately from the effective requirements it supplies. A complete type's `items` are its complete exact payload, not a suffix to append again. A type need not look like a programming-language class. A node representing a particular individual may itself become a type; its fixed content then constrains descendants. ### 6.2 Definition and completed value **LANG-GOAL.** Definition admission establishes valid declarations, fixed contributions and specified local consistency while allowing future payloads to remain unspecified. Completed-value admission additionally checks all active value obligations. Neither goal exempts malformed shapes, unknown required type definitions, incompatible fixed content or explicit weakening. The caller must select the goal; a failed value request MUST NOT silently fall back to definition admission. ```yaml name: Currency type: Text ``` This is a valid definition. It is not a completed Text scalar because no payload was supplied. Its `name` does not itself select definition mode. A value of that type can supply `value: PLN`. ```yaml name: Two to four integers type: List itemType: Integer schema: minItems: 2 maxItems: 4 ``` This is a valid list definition with an unspecified future payload. Adding `items: []` supplies a concrete empty list, which violates the minimum even during definition admission. Omitted payload and explicit empty payload are different. ### 6.3 Preservation versus equality **LANG-PRESERVATION.** A descendant must retain all inherited guaranteed fields, fixed scalar values, applicable types, collection requirements, schema obligations and list-prefix guarantees. Fixed scalar comparisons use effective scalar type and value. Object refinement may add fields without contradicting any inherited child; it does not require the whole object's ID to remain equal. List preservation follows §8. For parent `x: 1`, supplying `x: 2` fails. For parent `address: {city: Warsaw}`, adding a `street` within `address` may succeed if no additional rule forbids it; changing `city` does not. An omitted contribution inherits what is already guaranteed. It does not remove a requirement. A referenced child is not exempt from comparison, and its effective enrichment must not overwrite its exact content. ### 6.4 Names and descriptions **LANG-LABELS.** Own `name` and `description` affect identity. At every type-to-instance boundary, the type root's labels do not flow to the new instance. Matching ignores root labels, but exact fixed-node preservation includes its identity-bearing labels. Reused inherited declaration children carry their own labels until permitted override; present labels on fixed child content cannot be changed incompatibly. An absent label may be supplied where the merge permits it. The own `specification` metadata also does not become an instance field. Its governing association remains discoverable on the exact referenced type and its ancestry; a subtype cannot erase a base protocol by declaring different own metadata. See §17 for definition-valid target checks and atomic preservation. An instance of Address may be named Delivery Address or have no name. Expanding its type may reveal `name: Address` inside that type node; this does not name the instance Address. Expanding a reference to the instance reveals the instance's own labels. ### 6.5 Type compatibility **LANG-SUBTYPE.** The six core types are nominal exact registry identities. Distinct cores are not interchangeable. Declared ancestry establishes a subtype relationship, and the specified structural comparison can establish compatible specialization by checking kind/core, guaranteed content, constraints and collection metadata. Matching a human-readable type name is not evidence. Merely finding one common accepted value is not a subtype proof. The procedure is a defined structural simulation over this vocabulary, not an unrestricted theorem prover. `guarantees_schema` can establish requirements from fixed scalars, finite alternatives and guaranteed structure. Applicability remains binding: `uniqueItems: false` still describes a list predicate, not an unconstrained scalar type. A supplied primitive may acquire a compatible contextual domain in its effective view. Canonical Integer text is interpreted under an inherited Integer requirement by `scalar_effective`. No contextual conversion changes the exact operand used for identity. The code supplies the complete decoder and compatibility cases. ### 6.6 Type chains, recursive graphs and termination **LANG-TYPE-CYCLE.** Resolve own-type ancestry depth-first and reject a type repeated on its active inheritance chain. Completed reuse in another branch is sharing, not a cycle. Supported recursive object/list references do not automatically make an inheritance cycle. Structural comparisons use the specified guarded repeated-pair algorithm; recursively unfolding declarations must not manufacture presence or a completed value. Recipes retain ordered exact contributions and contextual requirements for one position. A head is its local effective interpretation with deferred child recipes. The exact same contribution is not merged twice merely because it was reached through two equivalent materializations. These records are notation; production implementations may store equivalent information differently. ### 6.7 Collections and content maps **LANG-COLLECTION-TYPES.** `itemType`, `keyType` and `valueType` inherit when omitted and may only be narrowed when supplied. Every applicable list element and Dictionary value must satisfy its requirements. Direct Dictionary keys must be canonical text of a supported scalar key domain; reject noncanonical keys rather than renaming them. The default key domain is Text when no key type is inherited or authored. A collection child has one contextual recipe: its exact own/inherited contributions plus the enclosing `itemType` or `valueType` requirement. Construction, validation, complete resolved export, selected query and semantic comparison MUST use that same recipe. A complete export cannot describe the raw child alone while a query describes the constrained child. Requirements retain their nested fields, schemas and nominal type, not only their primitive kind. For `type: Dictionary`, `valueType: {type: Integer}`, `foo: "3"`, both complete and selected effective observations describe Integer 3. The exact admitted child is still the supplied Text "3"; contextual interpretation is not an identity rewrite. Adding `schema: {minimum: 2}` to `valueType` must preserve that constraint in both observations. Strict admission establishes all declared type definitions even for empty collections. A Dictionary key domain that is not a supported scalar is invalid even when there are no keys. This is distinct from selected resolution of an unrelated field. **Algorithms:** A06 for types/heads/preservation and A07 for exact refinement. **Results:** effective declaration/value or a compatibility, schema, type-cycle or evidence outcome. Examples do not override the procedural checks in the annex. --- ## 7. Schemas: predicates, narrowing and conjunction ### Purpose A schema is ordinary exact content with a separately defined interpretation. Refining an inherited schema is not the same operation as conjoining independent requirements. This distinction prevents an invalid authored weakening from being hidden by a stronger inherited predicate. ### 7.1 Vocabulary and operands **LANG-SCHEMA-VOCABULARY.** Interpret only the keywords in the following table. Establish referenced schemas and operand nodes before using them. Inline, wrapped and referenced operands must select the same predicate when they identify the same admitted scalar or sequence. Unknown keywords and wrong operand types fail; there is no implicit `const`, general expression language or `enumAll` keyword. | Keywords | Operand | Predicate domain | |---|---|---| | `required` | Boolean | Child presence; root existence already satisfies root requiredness | | `minItems`, `maxItems` | Safe nonnegative Integer | Number of effective list elements | | `uniqueItems` | Boolean | Exact element identities in an effective list | | `minFields`, `maxFields` | Safe nonnegative Integer | Present ordinary object fields | | `minLength`, `maxLength` | Safe nonnegative Integer | Unicode scalar count in Text | | `minimum`, `maximum` | Numeric scalar | Inclusive exact-rational endpoints | | `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum` | Numeric scalar | Exclusive exact-rational endpoints | | `multipleOf` | Positive numeric scalar | Integral exact-rational quotient | | `enum` | Payload-only sequence of scalar restrictions | Required primitive payload and compatible type domain | Every scalar operand MUST itself be certified as a completed value, including its own fixed data, nominal ancestry and schemas, before its scalar description is used or memoized. Describing a number without checking its own minimum, enum or other constraints is not sufficient. This obligation applies even when the containing node is being admitted only as a definition. The same rule applies to numeric, count, Boolean and enum operands, whether inline or referenced. A successful address check is not operand admission. Reentrant operand validation is an invalid recursive operand dependency, not provisional success; reaching an operation limit remains incomplete. Operand diagnostics identify the relevant schema keyword and, for enum, the item path. A numeric-looking Text is not automatically a numeric bound. Use an explicit Integer node for large Integer bounds. Schemas affect validity, not the identity codec of their enclosing scalar. ### 7.2 Presence and applicability **LANG-SCHEMA-PRESENCE.** A metadata-only declaration does not by itself supply a completed payload. Fixed inherited content can establish presence. `{}` and `[]` are present content. An optional absent child's value obligations remain inactive, while definition checks still apply. A pure reference cannot be classified as an absent field merely because its body is unavailable. **LANG-SCHEMA-APPLICABILITY.** A predicate's domain must match the effective known kind. Do not silently ignore a string predicate on a number or a list predicate on an object. A seemingly neutral operand, such as `minLength: 0`, retains its domain requirement. For a nominal scalar with no established primitive ancestor, a supplied effective scalar payload nevertheless establishes the predicate carrier: Boolean, Integer, Double or Text according to its already normalized scalar category. Apply applicable predicates to that carrier and reject incompatible predicates; do not skip them merely because `core` is absent. This does not synthesize a nominal ancestry edge or rewrite the exact type. A payload-free definition may defer that carrier until a payload is supplied; ordinary local-consistency and definition obligations still apply. Enum domain compatibility remains the declared subtype check, not host-language coercion. Count present ordinary fields only; reserved metadata does not contribute to `minFields` or `maxFields`. ### 7.3 Numeric predicates **LANG-SCHEMA-NUMERIC.** Integer values are exact mathematical integers. Double values and bounds use their exact binary64 rational values. Compare rationals exactly. `multipleOf: m` requires positive m and an integral quotient. No epsilon, decimal-display rounding or host floating-point modulo is permitted. For positive reduced rationals `p1/q1` and `p2/q2`, independent divisibility requirements combine to `lcm(p1,p2)/gcd(q1,q2)`. This is an internal exact constraint, not permission to emit a rounded Double schema. The constraint descriptor may retain exact numerator/denominator values without inventing new identity-bearing Blue fields. ### 7.4 Explicit refinement **LANG-SCHEMA-NARROW.** Check the authored facets against inherited facets before conjunction. Omission inherits. An explicitly supplied facet must retain or increase strictness; incompatible or weaker facets fail even if conjoining them with the parent would restore the parent's restriction. | Inherited facet | Allowed explicit descendant facet | |---|---| | Lower endpoint | Equal or higher; inclusive at an equal inherited exclusive endpoint is weaker | | Upper endpoint | Equal or lower; inclusive at an equal inherited exclusive endpoint is weaker | | Minimum length/count | Equal or higher | | Maximum length/count | Equal or lower | | `required: true` or `uniqueItems: true` | Repeat true; omission inherits; explicit false fails | | `multipleOf: m` | A positive integral multiple of m under exact rational comparison | | Enum alternatives | Alternatives covered by the inherited domain/payload restrictions according to the algorithm | When both inclusive and exclusive endpoints are written on one side, check **each authored endpoint separately** against the inherited effective endpoint before selecting the stronger resulting endpoint. Over inherited `minimum: 5`, authored `{minimum: 4, exclusiveMinimum: 6}` is invalid: the second facet does not excuse the first. Likewise inherited `maximum: 10` rejects `{maximum: 11, exclusiveMaximum: 9}`. Raw authored-facet provenance is distinct from the conjoined effective constraint descriptor. Thus `[5,10] → [6,9]` succeeds, while `[5,10] → [4,11]`, `[4,9]` or `[6,11]` fails. `multipleOf: 4 → multipleOf: 6` is not narrowing: 6 itself violates the parent. Requiring both independently is a different operation and yields multiples of 12. The decisive call order is the executable rule: ```python def refine_schema(parent,authored,c=None): check_schema_narrowing(parent,authored,c) return conjoin_schema(parent,authored) ``` ### 7.5 Independent conjunction **LANG-SCHEMA-CONJOIN.** Independent applicable obligations all remain in force. Combine requiredness and uniqueness with OR, minimum sizes with maximum, maximum sizes with minimum, numeric endpoints with the stronger bound, and divisibility by exact rational LCM. Exclusivity wins at an equal endpoint. This operation does not admit an explicitly invalid override. Exact schema refinement retains the ordered base/overlay's supplied keyword encodings after successful admission. Independently combined internal constraints need not be serialized as one new exact schema node. There is no universal semantic-schema minimizer in the identity calculation. ### 7.6 Enumerations **LANG-SCHEMA-ENUM.** An entry denotes its scalar domain and canonical primitive payload. A candidate must match the primitive payload and have an equal or narrower established domain. Labels do not select another scalar predicate. A referenced restriction has the same meaning as its verified inline form. Exact enum order/multiplicity remains content; effective interpretation may eliminate duplicate alternatives. Independent enum requirements are conjunctions of alternative groups: every group must accept. The internal descriptor may retain those groups rather than invent a type representing their intersection. An established empty primitive-payload intersection fails. Equal primitive payloads do not by themselves prove compatible type domains; the specified subtype procedure still applies. ### 7.7 Consistency versus existence of a future value **LANG-SCHEMA-LOCAL.** Definition preparation checks the specified local contradictions: keyword forms and applicability, size-bound order, numeric endpoint consistency, nonpositive divisibility, empty alternatives and violations by supplied fixed data. It does not prove the existence of every possible completing value. A supplied fixed prefix below its minimum is invalid; an omitted future payload retains its obligations. Completed values must satisfy every active predicate. **Algorithm:** A05, with scalar domain/type procedures in A06. **Outcome:** normalized internal constraints or a specific invalid/incomplete result. The algorithm never changes schema content merely to make its own acceptance test succeed. --- ## 8. Lists and specialization ### Purpose Separate an exact list's complete payload from Source authoring and from compatibility checking. Append-only Source explicitly declares its inherited prefix. Ordinary positional Source presents indexed elements or a separate, pure edit sequence. Neither mode guesses intent from how many values happen to be written. The exact element fold remains §4; authoring is not a second list hash. ### 8.1 Complete candidates preserve inherited guarantees **LANG-LIST-PRESERVE.** A complete positional descendant of `[N, HOLE, R]` must retain at least that prefix. Its elements are `[N′, V, R′, ...]`, where N′ preserves N and R′ preserves R. The hole supplies no fixed-value guarantee; applicable element types, schemas and container rules still apply. `{}` is an ordinary object, not a hole. Neither a repeated scalar nor `$replace` may contradict inherited fixed content. **LANG-LIST-POLICY.** Omitted policy inherits; absent any selected policy, the default is positional. An explicitly conflicting inherited policy fails. Under append-only, every inherited element retains its exact identity, including a hole. Positional edits are forbidden. The suffix remains subject to `itemType`, bounds and uniqueness. `$previousItems: false` does not switch policy or remove a prefix. ### 8.2 Select the Source mode from established context **LANG-SOURCE-LIST-CONTEXT.** Apply authoring rules only to Source expressions. Exact handles, pure references and explicitly Exact/Direct content are already complete operands, not programs to replay. Compile type-expression positions before establishing the enclosing declaration. A supplied item sequence always uses both the node's own type and its containing context, including collection metadata even when that context has no fixed items. | Condition | Required action | |---|---| | Exact handle or pure reference | Retain the complete exact operand; do not recompile its body as Source | | No authored `items` slot | Inherit normally without injecting a complete inherited payload into exact identity | | Contextual declaration has an inherited list payload | Establish its complete exact prefix and collection requirements, even with local `type: List` or omitted local type | | Established policy is append-only and `items` is authored | Require exactly one initial verified prefix assertion, then compile only suffix elements | | Established policy is positional and any top-level item is an edit | Require an edit-only sequence; edits address the original base | | Established policy is positional and there are no controls | Interpret ordinary elements at indices 0 through n−1, retaining/refining each inherited position | Unavailable evidence needed to establish the declaration is incomplete, not an empty prefix. The spelling or placement of the same admitted type must not drop `itemType` requirements. Unrelated siblings cannot select another list's authoring mode. ### 8.3 Establish the inherited base **LANG-LIST-BASE.** Combine the own type and independently applicable containing declaration using the ordinary requirement rules. Keep complete exact base elements separate from their effective interpretation. Conflicting fixed contributions fail; traversal order does not choose a winner. A published type's exact items are already complete. An anchor verifies that selected payload; it cannot choose another provider list as a base. ### 8.4 Disjoint Source grammars **LANG-LIST-CONTROLS.** Recognize controls in their instruction position before ordinary element inference. A sequence belongs to exactly one of the following grammars. Reject malformed, misplaced, repeated or mixed controls; never silently reinterpret them as ordinary data. | Mode | Sequence | Meaning | |---|---|---| | Append-only shorthand | `[{$previousItems: true}, X, Y, ...]` | Assert a nonempty inherited prefix; append the new elements | | Append-only empty-prefix shorthand | `[{$previousItems: false}, X, Y, ...]` | Assert that there are zero inherited elements; supply the new elements | | Append-only exact assertion | `[{$previous: {blueId: P}}, X, Y, ...]` | Verify P is the payload-only ID of the selected inherited prefix; append the new elements | | Positional presentation | `[X0, X1, ..., Xn]` | Present successive positions, refining inherited entries and then extending beyond the inherited length | | Positional edits | `[{$pos: i, ...overlay}, {$pos: j, $replace: X}, ...]` | Edit only specified original inherited positions; retain all other positions | `$previousItems` has exactly one member whose value is a Boolean literal, not a string, wrapper, reference or truthy value. It must be first and unique, and it is legal only for an established append-only list. `true` requires at least one inherited element; `false` requires zero. Both an absent inherited payload and an established empty payload have zero elements, but unavailable evidence establishes neither. `$previousItems` and `$previous` cannot be combined. Whenever append-only `items` is authored, an initial assertion is REQUIRED, including for a new list, an empty suffix or an empty resulting list. Thus `items: []` and an unmarked `[C]` are not valid append-only Source. Omit `items` to inherit without a local list contribution. Use `[{$previousItems: true}]` to explicitly contribute no suffix over a nonempty prefix, and `[{$previousItems: false}]` for an empty prefix with no new elements. These remain distinct authoring forms and may retain distinct own payload contributions. The `$previous` record has exactly one `blueId` member containing a valid plain content ID. Its identity must match the complete payload-only inherited sequence, not the surrounding typed List node. It is an assertion, not a reference element or a base selector. Prefix controls are forbidden in positional Source even when they happen to name its inherited payload. For positional edits, index i is a safe nonnegative Integer token, not a decimal/exponent token, string or Boolean. It must address an existing position in the original inherited base. Duplicate indices fail. `$replace` requires `$pos` and cannot be combined with overlay fields. The concise `{$pos: i, value: v, ...scalar metadata}` form and compatible object overlays remain supported. An edit sequence cannot append, and ordinary positional elements cannot be mixed with edits, including an edit at a fifth or later position. To extend and refine in one authoring expression, use the full positional presentation. A normal exact reference in an element position always supplies a complete element, even when its body has control-looking keys. Literal control-looking exact content can be published separately and referenced; it is not a way to inject another authoring instruction. ### 8.5 Construct once, then validate **LANG-LIST-CONSTRUCT.** Prepare each Source operand once in its final position's context. For append-only, retain the exact base unchanged and append in written order. Suffix item j is compiled at absolute position `len(base) + j`, not without an index. For pure edits, process distinct original indices in increasing order. For positional presentation, the number of elements must be at least the inherited length: each inherited element is refined by the candidate at the same index, and elements beyond that length are appended. A shorter presentation is invalid, not an implicit suffix or truncation. A positional hole supplies no payload-kind constraint for its replacement, but the enclosing `itemType` still applies. Both replacements and positional overlays preserve fixed inherited guarantees. Retain base-only object fields; do not manufacture deltas that lose the complete child. At the admission boundary, validate the complete constructed node and all applicable containing declarations before returning success. Source construction alone does not certify validity: raw structural naming need not fetch opaque child references solely because a list is present. The exact result retains its own explicit metadata; do not copy every effective schema or a type root's labels into stored content. ### 8.6 Nested list context — informative example The following Source selects append-only behavior at the inner list and supplies both prefix assertions explicitly: ```yaml type: List itemType: type: List mergePolicy: append-only items: - $previousItems: false - 1 items: - - $previousItems: true - 2 ``` Its effective items are `[[1, 2]]`. Moving `type: List` and the same `itemType` declaration into an inline or separately published enclosing type retains the inner context and the same effective result. Different explicitly supplied metadata need not produce the same outer exact ID. Without `mergePolicy: append-only`, the inner list is positional. Its full presentation is `[1, 2]`; `[2]` attempts to replace fixed 1 with 2 and fails in both declaration placements. This is an intentional grammar distinction, not a remaining context bug. **Algorithms:** A07 defines preservation and pure edits; A09 defines Source construction and contextual child selection; A13 defines compact wire. Exact/Direct loading never executes these Source controls. --- ## 9. Preprocessing and Source preparation ### Purpose Turn authored syntax into a single, explicitly interpreted Source expression, then construct exact content where the language requires it. Preprocessing does not change what an already-published exact reference means. ### 9.1 Directive and bindings **LANG-PREPROCESS-DIRECTIVE.** With no root `blue` field, apply the mandatory baseline using the selected environment. A present directive is an inline configuration, a verified reference or an explicitly configured directive-alias string. A null root directive is invalid. Nested or transformation-introduced `blue` fields fail. Unknown directive fields are not silently ignored. The directive permits `imports`, `transformations` and its own identifying `name`, `description` and exact `type`. These metadata identify the configuration; they do not become fields of the resulting document. Null optional members denote omission, not a Boolean/number/string fallback to an empty configuration. **LANG-ALIASES.** Directive imports map aliases to pure final-ID references, including finalized cyclic-member addresses. Their target bodies are required when a later operation needs them, not merely to bind a name. Do not rebind a core alias to another ID. Automatic alias substitution applies only in `type`, `itemType`, `keyType` and `valueType`; an ordinary Text with the same spelling is unchanged. A matching node `name` does not create an alias. Directive aliases are explicitly selected environment bindings. URL-looking text is not permission to fetch and execute unverified content. Exact IDs, not provider locations, select configuration. ### 9.2 Establish the entire plan before execution **LANG-PREPROCESS-ORDER.** Resolve and verify required directive/configuration operands, establish imports and validate the complete ordered transformation plan before running its first transformation. Remove root `blue`; run transformations once in order; then run mandatory wrapper/null normalization, alias substitution and primitive inference. A transformation sees Source before automatic baseline inference and may emit Source shorthand for the baseline to normalize. | Stage | Output or stopping condition | |---|---| | Parse | One Source value with retained numeric tokens | | Establish configuration | Verified directive, imports and complete supported transformation plan | | Remove directive | Working Source, not a document carrying `blue` as ordinary content | | Execute transformations | Complete result of each prior transform, exactly once | | Mandatory baseline | Valid prepared Source expressions; construction controls may remain | | Compile | Exact node, with actual constructors selected by §8 | A preflight failure runs no transformation. A transformation failure does not yield a successful partial document. An implementation may fuse steps only when the same ordering and outcomes are preserved. ### 9.3 Transformation semantics **LANG-TRANSFORMS.** Select transformations by their exact registered selector, never by a human name. Required unsupported selectors fail explicitly. Configuration operands are exact content and use the same rules inline or referenced. Transforms are deterministic functions of the fixed input and verified operands; no clock, locale, randomness, mutable database or unverified network data selects the result. The selected reference environment implements primitive inference, mapped alias replacement, root-field renaming, root-Text suffix appending and root Source-expression assignment. Selector IDs, precise fields and procedures are in A08 and Appendix B.2. This is not a generic executor for unspecified extensions. The Set Root Source Field transformation stores its input expression as Text under `expression`, with an explicit `json`/`yaml` format. It does not place arbitrary object content in reserved scalar `value`. Expression parsing happens during preflight; assignment happens during execution; baseline alias/type inference follows execution. ### 9.4 Compilation is not full-view replacement **LANG-SOURCE-COMPILATION.** Compile authored inline definitions once in their own context, retain dependency bodies, preserve ordinary explicit content and execute only the constructors selected in §8. A complete exact handle/reference is retained, not recompiled. A constructor can demand inherited operands; the hasher still receives the newly constructed exact result rather than an effective resolver record. A node with no supplied items does not acquire its inherited list payload for identity solely because resolution can reveal that payload. An authored supplied sequence at a contextually inherited list path is different: §8 selects construction and produces the complete exact sequence. This distinction is part of Source meaning and does not apply to exact loading. Source preparation itself does not certify the entire result. `ADMIT_SOURCE` performs the additional checks and canonical root normalization in §11. Preprocessing configuration is not recoverable from the final node; applications needing source provenance retain it separately. **Inputs:** Source, fixed aliases/directive bindings, selected transform definitions and evidence. **Outputs:** preprocessed expression or constructed exact node and retained dependencies. **Algorithms:** A08 and A09. **Failures:** syntax/configuration, unsupported required transformation, invalid construction, invalid or unavailable evidence, declared limits. --- ## 10. Complete and selected resolution ### Purpose Interpret a node under its own and contextual requirements without changing the node's exact identity. A query can establish one answer; definition preparation and completed-value certification establish broader guarantees. Coverage belongs to the result, not to the node. ### 10.1 Effective contributions **LANG-RESOLVE-MERGE.** Resolve required own-type plans before combining them with instance contributions. Merge ordinary child fields recursively, preserve compatible fixed scalars and list guarantees, narrow authored metadata and retain all independent requirements. No conflicting fixed requirement wins by traversal order. Keep exact origins and the required contribution relationships available for subsequent checks. The local effective result includes kind, type, scalar value or deferred child recipes, labels, collection metadata, merge policy and constraints. Child recipes are opened only when the requested operation requires their semantic facts. A fully known local head does not by itself certify every child target. ### 10.2 Certification order **LANG-CERTIFY.** Certification first checks the definition and its fixed data. A value goal then certifies active completed values. Optional absent value subtrees remain inactive; definitions are not manufactured into present values. Strict admission additionally verifies the reachable exact graph and every declared type slot, including empty collection definitions. The decisive goal ordering is: ```python def certify(exact,c,goal='value'): require(goal in ('value','definition'),'InvalidOperation','validation goal') validate(exact,c,'definition') return validate(exact,c,'value') if goal=='value' else head(recipe(exact),c) ``` The finite traversal memoizes exact recipe/goal obligations. An identical exact child used under different contextual requirements does not inherit a certificate for requirements that were never checked. Missing proof cannot be replaced with a provisional success. ### 10.3 Selected observations **LANG-OBSERVE.** To establish a selected answer, resolve its semantic dependency closure: the relevant source/type contributions, path ancestors and constraints needed for that question. The answer must agree with complete processing on the declared coverage when the same evidence is available. In particular, traversing a Dictionary child through `valueType`, or a List child through `itemType`, retains the same contextual type, scalar value, constraints and nested requirements as complete resolved export. Use the contextual `child_recipe` rule, not independent copies of field traversal. Do not resolve an unrelated sibling payload solely because it exists. The reference observation vocabulary includes exact identity, effective kind, existence, literal/value observations, object keys, list length or an item, effective type, constraints and validity. Each question has its own evidence requirements. An exact identity can be known while an effective kind or value remains unavailable. A field's absence requires evidence of the relevant direct and inherited contributions. **LANG-OUTCOME.** A requested operation establishes a result, establishes absence where applicable, is incomplete, or finds invalid content/evidence. Those outcomes are distinct. A limit, unavailable reference or incomplete manifest must not become normal absence. A partial observation must not be promoted into whole-node canonical creation, completed-value admission or unrestricted minimization. Concrete SDK result objects may have different shapes. The semantic conclusion, required diagnostic facts and claimed coverage must remain the same. A result containing only some observations is not a second, partially valid Blue node. ### 10.4 Resource controls and repeatability **LANG-LIMIT.** Language imposes no universal resource/cardinality ceiling on otherwise valid finite input. Text size, parsed depth and value count, Integer text length, decimal normalization scale, internal work counters and provider-demand counts are not content-validity or identity rules. Explicit schemas, numeric kinds, canonical encodings and actual semantic errors remain binding. An implementation may expose host resource controls. An omitted resource control means no library-imposed ceiling for that operation, not an implicit reference default. Such controls are out of band. Exhaustion, allocation failure, recursion failure, cancellation or an unavailable required resource before the requested conclusion is established yields incomplete work, never a truncated successful value, normal absence, invalid-content conclusion or alternative BlueId. A host unable to establish a result must report its inability; another adequately provisioned conforming host may establish the same result. Controls must be applied consistently to equivalent Source/Exact spellings and every relevant helper; no helper silently reinstalls the old defaults. A requested export either completes in its declared exact format and can be verified, or remains incomplete. An export-envelope or transport-size restriction is operational, not a smaller domain of Blue values. Language physical work/fetch counts are not Contracts gas and must not be converted into a gas rejection. In a Contracts invocation, the caller's deterministic meter remains authoritative for semantic processing. Physical Language optimizations and private admission evidence do not change that meter's prescribed charges or justify accepting invalid or missing content. Standalone Language parsing, identity, admission and source-proof acquisition do not acquire an invented 100,000-gas charge merely because Contracts has that budget. Implementations should use lazy exact references and iterative/incremental processing where required to avoid incidental stack or materialization failures. This requirement does not promise completion on every machine or change type inference, constraints, canonicalization or BlueId algorithms. **Algorithms:** A06 defines type plans and merging; A05 defines constraints; A12 defines selected operations and outcomes; A13 supplies strict graph/type admission. Revise their resource-control plumbing and incomplete-result handling coherently; resource controls add no identity-bearing fields. --- ## 11. Validated creation, canonical authoring, minimization and export ### Purpose Make normal document creation safe while retaining low-level structural calculation. Distinguish a new canonical authoring result from existing exact content and from an alternative rendering of that content. ### 11.1 Admission **LANG-ADMIT.** An admitted result must establish the exact graph, all declared type definitions and the selected definition/value goal. Missing required type content is incomplete. Fixed-value contradictions, invalid evidence, malformed types and explicitly weaker schemas are rejected before canonical cleanup. A failed admission must not be presented as successful publication. `ADMIT_SOURCE` parses/preprocesses/constructs, performs strict admission, removes only the canonical duplicates permitted below and rechecks when removal occurs. `ADMIT_EXACT` validates existing content without running Source compilation or authoring normalization. `ADMIT_CANONICAL` decodes its declared wire codec, then admits the resulting exact node without migrating its identity. ```python def admit_document(text, context, *, goal="value", mode="source", format="json"): """Construct or decode, validate, normalize permitted duplicates, and export. The context is an operation-local fixed environment. No persistent provider write occurs here. Authentication or reuse of this result is a host boundary. """ try: with B.error_scope(context, "", "operation"): context.diagnostic_goal = goal exact = read_input(text, context, mode=mode, format=format) context.diagnostic_root = exact original_id = B.identity(exact) B.strict_certify(exact, context, goal) if mode == "source": exact, removed = B.omit_root_duplicates(exact, context) else: removed = () if removed: B.strict_certify(exact, context, goal) exact_text = B.export_exact(exact, context) compact_text = B.canonical_export(exact, context) records = B.admitted_records(exact, context) return AdmissionResult( B.identity(exact), original_id, goal, exact_text, compact_text, tuple(removed), json.dumps(records, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False), ) except RecursionError as error: raise B.Failure("OperationLimitExceeded", "recursion") from error ``` The composition returns semantic content, role and associated artifacts. SDK capability tickets, storage installation and receipt authentication are not part of this abstract procedure. ### 11.2 Whole-root duplicate normalization **LANG-ROOT-DUPLICATE.** For a newly authored materialized Source root with its own type, compare each explicitly supplied ordinary child with the complete exact child supplied by that type. Omit the edge only when the exact child IDs match, after the authored specialization has passed validation. Require semantic-view preservation. Do not remove labels, rewrite own type, reduce a partly inherited child to a delta, normalize exact schemas as semantic sets, recursively migrate independently addressed children or rewrite an existing root reference. If T fixes exact Integer 42 at `amount`, new Source roots with and without the repeated `amount: 42` create the same canonical node. A named or differently typed 42 is not that exact duplicate. Text PLN and Currency PLN remain distinct under Holder because neither complete value is an exact duplicate of the inherited payload-free declaration. This rule applies at the creation root, not every nested node. Creating a child independently as a new Source root is a separately selected authoring operation. Existing Exact, Direct and Compact inputs retain their existing exact identities. The created result should retain the original structural ID and removed paths as out-of-band transformation facts; they are not fields of the node. This is a limited normalization contract, not a theorem that all logically equivalent Source programs have one identity. General minimization is not substituted for it. ### 11.3 Exact and compact exports **LANG-EXPORT.** Export the identified exact content, not its helper or effective view. Type slots contain exact references and newly established definitions remain available as dependencies. Preserve numeric category on reload: an integer-looking binary64 wire payload uses a decimal marker where the exact codec requires it; helper bytes do not acquire that marker. Verify the exported representation reloads to the same exact ID. Different permitted child materializations may yield different wire bytes with the same identity. Serialization-inspection choices are not canonical authoring choices. A provider returning an exact export must label it as exact content, not Source. **LANG-COMPACT-PREFIX.** Compact canonical wire may encode an unchanged nonempty inherited **append-only** list prefix as its first item `{$previous:{blueId:P}}`. P identifies the payload-only prefix. Decode the verified sequence and concatenate the suffix; the marker is not an element. A bare reference in an ordinary element position remains a nested node. Metadata-bearing outer List identity is not a payload-prefix identity. The reference exporter selects this compression only for an established append-only policy and the complete inherited base at that path, with identical prefix element IDs. It emits ordinary full item sequences for positional lists and for append-only lists without a nonempty prefix. `$previousItems` is Source-only and is never emitted as a canonical prefix control. The compact decoder rejects that shorthand and positional prefix anchors, verifies the payload-only prefix and its equality to the selected inherited base, then validates the resulting exact content. It does not choose a random provider list or an arbitrary longest prefix. This codec tightens prefix acceptance without changing the exact list fold. Literal exact elements with top-level control-looking fields are escaped as ordinary exact references with supplied bodies. Noninitial or mixed compact controls fail. The codec is explicitly selected; exact-body failure must not trigger guessed compact decoding. **LANG-DEPENDENCIES.** A result promising reusable serialization must retain or return bodies for newly introduced references and required cyclic proofs. Returning an ID does not publish its dependencies automatically. A reference known only to a temporary calculation context is not a self-contained public round trip. Existing dependencies may remain externally supplied under the documented provider contract. ### 11.4 Minimization **LANG-MINIMIZE.** Return valid Source that re-resolves to the same required effective observations as the certified input. Exact Source identity may change. A bare effective view cannot uniquely recover an original exact input; retain the certified exact origin required by the operation. Different valid renderings are permitted; no globally shortest serialization is required. The reference strategy constructs a lossless Source representation, proposes finite smaller reductions in a fixed order, re-prepares and certifies each candidate, and accepts only candidates passing `same_view`. Each accepted reduction decreases size. Append-only output retains a valid initial assertion: a bound `$previous` for a selected nonempty prefix, or `$previousItems: false` for a zero-element base. Positional output uses a complete indexed presentation or a valid pure edit form. Reductions cannot erase a required assertion, introduce mixed modes or replay an append-only complete payload as a suffix. Nested candidates retain their applicable collection context. Newly introduced replacement values must remain available across the output boundary. `same_view` compares types, kinds, labels, policy, collection requirements, constraints, scalar payloads, presence, fields, items and `contracts`. It does not compare only business-value displays or require equal origin IDs. A caller cannot ignore missing evidence encountered in establishing a purported equivalent result. ### 11.5 Reusable validation evidence **LANG-VALIDATION-EVIDENCE.** Previously established validation may be reused only for the same exact content, selected rules, validation goal, applicable requirements and adequate coverage. A caller's unchecked `valid: true` assertion is not such evidence. A definition proof cannot certify a completed value; a standalone proof cannot establish new contextual requirements. Evidence reuse changes work, not canonicalization or the resulting ID. The abstract obligation is independent of authentication mechanism. HMAC records, in-process issued handles, storage atomicity and trusted issuer configuration belong to the separately documented SDK/host contract. A library may expose raw storage for untrusted content, but that operation must not imply semantic admission. **Algorithms:** A04 for exact export; A11 for minimization; A13 for strict certification, root duplicates and compact wire; `OPERATIONS` for storage-independent composition. --- ## 12. Cyclic identities and owning-set proofs ### Purpose Ordinary child-first identity cannot assign mutually dependent new node IDs. A cyclic-set operation establishes one master and a stable member mapping for an explicitly bounded symbolic set. This does not make cyclic inheritance valid. ### 12.1 Symbolic input **LANG-CYCLE-INPUT.** Supply a finite nonempty strongly connected set with explicit local edges `this#i`. A one-member self-loop is permitted. No member root is a pure reference. Local indices must be in range. Local-edge text is allowed only by this symbolic operation; literal strings that merely contain it are not graph edges. Caller-supplied ZERO sentinels fail. Keep every path containing a local edge visible through symbolic normalization, including inline type definitions. External children use ordinary exact identity. Do not hash away a local dependency before the masking and relabeling steps. ### 12.2 Preliminary order **LANG-CYCLE-ORDER.** Temporarily map each local edge to the private 44-character ASCII-zero token for preliminary calculation. Sort by preliminary identity text, then by canonical root-commitment bytes whose child contributions are their exact identities. If both keys tie for distinct members, reject ambiguity. Do not use input order, file name, visible expansion depth or allocation identity as a tie-breaker. The zero token is not a plain BlueId. Its temporary contribution behavior is confined to this algorithm. The commitment projection makes external exact expansion independent of the ordering key. It is not the canonical JSON of arbitrarily expanded member bodies. ### 12.3 Master and member identities **LANG-CYCLE-FINALIZE.** Return to the original symbolic members, arrange them in canonical order and relabel local targets to canonical indices. Identify that ordered payload-only list with local `this#j` strings as the scoped temporary contributions. Its ordinary list identity is MASTER. Original member i receives `MASTER#canonicalIndex(i)`. Final materialization replaces symbolic edges with the final member IDs. Retain the complete symbolic proof needed for verification. No local token or ZERO sentinel may escape as a finalized ordinary reference. ### 12.4 Verification **LANG-CYCLE-PROOF.** A member proof contains the complete symbolic member set in canonical order. Re-finalize it, require the expected master and canonical member mapping, check the index range and derive the selected final body. An optional separately supplied body must be a materialization and have the same ordinary body commitment as that derivation. A repeated member reference is not body proof. The ordinary identity of a detached member body generally differs from its `MASTER#index`. The comparison authenticates two materializations of the derived body; it does not substitute the detached-body identity for the member ID. The proof establishes the set's exact addressing, not semantic validity of every external dependency. Strict admission performs additional type/content checks as required. This protocol does not infer hidden symbolic boundaries, discover arbitrary compressed proofs or solve graph isomorphism for indistinguishable members. Those are not implicit capabilities of Language 1.0. **Algorithms:** A10, with normalization and helper functions A03. **Errors:** invalid set shape/edges, ambiguous ordering, invalid proof or missing required evidence. **Worked result:** the single node `name: Loop; self: {blueId: this#0}` has master `7Ydx3cm8uySLmzNyTcbpM5fufGaLSKnEs9cUcMMxRkeC`. --- ## 13. Diagnostics and safe operation boundaries ### Purpose Report what failed, where it failed and which established facts explain it. Diagnostic metadata is not Blue content and must not require speculative resolution or alter the operation's outcome. ### 13.1 Semantic result categories **LANG-DIAGNOSTIC-FACTS.** Preserve a machine-readable category, the failing logical path when established, the selected operation/validation goal and known expected/actual facts. Incomplete evidence/limits remain distinct from invalid content. Do not invent a constraint origin, payload or type name that the failing comparison did not establish. Do not fetch additional data merely to make an error message prettier. The reference error record includes `category`, `detail`, `path`, `phase`, `goal`, `expected`, `actual`, and optional document/declaration identity context. Another carrier may encode equivalent facts. Human wording, colors, preview lengths and stack traces are not part of semantic conformance. | Example | Required useful facts | |---|---| | Inherited Text PLN supplied as USD | `/currency`, expected Text PLN, received Text USD, fixed-value category | | Integer field supplied as Text | `/bar`, exact expected Integer identity and actual Text identity | | Payload-free Currency admitted as a value | Root path `""`, value goal, missing Text payload | | Explicit interval weakening | Authored endpoint/facet and inherited endpoint it violates | | Missing referenced type | Required identity and incomplete/unavailable outcome, not successful node ID | **LANG-DIAGNOSTIC-NAMES.** Label an exact core type with its canonical registry name. A custom type merely named Integer remains custom; its full ID must remain available. Human names are display context, never evidence for a subtype decision. Preserve the distinction between the root pointer `""`, empty-named child `/` and escaped member paths. ### 13.2 Validation intent **LANG-EXPLICIT-GOAL.** An interface may offer an explicit action to validate as a definition after a missing-value error. It MUST NOT silently change the requested goal, insert a fabricated payload or publish after a failed value admission. A displayed success must state the goal actually established. A declaration without a payload is not necessarily illegal. `name: Currency; type: Text` is valid as a definition but does not satisfy completed Text-value admission. This is an invalid value request, not an unavailable-evidence result. The correct explanation is the operation mismatch, not a suggestion that primitive types cannot be specialized. ### 13.3 Security and implementation boundary **LANG-FAIL-CLOSED.** Neither a supplied address, a transport success nor a locally available cache entry establishes semantic validity. No invalid or incomplete result may carry a successful admitted-document claim. Keep receipt/storage metadata outside content and preserve the selected input role across APIs and persistence. A host decides transport, keys, persistence and external trust. The Language decides the exact identities and semantic checks. SDK-specific proof authentication must implement the abstract evidence obligations of §11; it cannot redefine them.
