The Language defines no network-fetched executable code or ambient authority discovery. **Algorithms:** A01 records/scopes and error sites throughout the annex. The annex retains the reference renderer as explicitly marked support; another implementation need not reproduce its English sentences. --- ## 14. Conformance and operation equivalence ### 14.1 Required behavior **LANG-CONFORMANCE.** A full implementation MUST implement all defined input roles, scalar codecs, core registry identities, normalization, Source preparation, exact identity, type and schema semantics, list construction, graph operations, definition and completed-value admission, selected observations, minimization, export, and cyclic proof verification. It MUST implement `specification` as metadata rather than an ordinary field. The standard package model is defined in the same Language release. A tool claiming package-processing conformance MUST also implement §18. A Language-only tool need not perform package acquisition or execute additional protocols. The normative algorithms and standard definitions are included in this document. Conformance data accompanying a release is evidence for these rules, not an alternative source of semantics. An implementation MUST NOT select behavior from a test identifier or substitute an expected result for executing the stated operation. ### 14.2 Required cross-operation relationships **LANG-CROSS-OPERATION.** Under the same interpretation context and adequate evidence, the following relationships MUST hold: | Operations | Required relationship | |---|---| | Expand and collapse | Preserve exact root and selected child identities. | | Inline and referenced access | Establish the same selected semantic observations. | | Selected and complete resolution | Agree on observations established by both. | | Source creation followed by Exact loading | Execute construction once; do not replay append operations. | | Exact and compact-canonical loading | Recover the same exact node and BlueId. | | Specialization | Preserve all applicable inherited guarantees. | | Minimization and subsequent resolution | Preserve the defined effective view; a minimized Source identity need not equal the input identity. | | Cyclic finalization and member verification | Agree on master identity, canonical member indices, and derived bodies. | | Failed admission and publication | Do not issue a successful admitted-document claim or install a partial publication as admitted. | | Alias renaming | Preserve exact results when the replacement names bind the same identities. | | Package relocation | Preserve its semantic identity independently of the retrieval location. | ### 14.3 Host independence **LANG-PORTABILITY.** An independent implementation MUST follow the arithmetic, Unicode, key ordering, input-role, evidence, and comparison rules defined here. It MUST NOT use locale, pointer identity, nondeterministic traversal, or cache state to select a content identity or semantic result. Mathematical Integer and finite binary64 are distinct categories. A native adapter MUST preserve those categories or reject an ambiguous input. Native adapters MUST reject unsupported host values such as nonfinite numbers, undefined or sparse elements, functions, symbols, non-string map keys, and pointer cycles in an ordinary builder graph. Such pointer cycles are not symbolic cyclic-set input. A different data representation MAY be used only if it preserves the declared operation contract. ### 14.4 Outcomes and comparison Conformance observations distinguish **Established**, **Absent**, **Incomplete**, and **Invalid**. Expected absence requires evidence sufficient to establish absence at the selected location. Missing content and exhausted physical work budgets are not absence. Structural identity alone is not an admission certificate. Identity strings and canonical bytes compare exactly. Ordered sequences compare by length, order, and element values. Scalar comparisons retain their prescribed categories. Effective views are compared as specified by `same_view` in Appendix D, not by discarding type and constraint information. Minimization is checked by its semantic round trip; a different permitted Source spelling is not itself a failure. Portable fixture requests and their comparison rules are specified in Appendix E. Tests for package roles and public admission additionally exercise the stronger admission guarantees, rather than confusing structural fixture `identify` with completed-value admission. ### 14.5 Incomplete implementation and resources A missing implemented feature is not permission to approximate a successful result. A processor MUST expose unsupported behavior or incomplete work without issuing an invalidity or success assertion that was not established. Host resource limits, parser protection, transport bounds, and diagnostic preview sizes MUST NOT become universal structural restrictions on Blue content. A conforming invocation either returns a result established by the selected rules or reports why it did not establish one. Finite tests, independent test vectors, and repeatability checks provide evidence; a count of passing tests is not proof for every possible document. --- ## 15. The result has three elements, not a nested prefix plus C. ### 15.5 Constraint tightening and a definition without payload A definition of an Integer range 5–10 may be specialized by an explicitly supplied range 6–9. It may not be specialized by 4–11, even though intersecting both would yield 5–10. Validate the authored specialization before considering any cleanup. A list definition with no `items` and `minItems: 2` leaves a future obligation. The same definition with `items: []` supplies a concrete violating payload. This is why a definition goal is not interchangeable with value admission or with filling missing payloads automatically. ### 15.6 One cyclic member Symbolic set with one member: ```yaml name: Loop self: blueId: this#0 ``` Its master is `7Ydx3cm8uySLmzNyTcbpM5fufGaLSKnEs9cUcMMxRkeC`; its member is that master followed by `#0`. The complete proof retains the symbolic set in canonical order. A detached body containing its finalized self-reference does not independently hash to that member string. ### 15.6 Positional presentation and pure edits Given a published type whose field `x` is positional `[N, HOLE, R]`, a descendant can write: ```yaml x: - N - $empty: true - R - another element ``` This is a presentation at indices 0–3, not four append instructions. The hole may instead be filled with any value satisfying its other requirements. N and R may be repeated or compatibly refined, not contradicted. No `$replace` is required. To modify only the inherited hole, a separate pure edit form is: ```yaml x: - $pos: 1 $replace: filled value ``` Mixing these forms, or putting an edit after ordinary entries, is invalid. A pure edit cannot target a new out-of-bounds fifth position; use the full positional form to extend the list. --- ## 16. Authoring bindings and exact content availability ### 16.1 Local names An authoring environment may supply a finite map from names to final BlueIds. A name is local syntax, not a type identity. Automatic substitution applies only at the type positions specified in §9. Ordinary text, `name`, and `description` are not rewritten because their values resemble an alias. A package mount assigns a prefix to selected exports. Mounting package X does not mount the aliases used by X's author or by X's dependency packages. To use dependency Y by name, the consumer MUST establish its own binding, for example `xyz/Order`. Definitions already published by X retain their exact references to Y, regardless of the consumer's bindings. **LANG-BINDING-SCOPE.** Binding addition MUST reject a name that is already bound to a different identity, without partially changing the environment. Repeating the same name-to-identity binding is permitted. Core aliases MUST NOT be rebound to different identities. Removing a mount removes its names and contributed provider layer; it does not revoke or delete separately retained immutable content. A mount prefix is a local name, not an instruction to execute code or fetch a URL. Prefix syntax for the package model is defined in §18. Independent applications may use different prefixes for identical definitions and obtain identical exact results. ### 16.2 Finalized cyclic-member aliases Alias targets may be plain final BlueIds or finalized cyclic-member IDs. A symbolic `this#i` is not a final alias target. Access to a finalized member requires its owning-set proof when the selected operation needs the member's body. A loader MUST preserve the member identity and MUST NOT replace it with the ordinary hash of the detached body. ### 16.3 Supporting content without additional names A content environment may contain definitions that have no authoring alias. A self-contained package may supply the exact definitions required by its exports without exposing the names of every supporting definition. Availability, naming, and execution support remain separate. Every supplied definition has the same identity, specialization, schema, collection-context, and admission rules as a definition supplied individually. Package membership creates neither an additional type kind nor an exemption from validation. Missing required content remains incomplete. ### 16.4 Reuse of established results Within an operation, verified immutable exact content and completed semantic obligations may be reused under keys that include the exact input, selected rules, recipe, goal, and root context. Active plans and unfinished obligations MUST NOT be cached as successful results. Reusing content across environments is permitted only under the evidence conditions of §5. Reusing a semantic result requires the same relevant interpretation. An ordinary-value cycle can establish structural presence as defined by the algorithms; a cycle of type edges cannot manufacture a concrete value. --- ## 17. Specification metadata ### 17.1 Meaning and shape `specification` is an OPTIONAL reserved metadata field alongside `name` and `description`. It identifies normative semantic context associated with the exact node. Unlike the two literal labels, its value is a node reference. In Source, the field accepts an explicit reference or an inline node. An inline target is prepared in its own context, retained as exact content, and replaced by its reference. Bare text is not a specification reference. To supply normative text inline, use an explicit Text node. Exact input may materialize the target; Direct input requires its pure reference. Symbolic local references are permitted only within the cyclic-set procedures in §12. ```yaml name: Example declaration description: A reusable declaration. specification: type: Text value: The additional rules governing this declaration. ``` This example defines the shape of the metadata; it does not establish a particular processor protocol. A plain field named `spec` is ordinary content and has no reserved metadata meaning. ### 17.2 Identity and payload structure **LANG-SPECIFICATION-IDENTITY.** The target's exact identity contributes to the containing node's identity as specified by the ordinary child-reference helper. Changing the target changes that contribution. An exact reference and a verified materialization of its target are interchangeable for identity. The metadata is permitted on object, scalar, list, and payload-free nodes. It does not create an object payload, establish value presence, or count toward ordinary field constraints. It is excluded from the ordinary business-field collection of an effective view. Resolution does not expand or merge the target's contents into the containing node. ### 17.3 Inheritance and refinement **LANG-SPECIFICATION-INHERITANCE.** A type's root specification is not copied into an instance as the instance's own metadata or as an ordinary field. Its association remains available through the exact type relation. A subtype may declare its own specification without deleting the base type's association. For a type A associated with SA, a subtype B associated with SB, and an instance x whose type is B and which has no own specification: | Observation | Result | |---|---| | x's own specification | Absent | | B's own specification | SB | | A's own specification | SA | | Declared associations along x's type chain | SB followed by SA | A specification association does not override the underlying type's content guarantees. If a concrete inherited child already has fixed metadata, an explicit refinement cannot substitute conflicting metadata. The comparison is atomic: it is not a recursive merge of two normative documents. ### 17.4 Observations and required evidence `query` of `/specification` or a root `specification` observation reports the node's own reference or Absent. Traversal below that metadata explicitly requests the referenced content. The processor must obtain the necessary verified evidence to answer such a traversal. Structural identity can use a final reference without its body. Strict admission verifies reachable content, declared types, and the specification target in the definition role. A missing target is incomplete evidence; a body with a mismatching identity is invalid evidence. A reference to reusable normative structure is not required to satisfy every completed business-value obligation merely because it appears as metadata. **LANG-SPECIFICATION-ROLE.** Definition-valid target content is not proof that the target is a complete protocol descriptor, that its prose is consistent, or that a processor implements it. Those conclusions require their own role-specific checks. ### 17.5 Discovery through a type chain The following procedure defines the direct type-chain association observation. It does not recursively activate every specification in an arbitrary content graph and does not resolve semantic prerequisites beyond that chain. ```python """Read governing metadata along a selected type chain; not a support assertion. Does not activate protocols, execute code, or scan unrelated provider records. """ from algorithms import blue as B def declared_requirements(node, context): result=[]; seen=set(); current=node while current is not None: identity=B.identity(current) B.require(identity not in seen, 'TypeCycle', identity) seen.add(identity) body=B.open_exact(current,context) link=body.get(B.SPECIFICATION) if link is not B.ABSENT: B.require(isinstance(link,B.Ref), 'InvalidNodeShape', 'specification position') result.append({'definedOn':identity,'specification':link.id}) parent=body.get('type') current=parent if isinstance(parent,B.Ref) and parent.id not in B.CORE_NAME else None return tuple(result) ``` The result identifies both the definition declaring the association and the target specification identity. Identical target specifications on different declaring types may appear more than once. Type cycles remain invalid according to §6. ### 17.6 Normative rules versus informative documentation A governing specification establishes additional semantic obligations. A guide explains use without introducing such obligations. A package may contain guides, examples, and specialized programs without defining a new protocol. A program fully expressed using existing primitives need not declare a new native protocol merely because it is published independently. Its existing type and primitive associations remain applicable in their defined roles. Conversely, an unrecognized executable declaration does not become interpretable merely by omitting specification metadata. --- ## 18. Standard packages and protocol descriptors ### 18.1 Package model A **package** is an immutable Blue document that identifies a selected collection of exports, exact imports, specifications, and documentation. A **source repository** is an authoring workspace; it is not itself the package identity. A **bundle** is an explicit selection of package mounts. A **registry** is a retrieval or discovery service. Package and Protocol Specification are ordinary standard definitions. Their complete Source definitions are included in Appendix C. Their identities are calculated using ordinary admission and identity operations. No core primitive, reserved `Package` keyword, or alternative hash function is introduced by those definitions. A package processor applies the role checks in this section in addition to Language checks. Package roots are admitted in the definition role because their graphs contain reusable definitions. The package-role checks then establish complete package structure, export validity, and supplied evidence. A tool MUST NOT reinterpret failed value admission as successful package admission without selecting the package role explicitly. ### 18.2 Semantic root and witness This edition uses the package model identifier `blue-package-model/2-specification-metadata`. The identifier is an exact format label, not a compatibility range. The root has the following fields. A semantic witness is the complete authoring-shaped record used to reproduce and verify the exact root; null optional witness slots are omitted by normal Source preparation. | Field | Required meaning | |---|---| | `type` | Exact reference to the ordinary Package definition in Appendix C. | | `format` | The exact package model identifier above. | | `name` | The package's identifying literal name. It is not a globally unique authority or a registry locator. | | `version` | A human-facing release label. It does not perform dependency resolution or establish compatibility. | | `identityProfile` | The exact supported Language algorithm profile selected before admission. For this edition: `blue-language/2026-09-26-specification-metadata-1`. | | `bootstrapLanguage` | Boolean indicating a bootstrap Language release. | | `language` | Reference to the exact selected bootstrap Language package, or null in the bootstrap witness. | | `exports` | Map from local export names to exact definition references. | | `imports` | Map from explicit local prefixes to exact imported package references. | | `protocol` | Reference to this package's governing protocol descriptor, or null when it defines no new protocol. | | `specBindings` | Verified associations from exported type identities to native specification references and the selected descriptor. | | `declaredRequirements` | List of exact protocol-descriptor references required by the package's declared use. | | `documentation` | Map from safe logical paths to identified Text assets and their byte descriptors. | Semantic witness keys are exactly those listed. Additional distribution metadata belongs outside the semantic root. The exact Blue document is the normal admitted result of this record, not its raw JSON byte hash. The release-label grammar is `major.minor.patch`, with nonnegative decimal components having no leading zeros except zero itself, and an optional hyphen followed by dot-separated alphanumeric/hyphen prerelease identifiers. Numeric prerelease identifiers have no redundant leading zeros. The label is descriptive; comparisons of labels MUST NOT substitute one identity for another. ### 18.3 Language bootstrap A bootstrap Language package has `bootstrapLanguage: true`, no `language` reference, no imports, and no protocol descriptor. Its rule selection comes from the implementation establishing that bootstrap context. It may export ordinary standard definitions and carry this complete specification as documentation. A non-bootstrap package has `bootstrapLanguage: false`, an exact Language reference, and an explicit direct import of that same Language package. Every semantically interpreted imported package must have the same Language selection. An imported bootstrap must be that exact selected package. These checks also apply to transitive dependencies and previously visited dependencies; a foreign bootstrap cannot bypass the check by being reached through another branch. This is the supported interpretation of this edition, not an assertion that every possible later Language edition must have identical representation or algorithms. §19 defines the versioning boundary. The bootstrap Package and Protocol Specification nodes need not point back to their containing Language package. Their standard role is established by the selected Language. Publishing them does not impose a package-to-type-to-package cycle. ### 18.4 Exports and scoped imports An export name is a nonempty string associated with one final BlueId. Exported targets MUST be available as verifiable exact definitions, including required cyclic proofs. There is no automatic historical-to-current identity substitution. An import binds one exact package to an explicit prefix within the importing author's source environment. For this package model a prefix matches: ```text @?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)* ``` For example, `orders`, `company/workflows`, and `@repo.blue` are permitted. A consumer constructs a local name by appending `/` and a selected export name. The resulting binding is a normal Language alias, subject to collision checks and the reserved core bindings. **LANG-PACKAGE-SCOPE.** Importing X does not introduce the aliases that X used for its imports. If X refers to Y1, mounting Y2 directly does not retarget that reference. A consumer may mount multiple exact package versions under distinct prefixes. Such coexistence does not establish that their types are interchangeable or that all associated protocols can be combined. Package import graphs MUST be acyclic in this model. Cyclic definitions within packages use §12; they are not cyclic package imports. Multiple paths to the same exact package are permitted and MUST be verified consistently. Retrieval locations, package version labels, and mount order do not select a different target. ### 18.5 Supporting exact content Supporting records provide the exact definitions and evidence required to establish exports and identified package content. They do not automatically add aliases, authorize actions, or install processor code. A selected package can therefore make an unnamed referenced Order definition available without mounting any `Orders/Order` alias. A self-contained package supplies the required exact content and owning-set proofs. A partial content delivery MAY be retained as partial evidence, but MUST NOT be represented as a successfully verified self-contained package. A receiver MUST distinguish a missing body from a known absent field. A package's own exported definitions and supplied supporting definitions retain their exact identities independently of which package distributes them. A package that re-exports a definition MUST NOT modify its description or metadata while asserting that the original identity is preserved. ### 18.6 Protocol Specification role A protocol descriptor uses the ordinary Protocol Specification type. Its required fields are `type`, `name`, `language`, `rules`, `requires`, and `status`. Its optional fields are `effectiveRules` and `schedulingPolicy`. This is a descriptor schema, not an instruction to execute new behavior. | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `type` | Exact reference to the Protocol Specification definition in Appendix C. | | `name` | Literal protocol name; not a dispatch or authority key. | | `language` | The same selected Language reference as the package context. | | `rules` | Exact reference to accessible Text containing the governing normative material. | | `requires` | Map from local requirement labels to exact protocol-descriptor references. Labels are local explanatory names. | | `status` | Publisher's Text classification of the descriptor. It is not certification or a trust grant. | | `effectiveRules` | Optional exact Text reference to an explicitly identified complete statement or supplement. | | `schedulingPolicy` | Optional exact Text reference to an explicitly selected policy. The field's existence does not make scheduling a Language operation. | A descriptor is admitted in the definition role, then checked for its complete descriptor structure. Its referenced rule documents MUST be established as Text. All protocol prerequisites use the same Language selection. The prerequisite graph MUST be acyclic. A descriptor cannot authorize an arbitrary replacement of its required protocol by a later release. Where supplementary rule documents are supplied, the protocol's normative content must define how they apply. The field names do not provide a generic override or precedence mechanism. A contradictory or incomplete prose contract is not repaired by a matching package hash. A package may define no new protocol. Specialized programs, clauses, schemas, or forms expressed through existing semantics may use informative documentation alone. An empty export set is permitted for an explicitly declared protocol package; the package need not invent operator types solely to distribute a specification. ### 18.7 Native specification associations In this package profile, a protocol package associates each of its own exports with its governing rules using native `specification` metadata. Its `specBindings` map is keyed by each exported definition identity and contains: ```json { "specification": {"blueId": "RULES_ID"}, "protocol": {"blueId": "DESCRIPTOR_ID"}, "binding": "native-metadata" } ``` The symbolic strings in this example stand for valid final identities. `RULES_ID` MUST equal the descriptor's `rules` target. The definition's own exact `specification` MUST contain that reference. `DESCRIPTOR_ID` MUST equal the package's selected protocol. Bindings cover exactly the package's exports when it has a protocol; otherwise the binding map is empty. Imported definitions retain their own associations in their imported package witnesses. A package does not acquire a new native implementation merely by copying these records. A bootstrap Language package is governed by its selected Language role rather than by a self-referential protocol descriptor. Changing the native rules reference changes the containing definition's identity. Adding a guide to the package without changing that reference does not change the definition. A package descriptor MUST NOT assign conflicting native semantics to an unchanged type through uncommitted explanatory metadata. ### 18.8 Declared requirements `declaredRequirements` is separate from `imports`. A library may import a protocol's data definitions without declaring that every consumer performs that protocol's task. A publisher selects direct imported protocol requirements explicitly; it may include the selected package's own protocol. Transitive prerequisites are followed through exact descriptor references. The package-level requirement list is an inventory for the declared use. It is not a proof of document-specific support, structural validity, or authorization. A processor still applies the relevant checks to actual content in the roles defined by its protocols. Omitting an execution requirement does not enable an unknown executable primitive. ### 18.9 Documentation and package identity Every included asset in this package profile is valid UTF-8 Text. A documentation entry contains exactly `content`, `sha256`, and `size`: ```json { "content": {"blueId": "TEXT_DOCUMENT_ID"}, "sha256": "sha256:HEX_DIGEST_OF_UTF8_BYTES", "size": 123 } ``` The Text value is encoded as UTF-8 to establish the byte digest and byte count. The package processor verifies the Text identity, byte descriptor, and delivered file contents. A source publisher in this profile uses LF line endings and no UTF-8 BOM; it must not silently normalize an already identified Text value. A logical path is relative, nonempty, uses `/` separators, and cannot address a parent, root, drive, or external location. Archive consumers also reject unsafe paths, duplicates, symbolic links, and file-type tricks before installation. Host-specific byte and extraction limits are operational safeguards, not alternative Language identity rules. The package BlueId commits to its exact semantic root and referenced definitions, imports, and documentation. It does not commit to registry hostname, cache path, archive compression, CI run, credential, or source-checkout path unless such text is deliberately included as declared content. The root's own computed identity is not inserted into that root before hashing. ### 18.10 Verification procedure **LANG-PACKAGE-VERIFY.** A package processor claiming a verified package MUST: 1. Establish the supported Language/profile and the expected package identity, when one is supplied, before semantic interpretation. 2. Parse the carrier without duplicate keys or unsafe file entries; verify its declared byte inventory. 3. Admit the exact package root in the definition role and require its recomputed BlueId to equal the requested package identity. 4. Verify each semantic package witness as the same ordinary admitted content it describes. Enforce the root field set, format, version shape, bootstrap rules, imports, and Language consistency. 5. Traverse package imports and protocol prerequisites with cycle detection. Revisited nodes do not bypass context checks. 6. Establish every selected rule document and the native specification associations. 7. Admit every export as a definition, preserving owning-set evidence for cyclic members. 8. Establish every documentation target as Text and verify its byte descriptor and, for files supplied by this artifact, exact file bytes. 9. Verify all supplied records and their agreement between indexes, package evidence, and exported-content evidence. Do not certify extra unrelated witnesses as part of the root's identified closure. 10. Return a verified package result only after those checks succeed. A partial or failed operation does not install a successful mount. This procedure does not certify that a protocol's requirements are implemented or that an author is trusted. Expected identity must be selected through the caller's own trusted context. Matching a checksum shipped beside an untrusted archive alone does not establish that it is the artifact the caller intended to obtain. ### 18.11 Reference archive profile The implemented archive profile is identified by the literal string `blue-package/0.3-local`. This historical format label identifies the byte carrier; it is not an instruction to use an earlier interpretation or a publication-status assertion. An equivalent implementation may use another transport while preserving the package-role requirements. The ZIP contains four structural files plus the identified Text assets: | File | Role | |---|---| | `package.blue.json` | Exact normalized package-root document. | | `package-records.json` | Exact provider records and owning-set evidence for the root's required content. | | `repository.json` | Explicit exported alias map and backing definition records. | | `package.json` | Distribution manifest containing file inventory, semantic witnesses, and provenance. | The distribution manifest records `packageBlueId`, `languageProfile`, `language`, `protocol`, exports, exact import pins, semantic package/specification witnesses, file byte descriptors, and validation information. These claims MUST agree with the identified root and verified records. Producer source hashes and URLs are provenance, not alternative semantic identities or proof of conformance. The repository carrier has `format`, `name`, `aliases`, `records`, `metadata`, and `identity`. Its format is `blue-python-repository/1`. Its `identity` is a SHA-256 checksum of the canonical envelope without that identity field, not a BlueId. The profile's precise envelope serialization and verification procedures are included in Appendix F. The same data can be consumed by implementations in languages other than Python. The semantic witness for an imported package is not a source program to be reparsed under a different registry. Reconstructing and admitting its declared root must produce its existing package BlueId. A registry's readable tag is only a lookup hint. Normal verification never upgrades an import, edits a lock, or rewrites an exported type. --- ## 19. Edition selection and cyclic identity boundaries ### 19.1 Scope of an edition A Language edition fixes the node model, input interpretation, registry, exact-identity procedures, type and schema semantics, and operation evidence rules. A document or package is interpreted under an established edition, not under the most recently available package with a matching name. The exact Language release is selected out of band before semantic processing. An envelope may identify a package and the required profile; the interpreter must verify those claims under a supported selection. Nested references do not select alternate interpreters independently. ### 19.2 Compatibility **LANG-EDITION-COMPATIBILITY.** This edition defines no general cross-edition conversion or semantic-import mechanism. Its package processor uses the exact Language selection required by §18. A release label, matching major version, equal-looking schema, or compatibility claim in untrusted package content does not relax that requirement. A later Language specification may define compatibility with an earlier one. Such a specification must state the operations covered, the preserved identities and observations, and how earlier evidence is verified. No machine-readable compatibility vocabulary, automatic version solver, or generic permission to mix editions is defined here. An implementation that merely stores or transfers a foreign artifact need not interpret it. Supporting two editions in separate contexts does not itself establish semantic composition between them. A processor that cannot establish the required interpretation reports unsupported processing; it does not recalculate old references under another edition or treat unavailable interpretation as a malformed original document. ### 19.3 Cyclic sets **LANG-CYCLE-EDITION.** A symbolic set, its preliminary ordering, master identity, canonical member mapping, final materializations, and owning-set proof MUST be constructed and verified under one selected Language interpretation. The algorithm cannot switch editions between members or between finalization and verification. External references in that set must be interpretable under the same established context. A foreign member body is not evidence of a current-edition member identity. A resolver MUST NOT hash an older detached body using a newer procedure and treat the result as verification of its former `MASTER#index` address. A specification that permits cross-edition composition must define the behavior of complete owning sets, external references, canonical ordering, and proof verification. Compatibility of acyclic scalar values alone is insufficient to establish that behavior. This edition grants no implicit compatibility for those cases. ### 19.4 Publication boundaries are not cyclic-identity boundaries Ordinary package imports and protocol prerequisite graphs are acyclic in this package model. A package may nevertheless contain definitions whose ordinary content references form finalized cyclic sets. These are different graphs and different checks. A cyclic member may be exported under several names or distributed in several artifacts. Its owning set and proof do not change merely because its publication location changes. An artifact claiming self-contained use must retain the required proof. The package or filename is not a substitute for that proof. ### 19.5 Revision and identity preservation A package-only documentation change may change the package BlueId while retaining unchanged type and specification identities. A change to exact type content changes the type identity. A changed governing-specification reference also changes any exact node that carries it. A dependency mount does not migrate previously published content. A processor MUST retain the edition and scope of validation evidence. A new Language selection does not retroactively validate old admission receipts, even when an exact node happens to retain the same BlueId. Migration is an explicitly established new operation, not a display conversion or a consequence of loading another package. --- ## 20. Protocol interpretation and document processors ### 20.1 Additional interpretations A **document processor** interprets Blue content to perform a defined task under a selected Language and applicable protocol specifications. A task may evaluate expressions, execute workflows, coordinate histories, render a form, evaluate a query, run a simulation, or verify a proof. No universal event-processing method or effect model is imposed by Language. A **protocol specification** identifies the additional rules and their exact prerequisites. It may govern several kinds of nodes and the relationships between them. It is not necessarily a predicate applied independently to each node. The standard Protocol Specification type and descriptor role are defined in §18. A Language implementation may store or inspect such content without implementing the protocol itself. ### 20.2 Support claims **LANG-PROCESSOR-SUPPORT.** A processor claiming to perform a protocol task MUST implement the exact required rules and the applicable prerequisites for that task. Availability of specification text, a matching package name, or a successfully verified type is not evidence of implementation support. Support declarations identify exact specifications and, where necessary, supported combinations and roles. A tool MUST NOT claim complete support while silently ignoring an applicable required interpretation. It MAY expose unsupported content as data without claiming the unsupported result. A provider or user-supplied package cannot install trusted runtime bindings by declaring that it is compatible. A support decision is made by the installed implementation and the selected context. This specification does not define a standard HTTP capability endpoint or an executable plugin installation protocol. ### 20.3 Applicability The selected protocol determines the roles and boundaries at which additional meaning applies. A processor MUST account for the relevant definitions, their inherited requirements, and declared semantic prerequisites in those roles. It MUST NOT globally activate all specifications mentioned in every mounted package, example, or supporting record. Package imports provide names and content. Declared protocol requirements provide semantic prerequisites. Neither alone proves that a particular document is valid or that a business operation is authorized. A document-specific support check is distinct from a package-level requirement inventory. Introducing a new required executable or managed structure requires support checking before that structure is interpreted or activated. A prior check of a different exact state is not evidence about arbitrary future content. ### 20.4 Structural extension boundary This edition reserves `contracts` as a structural attachment that may accompany scalar, list, or object payloads. Language parses, identifies, and refines it; Language does not execute it. An application protocol may assign interpretation to that content in a defined task. Other application names remain ordinary fields unless listed as reserved in this Language edition. A package cannot add a Language-reserved word, change payload classification, or change identity contribution by placing a declaration in its documentation. A different structural attachment mechanism requires a Language specification that defines it. ### 20.5 Examples of independent protocol roles — informative A rendering protocol can define a Form and Text Field, with their types identifying the rendering rules. An application package can specialize Text Field with a fixed label without creating a new rendering protocol. A generic Language reader can inspect the resulting form; a rendering processor is required to produce the specified interaction. A query protocol can define filters, projections, and their evaluation rules. A library of queries using those primitives supplies programs rather than a new evaluator. A scientific-transformation package can likewise supply computations, units, or input constraints through an existing expression protocol. A workflow protocol can define step order and effects. A coordination protocol can add source evidence, authority, and history rules. A package of commercial workflows may use those rules without requiring an implementation for every exported commercial type. A newly defined native scheduling rule, however, is additional behavior that an implementation must support explicitly. ### 20.6 Authority and consistency A protocol dependency does not authorize redefinition of the required protocol. Two incompatible rules cannot be combined merely by importing both packages. The selected task must have an explicitly defined, coherent interpretation; import order is not a conflict-resolution procedure. No Language operation proves arbitrary prose specifications mutually consistent. It establishes exact content and the checks within its defined role. Conformance, domain validation, authenticity, and authorization remain distinct claims. ## Appendix A. Algorithm notation and primitive operations The code in Appendix D is normative executable notation. `Node` is an immutable set of uniquely named exact contributions; `Ref` is a final content reference; `Local` is a temporary cyclic-set edge. `ABSENT` is a distinguished sentinel, not JSON null. Lists and tuples are ordered. Maps have unique string keys. Sets are used for membership and logical conjunction; their physical iteration order does not establish a different portable content result. `int` denotes an arbitrary-precision mathematical integer, distinct from Boolean. `Fraction` denotes an exact reduced rational with positive denominator. `float` denotes a finite IEEE 754 binary64 value where admitted. `struct` bit conversions use the indicated fixed byte order. `Decimal` is used only to construct or inspect exact decimal candidates as specified; it does not authorize rounding where exact rational comparison is required. Integer division, remainder, greatest common divisor, bit shifts, and bit length have their usual exact mathematical meanings. Strings are sequences of Unicode scalar values. Strict UTF-8 decoding rejects malformed encodings and unpaired surrogate content. `key_order` encodes UTF-16 code units solely to determine the required object-key order. JSON `\\u` escapes decode to scalar values; decoded keys, not their source spelling, determine duplicates. Required JSON escapes are quotation mark, reverse solidus, and control characters U+0000–U+001F; the canonical encoder uses the specified short escapes and lowercase four-digit hexadecimal escapes for the remaining controls. Input JSON uses objects, arrays, strings, decimal number tokens, `true`, `false`, and `null`. Object names are strings. Insignificant whitespace consists of space, tab, carriage return, and line feed. There is exactly one root value and no trailing non-whitespace. A number uses the complete grammar in §3.1. The decoder must preserve number-token spelling until the Blue scalar codec selects its category. Comments, trailing commas, hexadecimal numbers, NaN, and Infinity are not JSON tokens. Portable YAML is a presentation of the same mappings, sequences, and scalars. Its indentation, flow collections, quoted strings, block folding, and chomping produce a syntax tree; the Blue scalar resolver in §3 is applied rather than a schema-dependent native YAML resolver. Anchors, aliases, tags, directives, implicit timestamps, merge keys, and multiple documents are excluded. The reference parser in Appendix D rejects those constructs before node normalization. Parser implementation choice does not authorize accepting additional Blue scalar types. `hashlib.sha256` denotes SHA-256 of exactly the supplied byte string, producing 32 digest bytes; it is not a generic selectable hash. Padding is a one bit, zeros to leave 64 bits in the final 512-bit block, and the original bit length in big-endian form. The 64 rounds use 32-bit words, addition modulo 2^32, the SHA-256 choice/majority functions, and its fixed initial values and constants. Blue then applies its independently specified base58 encoding, not hex encoding or a multihash wrapper. `copy` operations preserve values; object identity is not content. `lru_cache` and context memoization are optimizations whose reuse must obey §§5 and 16. `dataclass` and `typing` describe records, not additional wire fields. Exceptions carry the defined semantic outcomes; an equivalent implementation may use tagged return values. The only non-Blue syntax composition supplied by a library in the executable notation is the permitted JSON/YAML parser. For t from 16 to 63: ```text small0(x) = ROTR(x,7) XOR ROTR(x,18) XOR (x >> 3) small1(x) = ROTR(x,17) XOR ROTR(x,19) XOR (x >> 10) W[t] = small1(W[t-2]) + W[t-7] + small0(W[t-15]) + W[t-16] ``` Initialize a..h from the current eight hash words. Each round t performs: ```text big0(x) = ROTR(x,2) XOR ROTR(x,13) XOR ROTR(x,22) big1(x) = ROTR(x,6) XOR ROTR(x,11) XOR ROTR(x,25) Ch(x,y,z) = (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z) Maj(x,y,z) = (x AND y) XOR (x AND z) XOR (y AND z) T1 = h + big1(e) + Ch(e,f,g) + K[t] + W[t] T2 = big0(a) + Maj(a,b,c) (h,g,f,e,d,c,b,a) = (g,f,e,d+T1,c,b,a,T1+T2) ``` All additions and complements are 32-bit. Add the final a..h to the current hash words modulo 2^32. Concatenate the final words in big-endian order to obtain the digest. For the empty byte string, its hexadecimal rendering is `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`. ## Appendix B. ## Appendix F. Exact repository carrier This appendix fixes the integrity and evidence rules of the `blue-python-repository/1` carrier used by §18.11. It is an interoperable data carrier, not a requirement to use Python and not a separate Blue identity scheme. Its envelope checksum is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON with keys ordered as Unicode scalar strings, no optional whitespace, unescaped non-ASCII scalar characters, and no nonfinite numeric values, after omitting the `identity` field. The checksum is prefixed by `sha256:`. This envelope encoding must not be substituted for the Language helper encoding when calculating a BlueId. The envelope contains exactly `format`, `name`, `aliases`, `records`, `metadata`, and `identity`. `name` is a nonempty package/repository label. `aliases` maps strings to valid final identities; core names cannot be rebound. `records` maps final identities to declared exact bodies or owning-set proofs. A non-core alias needs its target record. A record cannot be accepted merely because its key has a valid identifier spelling. Each record is independently opened under the selected Language and verified against its key. A Text record has `mode: "exact"`, `format: "json"` or `"yaml"`, and `text` containing the original body. A cyclic record contains the complete `proof` and may include a separately supplied `body`; its verification follows §12. Inline and referenced bodies use the same evidence rules. Metadata is non-authoritative carrier information unless separately committed by the package root. It must not install aliases or imply executable support. Structural carrier verification is distinct from `audit`, which admits every exported target as a definition. A package processor also verifies the ordinary Package root, its documentary assets, semantic witnesses, and reachable-record agreement. No carrier checksum or audit count replaces those steps. Implementations can transmit equivalent verified content using a different physical record carrier. A consumer that claims this particular envelope format must follow its exact checksum, required-key, alias, and record-verification rules. "}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts

Blue Contracts processes an original event against exact managed Blue documents and returns a complete result, ordered emitted occurrences, gas and replay evidence. It uses Language for content semantics and BEX for evaluation. Coordination, timeline providers, account ownership and transport are outside this protocol.

## Specification and types

`SPECIFICATION.md` is one complete normative document: transition rules, metering, counter schedule and eighteen executable modules. The identical package Text is `spec/contracts.md`. `types/` contains generated views of the 32 standard definitions. The source of those definitions is the unchanged `publish_catalogue` algorithm in the reference; they are not an independently maintained catalogue.

Every exported definition has native `specification` metadata pointing to this complete normative Text. These are new type identities; none of the previously published types are reinterpreted or overwritten. `MIGRATION.md` explains the binding change.

## Local use

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package requirements
./blue-package demo
./blue-package test
./blue-package reference-tests
```

Python 3.13 or newer is required; pytest is required for tests. Normal verification does not update locks. `build` must reproduce the frozen release. The data archive is `dist/package.bluepkg`; the included Python source is build/test tooling and is not installed through package loading.

## Release status

Version `1.0.0-rc.2` is a clean, specification-bound publication candidate. The known enum-metering ordering defect in the supplied Python host boundary prevents an unconditional deterministic-runtime certification. See `QUALIFICATION.md`. This package does not hide that defect by fixing a hash seed or claiming that a larger gas allowance corrects metering defects.

A Java runtime must explicitly bind these new native type identities and specification before it claims support. Successful generic package verification alone is not execution support. Old snapshots and old fixtures remain attached to their previous release.

## Gas allowance

The shared default and maximum is **10,000,000 gas units** per atomic attempt. Smaller explicit budgets remain valid. The previous 100,000-gas edition is preserved under `editions/gas-100k/blue-contracts` in the package home; it must be selected explicitly for replay. See `MIGRATION.md`.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Timeline Access update events

This specification addendum defines the access-event publication of the Timeline
Access application program. The frozen Coordination transport and admission rules
remain unchanged. This is a new exact program and package, not a reinterpretation
of an older access document.

After validating and replacing both permission lists, Update Timeline Access MUST
execute the ordinary Contracts Trigger Event step with a Timeline Access Updated
value. The event contains no copies of permissions or additional document identity.

Each successful update emits exactly one event, including unchanged-list updates.
Invalid or rolled-back updates commit neither permission changes nor an event.
Reprocessing a consumed request does not execute the update or emit again. Distinct
successful requests have distinct occurrences even if their event values match.

The event is a notification, not proof of permission. Authority comes from verified
provider history and the executed access document. Consumers use ordinary Embedded
Node Channels filtered to the exact source path and event type. Contracts installs
the completed child state before delivering application events. Initial readiness
is calculated from the installed state without replaying a prior notification.

The host must recognize the new exact access program. Prior publications retain
their original program and output behavior; changing a package alias does not
upgrade an existing document. No extra native state channel or callback is used.
"}

objects. The explicit data-only `RetainedTransport` dependency is package

range evidence and signatures are not rewritten or re-signed for this edition.
This boundary does not equate distinct exported type identities or declare fresh
transport exports to be subtypes of retained definitions. Producers of the
supported retained transport continue to use its original exact types. Other
exports retain their explicit authored schemas; their presence is not a claim
that an arbitrary mixed-edition envelope satisfies those schemas.

## 1. Inputs and evidence boundaries

An input has its original signed Timeline entry and full canonical order
`K = (timestamp, timelineId, entryId)`. Contracts receives the original
`event: {blueId: entryId}` and original time; neither a replacement entry nor a
proof sidecar is introduced. Authenticating the entry, establishing a verified
source prefix, authorizing its actor, and executing it are separate obligations.
Knowing an entry identity is not evidence that its payload or authority is valid.

A receiver is a logical document lineage with a specific member/channel lifetime.
A receiving occurrence additionally identifies its source, path and generation.
Source processing history and an occurrence's history of receiving source work
are distinct. Sharing an acquisition does not merge these obligations.

`PRE(R,K)` is the exact receiver view established from work strictly before K,
including earlier attachment prerequisites and terminal input dispositions.
It includes the genuine original document identity, the ordered established
versions of that lineage before K, and the applicable declarations and authority.
It does not include a later version merely because its content is locally cached.
Completeness requires the existing verified source-prefix conditions, pending
work checks and exact predecessor proofs. A timestamp alone is not a boundary.

Missing evidence needed to establish PRE is a wait. A recursive visit is not a
proof of completeness. An uploaded initialized body is not a substitute for its
required history. Contextual constraints and actual reads remain obligations of
the selected Contracts edition; opaque references do not discharge them.

## 2. Q06: request selection relative to the receiver

The following classifier concerns operation dispatch, not ordinary event
observation. First establish the entry's framing, signature, source membership,
canonical order and complete PRE(R,K). If these prerequisites are missing, wait;
if they are invalid, retain the existing specific rejection. Do not fetch the
request's target body simply to classify an exact-version mismatch.

Let `current` be the exact document identity in PRE and `ownPast` the genuine
original identity plus every established own-lineage version strictly before K.
These are identities established by the receiver's history, not all identities
known to a global store. The original identity remains usable for non-exact
requests after initialization and subsequent changes.

```
classifyOperation(request, R, K):
    pre = requireCompletePRE(R, K)
    if request has no document target:
        return SELECT_USING_CURRENT_DECLARATIONS
    t = request.document
    if request.requireExactDocumentVersion:
        if t == pre.current: return ELIGIBLE
        if t in pre.ownPast: return REJECT_STALE_EXACT
        return OUTSIDE_EXACT_PRE_VIEW
    if t == pre.current or t in pre.ownPast:
        return ELIGIBLE
    if authenticated established lineage evidence proves t belongs elsewhere:
        return OUTSIDE_LINEAGE
    return WAIT_TARGET_HISTORY
```

`OUTSIDE_EXACT_PRE_VIEW` is an operation no-match for this receiver at K. It
makes no claim that t is globally foreign, invalid, or unavailable. In particular,
a future own version mismatches at K whether or not it is cached. This is an
explicit new-edition rule. It is not the old rule with a missing-content error
caught and converted to no-match. An incomplete own prefix cannot use this rule.

`ELIGIBLE` is not authorization or success. Resolve the actual operation/channel,
its schema, actor/mandate and business prerequisites in PRE. Missing required
operands wait; established denial rejects. A non-exact request to an unknown
identity still waits unless actual evidence establishes a different lineage.
Neither inequality nor inability to fetch proves that distinction.

Independently select ordinary observer channels from the same original entry.
An operation outside the receiver's audience does not suppress an otherwise
eligible observer. Such an observer may legitimately need payload data and wait
for it. Operation-path rejection/no-match is scoped separately from any real
observer processing; a feeder must not stamp a whole-entry rejection that hides
an eligible observer. All applicable paths must settle before this input is
complete for the receiver. If observation executes, only its actual Contracts
result may establish a checkpoint. A pure operation rejection/no-match establishes
only a private InputDisposition, never a fictitious Contracts checkpoint.

A disposition binds original entry and K, receiver lineage/lifetime, member and
channel generations, exact PRE and verified source/authority evidence. A settled
path cannot be resurrected by later state in that lifetime. Other receivers and
new generations remain independently evaluated. Publish decisions atomically
with any actual receiver result; do not advance past unresolved selected work.

## 3. Q13: raw node establishment and replay

Every lineage starts from its genuine pre-initialization content. Record that
exact reference before initialization. An already initialized reference follows
the existing-history attachment algorithm below; it is never treated as raw.

For a genuinely new raw child captured by a parent attempt at Kbirth:

1. Retain Contracts' raw source and actual creation provenance. Establish the
   child's own initialization semantics as for standalone admission of that raw
   source. Do not inject a fabricated event/time into initialization. Creation
   provenance remains host/runtime evidence and is not substituted for raw input.
2. Discover the child's required sources using the new edition's ordinary
   source/authority rules. Its replay frontier starts at its own initialization,
   not the parent's last processed order, inherited channel cursor or birth time.
3. Establish its ordered history from the beginning through Kbirth **inclusive**.
   Execute each selected original entry once for its own lineage/channel lifetime.
   Lack of relevant access, authority or content remains a real prerequisite.
4. Deliver retained child results through the completion receiving kernel to the
   eligible occurrence. This turn has no external parent seed. It must not invoke
   the parent's creating operation again or replay the parent's direct history.
5. Record source processing and occurrence receiving separately. Persist pending
   prerequisites and source/receiving positions so a restart resumes the same
   obligations. Do not expose the creating graph as stable while required child
   catch-up or receiving work remains unfinished.

The creating attempt still has its normal rollback boundary: a failed attempt
cannot expose a successful child. Separately committed source work can survive a
later receiving failure; it is reused through verified completion provenance,
not executed again. Intermediate positions retain their non-stable status.
Publication of a stable result must include all required owner/member results,
origin mappings and completed receiving obligations atomically.

Equal timestamps use the full K ordering: earlier ties precede the birth, the
birth entry is eligible exactly once for the child, and later ties remain later
work. The parent is not reseeded at any tie. If a child declaration appears while
processing Kbirth, the dispatcher must not also deliver that same entry as an
additional external live seed after replay has covered it.

### Historical channel activation: scan, causal and attachment coordinates

A newly installed channel lifetime is an ACTIVATION continuation, distinct from
raw-node INITIAL replay. Retain its member/channel/generation, exact committed
activation snapshot and receipt, scanActivationBound A, causalVisibilityBound V,
and original examined full-K cursor. A is the installing invocation's original
input K; V is the maximum full-K bound of the installing invocation itself and all its
causal ancestors.
Outer child attachment visibility Kbirth remains a separate coordinate.

ACTIVATION examines authenticated source entries strictly before A. Raw INITIAL
replay examines its own sources inclusively through Kbirth. Neither boundary is
changed by cached future content or wall-clock time. Installing an existing
channel does not silently consume the installing entry a second time.

For an activation delivery of original K, PRE_ACTIVATION is the exact invocation
prestate established by a contiguous shared receiver causal publication chain
anchored at the activation receipt. Include all earlier scheduled applicable
lifetime turns and receiving results, not merely this lifetime's own turns.
Select operation declarations, receiver actor-policy/business state and exact
current/own-past target classification from that proved prestate. The original
lineage identity remains available for nonexact targeting. Original-K source,
signature, mandate, grant and revocation history remains the authority bound;
a later grant at A never retroactively authorizes the original K.

For a supported canonical Mandates/Mandate Authority, signed-prefix admission and authority-header reads require the contextual authority header, its actor, its closed field set, and an authored original-mandate identity. Only an exact reference occurrence governed solely by the canonical Mandate Authority.mandate declaration may defer that declaration's Mandate value/type obligation until owned original-mandate history before the entry's order key is available. Additional contextual contributions, requirements, type narrowing, or inline governing metadata retain ordinary required-value validation. After resolving that history and before granting authority, the original contextual mandate occurrence MUST satisfy its full value/type obligations. Header admission, retention, and reuse establish neither a whole-value certificate nor authorization; signature, actor, history, approval, status, participant, and scope checks remain mandatory.

A deterministic worklist completes activation prerequisites before the next
ordinary receiver input. Select the minimum original full K within ready
obligations, retaining per-lifetime cursors and exact predecessor receipts.
Equal-K deliveries may share an invocation only if their actual receiver
prestate is proved identical; otherwise execute in ascending `(member identifier, channel name, generation)`
order: the first two use the existing canonical string ordering, followed by the
numeric generation. Map iteration order is not a scheduling rule.
Nested activation retains its own strictly-before scan bound and inherits causal
visibility. For example, L3 installed at original K10 during A100 replay scans
before K10 but remains visible at100, never at10. An earlier logical input cannot
observe effects from a future causal ancestor merely because they were cached.

Operation dispositions bind these coordinates and their exact receiver prestate.
Terminal-only progress, retired/replaced lifetimes and actual receipts remain
separate. A repeated worklist key is unresolved until every local/source/receiving
premise is proved. No global original-K monotonicity shortcut, latest-head
substitution, checkpoint rewrite or parent reseeding establishes completeness.

Conformance additionally covers shared L1/L2 state, nested decreasing scan bounds,
exact-current/stale and nonexact-original targeting, original-time grant/revoke,
full-K ties and persisted restart between installation and historical delivery.

### Existing source and occurrence attachment

An established source retains its original birth, identity and source history.
Attaching it at K freezes the last established source position from work strictly
before K, including that source's earlier attachment prerequisites. Reject a
supplied initialized position beyond this goal. Apply contiguous missing source
successors through the goal without repeating initialization or source effects.
A K-live step then uses its own exact checkpoint/disposition and is not duplicated.

Receiving old source work is effective at the receiving attachment boundary for
receiver history queries, while Contracts keeps the source's original cause/time.
Do not rewind parent checkpoints. Finish required attachment work before the
parent's next input. Detach retires an occurrence, not source history; reattach
creates a new generation and cannot inherit retired pending receiving tickets.

Member origin keys remain exact across promotion/re-root/cold restore. Runtime
constructor keys and independent standalone root keys must not be silently
merged. State-equality conformance compares the child document projections;
completion reuse additionally requires compatible member origins and before-view.
Exact state parity requires the same raw source, applicable semantic context and
relevant authenticated histories. Different parent-imposed constraints are not
assumed equivalent. The same raw source in an independent account is independently
established, not a portable capability to adopt another account's local completion.

## 4. Temporal dependency algorithm and cycles

A pending history obligation is keyed by logical lineage, exact bound, phase
(initialization, before-view, source execution or receiving), and occurrence
generation when applicable. Dependencies retain their bounds; do not collapse
`A before K1` and `A before K2` into one visited document flag.

Maintain unresolved obligations and exact dependency edges. A completed memo can
be reused only for the same obligation and verified evidence. On a repeated
unresolved key, record the edge and analyze the component; never return complete
just because a DFS has encountered it before.

- A historical edge that reduces the bound is ordinary predecessor work. Resolve
  its finite established prefix, then its dependents. Example: A before K30 needs
  B before K20, whose earlier attachment needs A before K10. A's established
  initialization/K5 prefix terminates this chain; this is not a live cycle.
- A missing predecessor, content record or verified prefix is a resource/history
  wait. Repetition does not turn it into an error or authorize a guessed state.
- A live cyclic component may use the existing Contracts component algorithm
  only after every member's exact compatible pre-view and external prerequisites
  are established. Select the canonical representative and publish the complete
  atomic owner set. This resolves simultaneous live computation, not absent past.
- A same-bound proof cycle with no established pre-view is not evidence that any
  member exists or is ready. If it is only waiting for an external predecessor,
  keep that concrete wait. If closed immutable lifecycle evidence proves mutually
  dependent creation with no legal predecessor/initialization, reject that
  inconsistent history with `INVALID_CAUSAL_HISTORY`; do not manufacture a member or spin until success. This error requires a closed proof of contradiction, not merely an unresolved SCC or unavailable predecessor.

No arbitrary new iteration ceiling is part of this rule. Native deterministic
work/gas limits still apply to actual execution. The implementation must retain a
bounded diagnostic for an unresolved dependency component without calling it a
success. Ordinary graph recursion alone does not prove inconsistent history.

### 4.1 Reference procedure for established local history

The following procedure consumes authenticated local journal history, not
caller-authored proof claims. It does not replace raw establishment in section 3.

```
proveBefore(receiver, K, journalView):
    queue := [(receiver, K, BEFORE, rootOccurrence)]
    checked := empty map
    while queue is not empty:
        obligation := removeFirst(queue)
        select exact last history position with effectiveOrder < obligation.bound
        require its binding, contiguous predecessors and committed completion link
        read member/edge generations from that position's immutable completion.after
        require the exact expected source version for an incoming occurrence
        require local prefix and earlier timer/attachment/rebase work to be settled
        derive source channels from this selected member, not current-head channels
        if any requirement is unavailable: return its bounded unresolved obligation
        if this exact obligation was checked with the same evidence: continue
        record its checked local premises
        enqueue every selected edge's source-view obligation, retaining generation
    return a token bound to receiver, K and this immutable journal view
```

The checks on an incoming edge also occur on repeated keys. Repetition cannot
hide incompatible expected source positions. A token can select only the entry
whose full K and journal view match it. Future cached versions are not own-past
facts. A source completion that the receiver has not applied cannot satisfy an
edge merely because both document rows exist. Terminal input decisions are
retained prefix evidence, not successful source transitions.

Receiving prerequisites retain the source's original cause bound separately from
the receiving effective boundary. For example, receiving source event100 at
attachment300 may require a source prefix through100 (completeBefore101); it
cannot demand301 solely because the receive is published at300. Conversely, that
completed receive does not prove the receiver's later PRE301: later relevant
source work still needs its own prefix and receiving evidence. These are distinct
obligations in the same time-indexed procedure, not one document-wide visited bit.

## 5. Completion, persistence and resource origin

Use the new Contracts edition's normal completion/receiving API. A result binds
before/after state, original cause, executing edition/runtimes, member origins,
operation scope and the actual validated obligations. A data-only snapshot or
source-prefix witness is not a completion. Local durable recovery may rehydrate
only authenticated journal provenance for that edition and exact result.

Receiving installs the eligible source states before callbacks, preserving
whole-batch order, owner boundaries, generation checks and gas accounting. It
never substitutes direct snapshot patches or an extra parent external seed.
Cold recovery must reconstruct pending admission, source execution and receiving
without granting full Language certification to an operation-scoped result.

A required content identity does not identify a provider. Original cause timeline
alone does not authorize fetching every reference encountered while processing
that cause, especially a reference reached through older history. Provider
selection must use existing authenticated/adopted source provenance and access
mechanisms. Invocation-local required-read provenance also covers native matcher
opens: it relates reported missing identities only through ordinary authored edges
of bodies actually opened by that evaluation. A wrapper-specific read path is not
the only source of such observations. This collector supplies an observed path,
not authenticated provider authority; it does not search imported/provider
inventory or infer authored paths from inherited type fields. This draft does not introduce a wire proof sidecar or unrestricted
search over imported timelines. The exact host mapping for historical obligations
is an implementation gate to resolve with source-access owners before publishing.

## 6. Required executable conformance cases

Each test runs old and new selections where behavior changes; do not update old
expected outcomes. Missing/cached variants use identical admitted logical input.

| Case | Minimal fixture and required outcome in the new edition |
| --- | --- |
| Exact current | Complete PRE at K, target current: dispatch plus normal authority checks. |
| Exact stale | Known own predecessor, exact=true: durable operation rejection, no operation checkpoint/effect. |
| Exact future absent | A future target identity signed into K, future body unavailable: exact mismatch, no fetch. |
| Exact future cached | Same K/PRE/entry as preceding case, later body/history cached: identical decision. |
| Exact other receiver | Private Agreement exact target then child-target operation: child reaches later input without parent fetch. |
| Incomplete PRE | Repeat exact mismatch with required earlier prefix absent: WAIT, then settle after that prefix arrives. |
| Non-exact original | Agent request targets original raw Order after initialization: normal authorized dispatch. |
| Non-exact unknown | Unknown target with no lineage proof: WAIT; no false foreign/no-match. |
| Mixed audience | Exact operation mismatch plus matching ordinary observer: observer receives original event, including real operand WAIT. |
| Raw birth | Counter observer sees K100, birth K200: standalone and embedded raw child have identical complete state/BlueId; parent birth executes once. |
| Ties | Three entries at one timestamp ordered before/equal/after birth: each eligible child effect once, no parent reseed. |
| Existing attach | Attach an established earlier position; contiguous receive only; initialized future position rejected. |
| Reattach | Detach/recreate same path: new generation, source effects unchanged, no transfer of old pending ticket. |
| Decreasing history | A@30 -> B@20 -> A@10 with established K5 prefix: resolves, including after cold reopen. |
| Live SCC | Two established mutually embedded members: coherent component result and atomic publication, no recursion shortcut. |
| Missing cycle predecessor | Same-bound dependency component with one missing external predecessor: durable wait and automatic resume after exact evidence. |
| Invalid birth cycle | Closed lifecycle evidence requires each of two unestablished members to precede the other's initialization: `INVALID_CAUSAL_HISTORY`, no invented stable member. |
| Unproven birth cycle | Same apparent cycle but missing one lifecycle predecessor/witness: WAIT, never `INVALID_CAUSAL_HISTORY`; adding the witness may prove consistency or contradiction. |
| Full acceptance | Real original raw Order, separate Seller/Partner/Customer stores, Seller Agent exact-original mandate, second operation and cold reopen: full state/BlueId equality and no private Agreement acquisition. |

## 7. Publication gates and source anchors

This draft selects exact mismatch-at-PRE semantics rather than claiming universal
foreign-target detection. Implementation must expose path-scoped operation and
observer outcomes or prove its existing admission representation can express
section 2 without suppressing observers. The immutable inconsistent lifecycle diagnostic is `INVALID_CAUSAL_HISTORY`;
a missing witness must remain WAIT. This distinction is mandatory even when a
worklist encounters the same unresolved key repeatedly.

Required design checks before reference implementation: bounded child-only
catch-up/receiving without parent reseeding; initialized child equality without
forged origin adoption; historical demand-to-authorized-source mapping; and the
Contracts completion contract for operation-scoped outputs. None is proven by
this prose. They must be settled in code-backed fixtures before publication.

Baseline anchors (retained, not edited): canonical `coordination.md`, source
coverage/admission around lines 865–925; Core `runtime/final-gas-bridge/spec/
prior-rules.md` Q06 and Q13–Q20. Current reference implementation anchors:
`CoordinationAdmission.verifyAdmission` (global target-known gate and separate observer
selection), `CoordinationHistory.belongs/before/completeBefore` (global version
membership, historical views and recursion), `CoordinationEngine` attachment,
receiving and member publication; `ContractGraph.freshKey` for member origins.
Existing small starting repros are `MinimalRawBirthBoundaryTest` and
`MinimalTemporalHistoryViewTest`; a cached future view test is not by itself an
admission conformance test.
